Concerning the distinction among freedmen: who may attain ecclesiastical honors and who are forbidden to advance. Council of Toledo IV, title 73, chapter 49.

That, if laymen are chosen for the clergy, a specified period of time is to be observed. Decree of Gelasius, general, 82, title 4.

What sort of men clerics ought to be, and concerning their marriages and ranks. Letter of Siricius to Eumerius, 3, title 8.

[Col. 0029B] Concerning those who hasten to sacred service at an advanced age, and concerning their periods of service. In the work cited above, title 10.

Concerning monks to be advanced to the clergy, and how they are to advance through ranks and periods of time. Letter of Siricius to Eumerius, 3, title 13.

Concerning laymen who can become clerics, provided that after baptism they have joined clerics or monks, or have never known a concubine or mistress. Letter of Innocent to Felix, 8, title 4.

Concerning the periods to be spent in the clerical orders. In the work cited above, title 5.

What sort of men are to be chosen for the clerical order. Letter of Innocent to all in Toulouse, 27, title 5.

That no one is to reach the priesthood except through the ecclesiastical ranks. Decretal letter of Zosimus to Hesychius of Salona, 28, title 1.

What periods of time are prescribed in each clerical rank, and concerning those who have given themselves to ecclesiastical ministries from infancy. The same letter, 28, title 3.

[Col. 0029C] That when clerics are lacking, men are to be chosen from among the monks; also, what sort of men they are to be, what offices they are to pass through, and for how long and under what conditions. Decree of Gelasius, general, 82, title 3.

## TITLE XIII. Concerning the rules of clerics

That if a monk becomes a cleric, he is to preserve the monk’s way of life. Letter of Innocent to Victoricus, 7, title 10.

Concerning the conduct of clerics, that they are to live in one chamber. Toledo IV, title 24, chapter 49.

Concerning the form of the tonsure to be held commonly by all clerics and lectors. Council of Toledo IV, title 41, chapter 49.

Concerning the cutting of clerics’ hair and orderly dress. In the Excerpts of Martin, title 66, chapter 64.

Clerics are neither to grow their hair nor shave their beards. Council of Carthage IV, title 44, chapter 15.

[Col. 0029D] Concerning clerics who grow their hair. Council of Agde, title 20, chapter 30.

Clerics are not to seek elegance in clothing or footwear. Council of Carthage IV, title 45, chapter 15.

Concerning clerics who cannot work: they are to learn crafts and letters. Council of Carthage IV, title 53, chapter 15.

That diocesan clerics are to serve their weekly turns, and that on Saturday all are to assemble together. Council of Tarragona, title 7, chapter 39.

Concerning the prohibition against clerics being absent from the church on Sunday, but requiring them to attend the solemn celebration of Mass while fasting. In the Excerpts of Martin, title 64, chapter 64.

Concerning clerics who are absent from the church’s service on solemn days. Council of Agde, title 64, chapter 30.

Clerics who withdraw from their duties or perform them negligently are to be removed from office. Council of Carthage IV, title 50, chapter 15.

Clerics who are absent from vigils are to be deprived of their stipends. The same council, title 24, chapter 15.

[Col. 0030A] That a cleric of any order who comes late to church is to be deposed. Council of Toledo I, title 5, chapter 46.

Rebellious clerics and those who come late to the service are to be excommunicated. Council of Agde, title 2, chapter 30.

Clerics who disdain to come to the service are to be restrained at the bishop’s discretion. Council of Orléans I, title 24, chapter 31.

Concerning clerics who do not assemble for evening or morning prayer in any place. In the Excerpts of Martin, title 63, chapter 64.

Clerics in good health who violate the fasts are to be regarded as inferior. Council of Carthage IV, title 62, chapter 15.

A younger cleric is not to be placed above an older one. Council of Agde, title 23, chapter 30.

Clerics who wish to become monks for the sake of license are to be excommunicated. Council of Zaragoza I, title 6, chapter 11.

Clerics who desire the monastic way of life are to have that desire permitted. Council of Toledo IV, title 50, chapter 49.

[Col. 0030B] Clerics who curse are to be degraded. Council of Carthage IV, title 57, chapter 15.

Either the bishop’s reasoning or exhortation is to reconcile clerics who are at odds, or a synod is to condemn them. Council of Carthage IV, title 59, chapter 15.

Clerics are to avoid the banquets and company of heretics. Council of Carthage IV, title 70, chapter 15.

It is not permitted for a layman or cleric to dine before the third hour, or to approach the table or eat without a hymn. Council of Braga II, title 65, chapter 64.

Clerics, ministers, or laymen invited to an agape are not to take away a portion. Council of Laodicea, title 27, chapter 7.

Clerics who sing during meals are to be restrained with the greatest severity. Council of Carthage IV, title 63, chapter 15.

That clerics are to avoid weddings. Council of Agde, title 39, chapter 30.

It is not permitted for altar ministers or any others to attend spectacles presented either at weddings or at banquets. Council of Laodicea, title 54, chapter 7.

[Col. 0030C] It is not permitted for priests or clerics to attend spectacles. Council of Braga II, title 60, chapter 64.

Clerics who are vulgar and jest with shameful words are to be removed from office. Council of Carthage IV, title 60, chapter 15.

Concerning vulgar and joking behavior. Council of Agde, title 10, chapter 30.

Clerics who swear by creatures are to be rebuked most sharply. Council of Carthage IV, title 61, chapter 15.

Envious clerics are not to be advanced. The same council, title 54, chapter 15.

Clerics who are flatterers and traitors are to be degraded. Council of Carthage IV, title 56, chapter 15.

That traitors to their brothers, or to sacred vessels or Scriptures, are to be deposed with beatings. Council of Arles I, title 13, chapter 21.

If a cleric commits theft against the Church. Council of Agde, title 5, chapter 30.

That if a cleric voluntarily causes damage to the Church and makes satisfaction, he is to be excommunicated. The same council, title 26, chapter 30. [OCR: “Cono.”]

Concerning clerics who have committed a capital crime. The same council, title 50, chapter 30.

It is not permitted for clerics to be magicians or enchanters, or to make phylacteries. Council of Laodicea, title 36, chapter 7.

Concerning sorcerers and those who observe auguries, that they are to be separated from the Church. Council of Agde, title 42, chapter 30.

Concerning the prohibition against priests or clerics making incantations or opposing bindings. Council of Braga II, title 59, chapter 64.

Concerning Levites or clerics, that they are not to be magicians or enchanters. Council of Agde, title 64, chapter 30.

Concerning priests, Levites, or clerics who consult magicians or soothsayers. Council of Toledo IV, title 29, chapter 49.

Clerics are not to walk through streets and passageways. Council of Carthage IV, title 47, chapter 15.

Clerics who walk about without necessity in markets or in the [Col. 0031A] forum are to be degraded. The same council, title 48, chapter 15.

That drunkenness is to be forbidden to clerics. Council of Agde, title 41, chapter 30.

Clerics are not to enter taverns except out of necessity while traveling. Council of Carthage III, title 27, chapter 14.

It is not proper for anyone of any rank, down to the lowest cleric, to enter taverns. Council of Laodicea, title 24, chapter 7.

It is not permitted for clerics to take interest or sixfold repayment. Council of Laodicea, title 5, chapter 7.

Clerics of every rank are not to be contractors, agents, or merchants, or pursue shameful profits. Council of Carthage III, title 15, chapter 14.

Concerning interest and profits from business, that clerics are not to engage in them. Council of Braga II, title 62, chapter 64.

Clerics are not to be usurers by giving less and receiving more, nor are they to receive anything other than what they gave. Council of Carthage III, title 16, chapter 14.

If clerics have lent a solidus, they are to receive it back without interest. Council of Tarragona, title 3, chapter 39.

[Col. 0031B] Clerics are not permitted to lend at interest. Council of Carthage I, title 13, chapter 12.

Clerical moneylenders are to be excommunicated. Council of Arles I, title 12, chapter 21.

Clerics are not to receive interest. Council of Arles II, title 14, chapter 22.

Clerics are not to be permitted to buy more cheaply or sell more dearly. Council of Tarragona, title 2, chapter 39. [Note: [Col. 0031] B. R., T. 1, 2, Urg., Ger., “to buy more cheaply or sell, etc.”]

Concerning clerics who pursue business and markets. Council of Eliberis, title 19, chapter 38.

Concerning clerics who receive interest or an increase, or pursue shameful profits. Council of Nicaea, title 18, chapter 1.

Concerning usurious clerics and laymen. Council of Eliberis, title 20, chapter 38.

That no cleric is to pursue dishonorable business or shameful profits. General Decree of Gelasius, 82, title 17.

That a cleric is not to conduct lending at interest either in another’s name or in his own. Letter of Leo to the bishops throughout Campania, 64, title 4.

That bishops, clerics, or monks ought not to accept secular estates. Council of Chalcedon, title 3, chapter 11.

Clerics are not to accept the affairs or agencies of secular persons. Council of Carthage I, title 6, chapter 12.

Laymen are not to appoint clerics as their agents or accountants. The same council, title 9, chapter 12.

Concerning clerics who flee to secular persons because of the bishop’s discipline. Council of Agde, title 8, chapter 30.

Concerning clerics who break out into mutual slaughter. Council of Lérida, title 11, chapter 44.

Concerning clerics who have taken up arms or have done so. Council of Toledo IV, title 45, chapter 49.

Concerning clerics who demolish tombs. The same council, title 46, chapter 49.

Concerning those who serve at the altar, that they are to abstain from bloodshed. Council of Lérida, title 1, chapter 44.

[Col. 0031D] Concerning clerics and monks who do not remain in their chosen way of life. Council of Chalcedon, title 7, chapter 11.

Concerning ministers, that they are not to enter the sacristy. Council of Agde, title 66, chapter 30.

## TITLE XIV. Concerning the honor of clerics and faithful laymen

Concerning a cleric who remains faithful amid temptations, to be raised through the ranks. Council of Carthage IV, title 42, chapter 15.

Concerning those who suffer persecutions from unbelievers for the faith. The same council, title 43, chapter 15.

Concerning the elderly and the poor of the Church, who are to be honored. The same council, title 83, chapter 15.

## TITLE XV. That crimes are not abolished by the conferral of ordination

That crimes or vices are not rightly [Col. 0032A] believed to be removed through ordination. Letter of Innocent to Rufus, 26, title 4.

## TITLE XVI. That clerics are not to receive penance through the laying on of hands

Concerning clerics, that they are not to receive penance through the laying on of a priest’s hands, and that a layman is not to become a cleric after penance. Letter of Siricius to Eumerius, 3, title 14.

That if a presbyter or deacon has fallen into any crime, he cannot obtain the remedy of penance through the laying on of hands. Letter of Leo to Rusticus, 66, title 2.

That hands are not to be laid upon fallen priests as upon laymen. Council of Carthage V, title 11, chapter 16.

## TITLE XVII. Concerning the testing of religious persons of either sex, or concerning wandering religious

[Col. 0032B] Concerning those who at a very young age have worn the religious habit in the presence of their parents. Council of Toledo X, title 6, chapter 55.

Concerning wandering religious, who are regarded as belonging neither among clerics nor among monks. Council of Toledo IV, title 53, chapter 49.

Concerning respectable or wandering recluses. Council of Toledo VII, title 5, chapter 52.

## TITLE XVIII. Concerning psalmists

How a psalmist is ordained. Council of Carthage IV, title 10, chapter 15.

Concerning the psalmist: he ought not to use an orarium. Council of Laodicea, title 22, chapter 7.

## TITLE XIX. Concerning doorkeepers

How doorkeepers are ordained. Council of Carthage IV, title 9, chapter 15.

[Col. 0032C] Ministers, that is, doorkeepers, ought not to enter the sacristy or touch the Lord’s vessels. Council of Laodicea, title 21, chapter 7.

Doorkeepers are not to enter taverns. The same council, title 24, chapter 7.

Ministers, that is, doorkeepers, ought not to be absent from the doors or from prayer. The same council, title 43, chapter 7.

If necessity compels it, a penitent may become a doorkeeper or lector; or concerning which penitents he speaks. Council of Toledo I, title 2, chapter 46.

If usage requires it, a penitent may be assigned among the doorkeepers; or concerning which penitents he speaks. In the Excerpts of Martin, title 23, chapter 64.

## TITLE XX. Concerning lectors

How lectors are ordained. Council of Carthage IV, title 8, chapter 15.

That lectors, psalmists, [Col. 0032D] and doorkeepers also retain the designation “clerics.” Council of Carthage IV, titles 8, 9, and 10, chapter 15.

Lectors are not to use an orarium. Council of Laodicea, title 22, chapter 7.

That lectors are not permitted either to sing psalms in the dress of secular persons or to let their hair grow. Council of Braga I, title 11, chapter 63.

That lectors are forbidden to touch the altar vessels. Council of Braga I, title 10, chapter 63.

Lectors are not to enter taverns. Council of Laodicea, title 24, chapter 7.

Lectors are not to greet the people. Council of Carthage III, title 4, chapter 14.

If necessity compels it, a penitent may become a lector. Council of Toledo I, title 2, chapter 46.

If usage requires it, a penitent may be assigned among the lectors. In the Excerpts of Martin, title 23, chapter 64.

[Col. 0033A] No one is to ascend the pulpit except a lector. In the same work, title 45, chapter 64.

If a lector is a bigamist or takes a widow, he is not to become more than a subdeacon. In the same work, title 43, chapter 64.

## TITLE XXI. Concerning exorcists

How exorcists are ordained. Council of Carthage IV, title 7, chapter 15.

That exorcists are not to enter taverns. Council of Laodicea, title 24, chapter 7.

Those who have not been ordained by bishops ought not to exorcise—that is, to give bread. The same council, title 25, chapter 7.

## TITLE XXII. Concerning acolytes

How acolytes are ordained. Council of Carthage IV, title 6, chapter 15.

An acolyte is not to enter taverns. Council of Laodicea, title 24, chapter 7.

## TITLE XXIII. Concerning subdeacons

[Col. 0033B]

How subdeacons are made. Council of Carthage IV, title 5, chapter 15.

If approved men have contracted a second marriage, they are not to become more than subdeacons. Council of Orange, title 25, chapter 22.

Those who have committed adultery after baptism are not to be subdeacons. Council of Eliberis, title 30, chapter 38.

A subdeacon is to be rejected if, after his wife’s death, he takes another; and if he takes a third, a thing that can neither be said nor heard. Council of Toledo I, title 4, chapter 46.

A bigamous subdeacon is to be counted among the lectors or doorkeepers. In the Excerpts of Martin, title 44, chapter 64.

A penitent subdeacon is not to advance to higher ranks. Council of Toledo I, title 2, chapter 46.

The same concerning the same matter. Council of Braga II, title 23, chapter 64.

It is not permitted for anyone except a subdeacon or acolyte to touch the ministries. In the Excerpts of Martin, title 41, chapter 64.

## TITLE XXIV. Concerning those from whom deacons are not to be ordained

[Col. 0033C]

A neophyte is not to be a deacon or presbyter. Council of Arles II, title 1, chapter 22.

Neophytes or laymen are not to be deacons or priests; this is also decreed with an adjuration in the divine name. Letter of Siricius to various persons, 5, title 3.

Bigamists, penitents, and husbands of rejected women are not to be deacons. Council of Arles III, title 3, chapter 23.

Married clerics are not to be deacons unless they profess continence. Council of Orange, title 22, chapter 27.

Bigamous deacons or presbyters are not to minister. Council of Agde, title 1, chapter 30.

That a bigamist or the husband of a widow is worthy of no honor. Decree of Hilary, 74, title 2.

Those who have taken widows are not to become deacons. Council of Toledo I, title 3, chapter 46.

Concerning one who has served in the army after baptism, so that he is not to be advanced to the diaconate. [Col. 0033D] Council of Toledo I, title 8, chapter 46.

## TITLE XXV. Concerning the election and marriages of deacons

It is not permitted for the people to elect altar ministers. Council of Laodicea, title 13, chapter 7.

Concerning those who are chosen for the diaconate while married. In the Excerpts of Martin, title 39, chapter 64.

When deacons are ordained, they are to be questioned about marriage. Council of Ancyra, title 10, chapter 2.

## TITLE XXVI. Concerning the age and periods of service of deacons

That Levites are not to be consecrated before the age of twenty-five. Council of Carthage III, title 4, chapter 14.

The same concerning the same matter: also concerning the consent and profession of married men. Council of Agde, title 16, chapter 30.

Concerning the number of years at which priests and Levites are to be ordained. Council of Toledo IV, title 30, chapter 49.

[Col. 0034A] That a layman is not to become a deacon before one year of conversion has passed. Council of Arles III, title 2, chapter 23.

Concerning the ordination of a deacon or of the entire order, that it is to be celebrated on Sunday, and that both the ordaining bishop and the one ordained are to fast on Saturday. Letter of Leo to Dioscorus, 72, title 1.

Concerning the ordination of the entire order: in which months and at what times it is to take place; and that no one is to be preferred for any advantage over those ordained before them. General Decree of Gelasius, 82, title 13.

## TITLE XXVII. Concerning the rules and number of deacons

It is not permitted for deacons to gather the people separately. Council of Antioch, title 5, chapter 6.

Concerning the honor owed by deacons to presbyters, and by clerics to deacons. Council of Laodicea, title 20, chapter 7.

Concerning the obedience of deacons to presbyters. Council of Carthage IV, title 37, chapter 15.

That a deacon is to do nothing without his presbyter. [Col. 0034B] Council of Arles I, title 18, chapter 21.

A deacon is not to enter taverns. Council of Laodicea, title 24, chapter 7.

That a bishop, presbyter, or deacon is not to use dogs for hunting or hawks. Council of Agde, title 55, chapter 30.

That deacons are permitted neither to offer nor to hand the body of Christ to presbyters, nor to receive communion or sit before them. Council of Nicaea, title 14, chapter 1.

That Levites are not to offer. Council of Arles I, title 15, chapter 21.

It is not permitted for ministers to give bread or bless the chalice. Council of Laodicea, title 25, chapter 7.

A deacon is not to sit before a presbyter or hand over the Eucharist. Council of Arles II, title 15, chapter 22.

A deacon is to give the Eucharist to the people, when necessity requires it, in the presence or at the command of the presbyter. Council of Carthage IV, title 38, chapter 15.

A deacon is to sit at the command of the presbyter. The same council, [Col. 0034C] title 39, chapter 15.

A deacon who is questioned in the presence of a presbyter is to speak. The same council, title 40, chapter 15.

Concerning Levites, that they are not to sit without the presbyter’s command. Council of Agde, title 65, chapter 30.

That it is not permitted for a deacon to sit without being ordered to do so. Council of Braga II, title 40, chapter 64.

A deacon is to wear a white garment only during the time of the offering and the reading. Council of Carthage IV, title 41, chapter 15.

Concerning the use by deacons of a single orarium, neither decorated nor ornate, but plain. Council of Toledo IV, title 40, chapter 49.

Concerning the orarium of deacons: it is not to be concealed but worn over the shoulder. Council of Braga I, title 9, chapter 63.

If a deacon or presbyter commits a capital crime. Council of Orléans I, title 6, chapter 31.

That deacons are to observe their proper measure according to the decrees of the fathers, and are not to baptize unless necessity compels it. General Decree of Gelasius, 82, title 9.

There are to be only seven deacons, even in a large [Col. 0034D] city. Council of Neocaesarea, title 14, chapter 3.

That deacons may neither sit in the presbyterium nor have the right to exercise the distribution of the sacred body. General Decree of Gelasius, 82, title 10.

## TITLE XXVIII. Concerning the ordination of deacons

How deacons are ordained. Council of Carthage IV, title 4, chapter 15.

It is not permitted for clerics to be made in the presence of catechumens. Council of Laodicea, title 4, chapter 7.

Neither deacons nor priests are to be ordained unless all the faithful who are with them are believers. Council of Carthage III, title 18, chapter 14.

## TITLE XXIX. Concerning those from whom presbyters are not to be ordained

A presbyter is not to be ordained from among neophytes. Council of Arles II, title 1, chapter 22.

[Col. 0035A] Neophytes or laymen are not to be presbyters. Letter of Siricius to various persons, 5, title 3.

Bigamists, penitents, and husbands of rejected women are not to be presbyters. Council of Arles III, title 3, chapter 33.

Concerning the prohibition against advancing bigamists to the presbyterate or diaconate. Council of Seville II, title 4, chapter 67.

A bigamist or the husband of a widow is not to be a presbyter. Decree of Hilary, 74, title 2.

Those baptized while ill are not to be presbyters, unless compelled by faith and charity. Council of Neocaesarea, title 12, chapter 3.

## TITLE XXX. Concerning the teaching and rules of presbyters

That priests or clerics ought not to minister in the church wearing cloaks or with their loins unbelted. Letter of Celestine to the bishops of Gaul, 34, title 1.

That parish presbyters, when ordained, are to provide an official document, and that those same presbyters are to be summoned to their duty during litanies. Council of Toledo IV, [Col. 0035B] title 26, chapter 49.

Concerning the things that presbyters are forbidden to do in the ecclesiastical sacraments. Council of Seville II, title 7, chapter 67.

Concerning the profession to be made to the bishop by presbyters or deacons when they are ordained in parishes. Council of Toledo IV, title 27, chapter 49.

It is not permitted for presbyters, disregarding the bishop, to gather the people separately and erect an altar. Council of Antioch, title 5, chapter 6.

A presbyter is not to ordain a minister or consecrate an altar. Council of Agde, title 43, chapter 30.

That a presbyter who presumes to prepare chrism or consecrate a church or altar is to be deposed from office. Council of Braga I, title 19, chapter 63.

A presbyter is not to presume to give a blessing or penance. Council of Agde, title 44, chapter 30.

Chrism, the blessing of girls, and the reconciliation of penitents are not to be performed by presbyters. Council of Carthage II, title 3, chapter 13.

[Col. 0035C] A presbyter, when commanded by his bishop, is to reconcile a penitent. Council of Carthage II, title 4, chapter 13.

How a presbyter may reconcile a penitent in the bishop’s absence when necessity requires it. Council of Carthage III, title 32, chapter 14.

That a presbyter is both to bless and to confirm a neophyte. Council of Riez, title 4, chapter 26.

That a presbyter is not to consecrate a virgin without consulting the bishop, and is never to prepare chrism. Council of Carthage III, title 36, chapter 14.

That a presbyter is not to ordain a deacon or presbyter. Council of Seville II, title 5, chapter 67.

If a presbyter celebrates the rite without consulting the bishop while the bishop is present, he is to be deprived of his rank. Council of Carthage II, title 9, chapter 13.

That, apart from the bishop, no one is to prepare chrism. Council of Toledo I, title 20, chapter 46.

A presbyter is not permitted to chrismate while the bishop is present. In the Excerpts of Martin, title 52, chapter 64.

[Col. 0035D] A presbyter ought not to enter before the bishop’s entrance or sit in the tribunal. Council of Laodicea, title 56, chapter 7.

A presbyter is not permitted to enter the baptistery before the bishop. Council of Braga II, title 53, chapter 64.

Concerning the baptized, that the clergy is to receive nothing. Council of Eliberis, title 48, chapter 38.

That no one is to receive a reward from the baptized. Council of Braga II, title 53, chapter 64.

Concerning presbyters, that they are not to enter into second marriages. In the Excerpts of Martin, title 38, chapter 64.

That foreign presbyters are not to dare to minister in the presence of the bishop or the city’s presbyter. In the Excerpts of Martin, title 56, chapter 64.

That presbyters from another region are not permitted to minister in the presence of the bishop or the city’s presbyter, and concerning the order in which they are to give bread or the chalice. Council of Neocaesarea, title 13, chapter 3.

That no minister is to depart without chrism. Council of Orange, title 2, chapter 27.

[Col. 0036A] If a deacon or presbyter commits a capital crime. Council of Orléans, title 6, chapter 31.

If a presbyter or deacon sells anything belonging to the Church’s ministry. Council of Braga II, title 17, chapter 64.

If parish presbyters receive chrism either personally or through their sacristans. Council of Carthage IV, title 36, chapter 15.

That no one is to receive chrism from another bishop. Council of Vaison I, title 3, chapter 28.

Concerning presbyters, that they are to presume nothing against the bishops; but if they do presume, they are to be deprived both of rank and of communion. Nor will the bishop himself be free from guilt if he neglects to judge one who does such things. General Decree of Gelasius, 82, title 8.

## TITLE XXXI. Concerning the election, age, periods, and ranks of presbyters

How presbyters are ordained. Council of Carthage IV, title 3, chapter 15.

[Col. 0036B] A presbyter is not to be ordained unless all who are with him are faithful. Council of Carthage III, title 18, chapter 14.

How married men are to be advanced to the priesthood. Council of Arles II, title 2, chapter 22.

A layman is not to become a presbyter before one year of conversion has passed. Council of Arles III, title 2, chapter 23.

A layman is not to be ordained presbyter unless he has passed through the ecclesiastical ranks. Council of Braga I, title 20, chapter 63.

A presbyter under thirty years of age is not to be ordained, even if he has an approved life. Council of Neocaesarea, title 11, chapter 3.

That a deacon is not to be ordained before the age of twenty-five. Council of Agde, title 16, chapter 30.

A bishop and presbyter are not to be ordained before full maturity, that is, before the age of thirty. Council of Agde, title 17, chapter 30.

A presbyter is not to be ordained before the age of thirty. In the Excerpts of Martin, title 20, chapter 64.

That the ordination of a presbyter is to be celebrated on Saturday evening. [Col. 0036C] Letter of Leo to Dioscorus, title 1, chapter 72.

Concerning the ordination of the entire order, and in which months and at what times it is to take place. General Decree of Gelasius, 82, title 4.

## TITLE XXXII. Concerning the honor of priests and the oblations they offer, which are not to be despised

Concerning bishops and presbyters, that they are to be received at any church in their proper order and invited both to preach and to celebrate Mass. Council of Carthage IV, title 33, chapter 15.

Concerning the offering of a married presbyter, which is not to be despised. Council of Gangra, title 4, chapter 4.

That a place for celebrating the sacrifice is to be given to a visiting bishop. Council of Arles I, title 19, chapter 21.

## TITLE XXXIII. Concerning heretical and schismatic bishops if they become Catholics

[Col. 0036D] Concerning heretical and schismatic bishops who come to the Catholic faith, and what they are to observe. Council of Riez, title 3, chapter 26.

## TITLE XXXIV. Concerning those from whom bishops are not to be ordained

Concerning those who immediately after baptism become bishops, or who previously possessed a mortal sin. Council of Nicaea, title 2, chapter 1.

A bishop is not to be ordained from among the laity. Council of Sardica, title 13, chapter 5.

A priest is not to be made from among neophytes. Council of Laodicea, title 3, chapter 7.

Neophytes are not to be ministers or priests. Council of Arles II, title 1, chapter 22.

Neophytes or laymen are not to be bishops. Letter of Siricius to various persons, 5, title 3.

Concerning Aggarus and Tiberianus, who were ordained from among the laity. Letter of Leo to the Africans, 69, title 3.

[Col. 0037A] A bishop is not to be chosen from among penitents, however good they may be. Council of Carthage IV, title 1, chapter 15.

Bigamists, penitents, and husbands of rejected women are not to be bishops. Council of Arles III, title 3, chapter 33.

The husbands of widows and those who have contracted numerous marriages are not to be bishops. The nobility of birth and character must also be sought. Letter of Leo to all, 64, title 2.

Bigamists, or the husbands of corrupted women or widows, are not to be bishops. Decree of Hilary, 74, title 2.

Metropolitans are not to ordain laymen, husbands of widows, or bigamists, but irreproachable men. Letter of Leo to Anastasius, 67, title 2.

No unworthy person is to be made a bishop; this is also established by the authority of the Council of Nicaea. Letter of Siricius to various persons, 5, title 1.

Illicit persons are not to be advanced to the episcopate or to any honor. Letter of Leo to the Africans, 69, title 1.

Penitents and those ignorant of letters, or lacking something through bodily defect [Col. 0037B] or amputation, shall not be bishops. Decree of Hilary, 74, title 3.

Those whom neither the clergy elected nor the people sought shall not be regarded as bishops. Letter of Leo to Rusticus, 66, title 1.

No one shall be ordained bishop against the will of those concerned. Letter of Leo to Anastasius, 67, title 4.

No one should be ordained bishop against the will of the clergy or the people. Letter of Celestine to the bishops of Gaul, 34, title 5.

The ministry or priesthood shall not be entrusted to unknown persons. Letter of Siricius through various recipients, 5, title 2.

On the harmful practice and on nearly all the persons who are not to be bishops, and on removing such men; and that two bishops should not be in one church. Letter of Hilary to Ascanian, 75, title 4.

On the ordination of a bishop and on all the persons from whom bishops are not to be ordained, and how and where a bishop is to be ordained. Council of Toledo IV, title 19, canon 49.

[Col. 0037C] One must abstain from illicit ordinations, and no one from the prohibited classes of persons shall be ordained bishop. Letter of Celestine to the bishops of Gaul, 34, title 6.

Each province should be content with its own metropolitan, and foreign, unknown, or itinerant clerics are not to be ordained for another church. Letter of Boniface to Hilary, 32.

No one shall be made bishop contrary to the established order. Letter of Innocent to Aurelius, in full, 17.

A bishop should not be ordained from among the laity while the clergy of the churches are disregarded. Letter of Celestine through Apulia, 35, title 2.

## TITLE XXXV. On chorepiscopi

Chorepiscopi were established on the model of the seventy elders. Council of Neocaesarea, title 13, canon 3.

On chorepiscopi and what powers they may exercise. Council of Ancyra, title 13, canon 2.

[Col. 0037D] Only chorepiscopi shall issue letters of canonical form. Council of Antioch, title 8, canon 6.

On chorepiscopi and their authority. In the preceding work, title 10.

## TITLE XXXVI. On the election, periods, and degrees of bishops

The people are not permitted to elect ministers of the altar. Council of Laodicea, title 13, canon 7.

The same matter, subsequently, concerning the same subject. Letter of Hilary to Ascanian, 75, title 4.

The same matter concerning the election of a bishop. In Martin’s excerpts, title 1, canon 64.

When a bishop is being elected, if he has opponents, five or six bishops shall assemble. Council of Carthage III, title 40, canon 14.

If there is disagreement in the election of a bishop, the opinion of the majority shall prevail; and concerning the primates of the metropolitans. Council of Nicaea, title 6, canon 1.

[Col. 0038A] A bishop shall not be ordained before the age of thirty. Council of Arles III, title 1, canon 23.

At what age a bishop or presbyter is to be ordained. Council of Agde, title 17, canon 30.

A layman shall not be ordained bishop before a year of conversion has passed. Council of Arles III, title 2, canon 23.

A bishop shall not be made from the laity unless he has passed through the prescribed periods and offices. Council of Braga I, title 20, canon 63.

A minister or bishop shall not be made from the laity unless he has observed the prescribed periods. Letter of Innocent to Felix, 9, title 5.

Monks or laymen shall not be bishops unless they have passed through the ecclesiastical degrees. Letter of Zosimus to Hesychius, 28, title 1.

On the periods, degrees, and offices through which each person must pass before he can be a priest. In the same work, title 3.

A bishop shall not be ordained unless all those who are with him are faithful. Council of Carthage III, title 18, canon 14.

The episcopal office must be reached through the ecclesiastical degrees, and no unworthy person shall be ordained [Col. 0038B] bishop. Letter of Celestine to the bishops of Gaul, 34, title 3.

## TITLE XXXVII. That bishops should not be ordained for a reward

Concerning monks or laymen ordained for a reward: together with their ordainers, they incur the crime of simony. General decree of Gelasius, 82, title 26.

It is wholly improper to ordain, for money, either any cleric or anyone to any office in the church, whatever the rank or person. Council of Chalcedon, title 2, canon 11.

A reward must not be accepted for the honor of the episcopate; and concerning participation in sin. Letter of Hormisdas to the bishops throughout Spain, 91, title 2.

No one shall accept an ecclesiastical honor in exchange for any reward. Letter of Symmachus to Caesarius, 85, title 2.

On the condemnation of clerics who attain ecclesiastical degrees through money. Council of Toledo VI, title 4, canon 51.

## TITLE XXXVIII. That bishops should not be ordained through canvassing, and that there should not be two bishops in one church, nor should one bishop hold two sees

[Col. 0038C]

No one shall seek the episcopate through canvassing. Letter of Symmachus to Caesarius, 85, title 5.

No one shall be ordained bishop through canvassing. Letter of Boniface to the emperor Honorius, in full, 30.

If two bishops are again ordained at Rome, both shall be rejected. Rescript of the emperor Honorius to Boniface, in full, p. 39.

That there should not be two bishops in one church, and concerning the removal of those who have been illicitly ordained. Letter of Hilary to Ascanian, 75, title 4.

Where he rejoices over the emperor’s faith concerning what was accomplished at the Council of Chalcedon, and concerning Anatolius, who sought, contrary to the decrees of Nicaea, to subject the churches of Alexandria and Antioch to himself through canvassing. Letter [Col. 0038D] of Leo to the emperor Marcian, in full, 55.

Where he praises Anatolius, bishop of Constantinople, for his faith at the Council of Chalcedon, but later rebukes him because he had wished, contrary to the Nicene synod, to subject the churches of Alexandria and Antioch to himself. Letter of Leo to Anatolius, in full, 55.

## TITLE XXXIX. That bishops should not be ordained without the metropolitan

A bishop shall not be ordained without the metropolitan bishop. Council of Nicaea, title 6, canon 1.

It is not permitted to ordain a bishop without the council of the metropolitan bishop or of all the bishops of the entire province. Council of Antioch VI, title 19, canon 6.

A bishop shall not be ordained without the counsel of the metropolitan and all the neighboring bishops, and without verification of his life and worthiness in learning. Council of Laodicea, title 12, canon 7.

No one shall be ordained bishop without the counsel of the metropolitan. Council of Carthage II, title 12, canon 13.

[Col. 0039A] No one shall be ordained bishop without the metropolitan; and concerning the days of the funeral rites of a deceased man. Council of Regium, title 6, canon 26.

No bishop is to be ordained without the metropolitan’s knowledge, nor by a single bishop. Letter of Innocent to Victoricus, 7, title 1.

No one shall be ordained bishop while disregarding the metropolitan; and concerning the authority of the Council of Nicaea. Letter of Boniface to Hilary of Narbonne, in full, 32.

A bishop is not to be ordained without the metropolitan. Council of Arles II, title 6, canon 22.

A bishop is not to be ordained without the presence of the metropolitan and three bishops, or without the consent of all those absent. Council of Arles II, title 5, canon 22.

A bishop is not to be ordained without the metropolitan and the neighboring bishops. In Martin’s excerpts, title 3, canon 64.

No bishop shall be ordained without the consent of the metropolitan. Letter of Hilary to Ascanian and the bishops of Tarragona, 75, title 1.

[Col. 0039B] Whoever is not ordained bishop in the metropolitan city shall appear there within two months after being presented. Council of Tarragona, title 5, canon 39.

## TITLE XL. That a bishop should not be ordained by two bishops

Two bishops shall not presume to ordain a bishop. Council of Carthage III, title 39, canon 14.

A bishop ordained by two bishops shall not be recognized. Council of Regium, title 1, canon 26.

If someone has been ordained by two bishops under compulsion, he himself shall remain a bishop, while the ordainers shall be endangered; but if he accepted it willingly, he too shall cease from office. Council of Orange, title 21, canon 27.

A person ordained by two bishops may at times be a bishop. Council of Regium, title 2, canon 26.

Bishops improperly ordained may sometimes remain in office out of necessity or by indulgence. Letter of Hilary to Ascanian, 75, title 4.

[Col. 0039C] No bishop shall be ordained without three bishops. Council of Arles I, title 20, canon 21.

## TITLE XLI. On bishops to be ordained at the request of the people

On bishops to be ordained at the request of the people, and that they should not be ordained in an insignificant or small place. Council of Sardica, title 6, canon 5.

Bishops are not to be ordained in villages or hamlets, nor are presbyters to do anything without a bishop. Council of Laodicea, title 57, canon 7.

## TITLE XLII. On bishops unwilling to undertake the ministry or occupy the see

On bishops who, after receiving the laying on of hands, do not agree to undertake the ministry. Council of Antioch, title 17, canon 6.

On a contemptuous bishop, if he is unwilling to perform the priestly office. In Martin’s excerpts, title 11, canon 64.

On a rebellious bishop who does not accept the parish in which he was ordained but seeks another. In Martin’s excerpts, title 12, canon 64.

On a bishop absent through necessity. In Martin’s excerpts, title 10, canon 64.

## TITLE XLIII. On bishops who, after ordination, are not received by the people

On bishops who, after being ordained, are not received. Council of Ancyra, title 18, canon 2.

On bishops who are not received, not because of fault but because of opposition from the congregations. Council of Antioch, title 18, canon 6.

## TITLE XLIV. On the funeral rites of a dying bishop and his acts

How a bishop is to be buried. Council of Valence, title 4, canon 45.

On the funeral rites of a dying bishop. Council of Toledo VII, title 3, canon 52.

[Col. 0040A] A bishop who has buried another bishop shall take charge of that bishop’s church. Council of Regium, title 5, canon 26.

The heirs of a dying priest shall not presume to take possession of his property before the appointed order has been observed. Council of Toledo IX, title 7, canon 54.

How much benefit a bishop may take for himself from the church whose priest he has buried. Council cited above, title 9.

## TITLE XLV. On not appointing successors to bishops

A bishop ought not to appoint his own successor. Council of Antioch, title 23, canon 6.

On not appointing successors. In Martin’s excerpts, title 8, canon 64.

A bishop shall not choose his own successor. Decree of Hilary, 74.

## TITLE XLVI. On not delaying the ordination of bishops

After the death of a bishop, the ordination of another must not be delayed for more than three months [Col. 0040B]. Council of Chalcedon, title 25, canon 11.

An interim administrator shall not retain the dead man’s see through any sedition. Council of Carthage V, title 8, canon 16.

## TITLE XLVII. On bishops to be ordained

How bishops are to be consecrated. Council of Carthage IV, title 2, canon 15.

How bishops ought to be ordained. Council of Nicaea, title 4, canon 1.

What kind of men, and how learned, bishops ought to be when ordained. Council of Carthage IV, title 1, canon 15.

On the ordination of a bishop. In Martin’s excerpts, title 2, canon 64.

When the ordination of ministers and priests is to take place. Letter of Leo to Dioscorus, 72, title 1.

In which months and at what times ordination is to take place. Decree of Gelasius, 82, title 13.

On all those who are to be ordained according to the provisions of the canons. [Col. 0040C] Letter of Hormisdas to the bishops throughout Spain, 91, title 1.

## TITLE XLVIII. On the learning and rules of bishops

A bishop shall know the canons before he is ordained. Council of Carthage III, title 3, canon 14.

Priests shall possess knowledge of the sacred Scriptures and the canons. Council of Toledo IV, title 25, canon 49.

A bishop shall read books of heretics or pagans only when necessity requires it. Council of Carthage IV, title 16, canon 15.

A bishop ought not to be absent from his church on Sunday. Council of Orléans I, title 27, canon 31.

A bishop shall have his lodging not far from the church. Council of Carthage IV, title 14, canon 15.

A bishop shall have simple furnishings and a modest table. Council cited above, title 15, canon 15.

A reading ought to be read at all the priests’ tables [Col. 0040D]. Council of Toledo III, title 7, canon 48.

A bishop shall not take upon himself any concern for household affairs; he shall devote himself solely to action and teaching. Council of Carthage IV, title 20, canon 15.

Bishops should recognize that responsibility for the people and the poor has been entrusted to them. Council of Toledo IV, title 32, canon 49.

A bishop shall protect the poor and the sick. Council of Orléans I, title 12, canon 31.

A bishop shall administer the care of widows, orphans, and the poor not personally but through his subordinates. Council of Carthage IV, title 17, canon 15.

A bishop shall not undertake the guardianship of wills. Council of Carthage IV, title 18, canon 15.

A bishop shall not litigate, even when challenged, over transitory matters. Council cited above, title 19, canon 15.

A bishop shall rebuke a foreign cleric who is sinning. Council of Vaison I, title 8, canon 28.

On priests who send messengers to a foreign people. Council of Toledo IV, title 30, canon 49.

[Col. 0041A] A bishop may prepare chrism at any time. In Martin’s excerpts, title 51, canon 64.

A bishop shall accept nothing for chrism. Council of Braga II, title 4, canon 64.

A bishop shall demand nothing for the consecration of a basilica. Council of Braga II, title 5, canon 64.

A bishop, wherever he is seated, shall not allow a presbyter to remain standing. Council of Carthage IV, title 34, canon 15.

On bishops giving one another precedence in seating, while preserving the primacy of the metropolitan. Council of Braga I, title 6, canon 63.

On the presbyter’s agreement with the bishop in the church. Council of Carthage IV, title 35, canon 15.

Whatever the predecessor-bishop illicitly lost, or whatever was illicitly entrusted to others, shall be corrected by his successor. Decree of Hilary, 64, title 4.

A bishop shall accept no advantage when ordaining clerics. Council of Braga II, title 3, canon 64.

## TITLE XLIX. On the metropolitan

[Col. 0041B]

The metropolitan shall report the elected bishop to the bishop holding the primatial office; likewise, the provincial bishops shall report the elected metropolitan; and how a metropolitan bishop is to be ordained. Letter of Leo to Anastasius, 67, title 5.

On the authority of the metropolitan, without whom the other bishops ought to do nothing, and who ought to do nothing without the other bishops; and on referring the affairs of the other bishops to his judgment. Council of Antioch, title 9, canon 6.

On the primacy of the metropolitan, without whom the other bishops ought to do nothing, and who ought to do nothing without the other bishops. In Martin’s excerpts, title 4, canon 64.

The rights of metropolitans shall be preserved. Letter of Leo to Anastasius, 67, title 1.

## TITLE L. On the primacy of archbishops

On the primacy of the bishops of Alexandria, Rome, and [Col. 0041C] Antioch, and that an episcopal ordination performed without the metropolitan must be entirely suspended. Council of Nicaea, title 6, canon 1.

On the honor of the bishop of Jerusalem. Council of Nicaea VII, canon 1.

On the honor of the bishop of Antioch. Letter of Innocent to Boniface, 19.

On the primacy of the bishops of Alexandria, the East, Antioch, and Asia. Council of Constantinople I, title 2, canon 8.

The bishop of the first see shall not be called “Prince of the Priests.” Council of Carthage III, title 26, canon 14.

That the first see is remembered as being at Antioch, belonging to blessed Peter, and that no bishop is to be ordained without the bishop holding the primacy. Letter of Innocent to Alexander, 23, title 1.

That the bishops of Thessalonica fulfilled the function of the apostolic see [Col. 0041D], and that correction should be applied with affection, while condemnation should not readily be exercised for minor causes. Letter of Leo to Anastasius, 67, title 15 and following.

On the delegated authority of the apostolic see. Letter of Simplicius to Zeno of Seville, in full, 77.

On the instructions issued and the delegated authority. Letter of Hormisdas to John, bishop of the church of Ilici, in full, 89.

He is to act more willingly and with greater authority against heretics; and he commands him to assume his own person. Letter of Hormisdas to Epiphanius, in full, 93.

On the delegated authority throughout Baetica and Lusitania. Letter of Hormisdas to Sallustius, in full, 94.

## TITLE LII. On clerics ordained contrary to prohibition or begetting sons

Clerics ordained contrary to prohibition, or dishonorably begetting sons, shall be deprived of honor and rank [Col. 0042A]. Council of Turin, title 7, canon 25.

Clerics ordained contrary to the canons shall be deposed. Council of Lérida, title 12, canon 44.

Whoever has been ordained contrary to the prohibitions shall be deposed together with his ordainers. On the commemoration of the Council of Nicaea. Letter of Innocent to everyone in Toulouse, 27, title 3.

Those who ordain contrary to the prohibition shall be excommunicated. Council of Arles III, title 3, canon 23.

## TITLE LIII. On priests and Levites promoted without examination and confessing voluntarily

On presbyters who, after being promoted, were later examined and confessed their sins. Council of Nicaea, title 9, canon 1.

If a presbyter has confessed or has been convicted of having sinned before ordination. Council of Neocaesarea, title 9, canon 3.

The same matter concerning deacons. In the work cited above, title 10, canon 3.

[Col. 0042B] If a presbyter or deacon is convicted after ordination of having sinned before it, and likewise concerning the other clerics. In Martin’s excerpts, title 25, canon 64.

On deacons, if they are proved to have sinned before receiving their honor. Council of Elvira, title 76, canon 88.

If a priest or Levite confesses a crime concerning himself. Council of Valencia, title 4, canon 24.

If a presbyter or deacon commits a capital crime, he shall at once be expelled both from office and from communion. Council of Orléans I, title 6, canon 31.

If a presbyter or deacon, because of some offense, abstains from the Eucharist. Council of Orléans I, title 8, canon 31.

## TITLE LIV. On the chastity of the entire clerical order and on those who profess it voluntarily

On the chastity of ministers and priests. Council of [Col. 0042C] Toledo IV, title 21, canon 49.

A bishop shall have suitable witnesses in his private chamber. Council of Toledo IV, title 22, canon 49.

Presbyters and deacons shall likewise have witnesses to their way of life. Council cited above, title 23, canon 49.

Chastity shall be observed by priests and Levites. Council of Carthage II, title 2, canon 13.

On adulterers. Council of Ancyra, title 20, canon 2.

If a presbyter marries or commits adultery. Council of Neocaesarea, title 1, canon 3.

On priests and ministers if they commit adultery. Council of Elvira, title 18, canon 38.

On those who serve at the altar if they suddenly fall through the grievous weakness of the flesh. Council of Lérida, title 5, canon 44.

On priests and ministers who fornicate. In Martin’s excerpts, title 27, canon 64.

Clerics shall not associate with widows in familiar companionship. Council of Carthage IV, title 102, canon 15.

Clerics shall also visit their own blood relatives with a witness [Col. 0042D]. Council of Tarragona, title 1, canon 39.

Clerics and doorkeepers who associate with adulterous women are to be expelled. Council cited above, title 9, canon 39.

On clerics with whom women live. Council of Seville I, title 3, canon 66.

## TITLE LV. On clerics abstaining from their own wives

On priests and Levites, that they are to abstain from their wives. Council of Carthage V, title 3, canon 16.

On those who are found incontinent after receiving the diaconate. Council of Orange, title 23, canon 27.

On presbyters and deacons who return to the marital bed. Council of Agde, title 9, canon 30.

On priests and ministers, that they are to abstain from their wives. Council of Elvira, title 33, canon 38.

On presbyters and deacons if they beget sons after ordination. Council of Toledo I, title 1, canon 46.

[Col. 0043A] Bishops, presbyters, and deacons coming from heresy may not have sexual relations with their wives; likewise, those who have always been Catholic shall not live in private rooms with unrelated women. Women who are found there, however, shall be sold by the bishops. Council of Toledo III, title 5, canon 48.

On incontinent clerics and the imposition of chastity. Letter of Siricius to Eumerius, 3, title 7.

Priests and Levites ought not to have intercourse with their wives but must be entirely chaste. Letter of Innocent to Victoricus, 7, title 9.

On the incontinence of priests and Levites. Letter of Innocent to Exuperius, 8, title 1.

Those who have begotten sons while in the priesthood are to be removed from office. Letter of Innocent to Maximus, 10.

On priests and ministers: they must cease from conjugal activity, but must not repudiate their marriages. Letter of Leo to Rusticus, 66, title 3.

[Col. 0043B] Carnal marriage is denied to subdeacons and clerics of higher rank. Letter of Leo to Anastasius, 67, title 3.

If any married persons have been ordained without testimony. Council of Gerunda, title 6, canon 40.

## TITLE LVI. That women should not live together with clerics

On women living in a cleric’s household. Council of Nicaea, title 3, canon 1.

No cleric of any rank shall have an unrelated woman in his household, except the persons listed below. Council of Arles II, title 3, canon 22.

The same concerning those women, and that a cleric should not visit the house of an unrelated woman. Council of Agde, title 10, canon 30.

On the women who may live with clerics. Letter of Siricius to Eumerius, 3, title 12.

On women living in a cleric’s household and adoptive women, and that religious women should not have the companionship of any layman or outsider. In Martin’s excerpts, title 32, canon 64.

A cleric or a woman dedicated to religious observance shall not live with unrelated men or women. Council of Carthage I, title 3, canon 12.

Unrelated women shall not live with clerics. Council of Carthage III, title 17, canon 14.

On removing women from association with clerics. Council of Toledo IV, title 42, canon 49.

A cleric shall not live with unrelated women. Council of Carthage IV, title 46, canon 15.

No cleric of any rank shall admit a girl into his storeroom or private quarters. Council of Arles II, title 4, canon 22.

No cleric shall admit any woman into his storeroom or private quarters. Council of Agde, title 11, canon 30.

On familiarity with unrelated women. Council of Orléans I, title 25, canon 31.

Clerics shall not have unrelated women in their homes. Council of Elvira, title 27, canon 38.

Clerics ordained without wives shall not have unrelated women in their homes. Council of Gerunda, title 7, canon 40.

No cleric from the subdiaconate upward shall live with an unrelated woman. Also concerning the regulation of the work of female servants. Council of Toledo II, title 3, canon 47.

Clerics shall not live with unrelated women. Council of Lérida, title 15, canon 44.

On the sale of women who are known to be attached to clerics. Council of Toledo IV, title 43, canon 49.

## TITLE LVII. On the evil of unconsummated desire

On unconsummated desire. Council of Neocaesarea, title 4, canon 3.

## TITLE LVIII. On priests and all clerics who desert and are not to be transferred to another place

[Col. 0044A]

Wherever someone is first enrolled, there he shall remain a cleric. Council of Carthage VI, title 15, canon 17.

No one shall leave his church for any reason of necessity. Council of Arles II, title 13, canon 22.

No cleric shall leave his bishop and transfer himself to another, or communicate with him, except when he transfers from heresy to the Church. Council of Toledo I, title 12, canon 46.

A cleric who migrates to another church ought not to remain there. Council of Antioch, title 3, canon 6.

A cleric may not minister in two churches, but must either be restored to the first or established in the second. Council of Chalcedon, title 10, canon 11.

A cleric of any rank who transfers elsewhere shall be excommunicated. Council of Arles I, title 21, canon 21.

[Col. 0044B] On clerics who desert. In Martin’s excerpts, title 34, canon 64.

Likewise, on clerics who desert, that they are to be restored to their bishops. Council of Seville II, title 3, canon 67.

If a bishop, presbyter, or deacon departs from the church or city in which he was ordained. Council of Nicaea, title 15, canon 1.

On wandering and disobedient clerics, ministers, and priests. Council of Valence, title 5, canon 45.

On presbyters, deacons, and clerics who transfer to other cities: they are not to be received elsewhere but compelled to return altogether. Council of Nicaea, title 16, canon 1.

A bishop shall not pass from one province to another unless he has been invited. Council of Sardica, title 2, canon 5.

On priests who abandon their churches and migrate to other churches. Letter of Damasus to Paulinus, 2, title 3.

On Anatolius, the bishop who attempted to usurp the church of Antioch and Alexandria. Letter of Leo [Col. 0044C] to Marcian, 55.

On the same subject. Letter of the same man to the same Anatolius, 56.

Bishops who have not been invited shall not enter beyond their dioceses. Council of Constantinople I, title 3, canon 8.

On one who, through ambition, transfers from a lesser city to a greater one and wishes to exercise the clerical office there. In Martin’s excerpts, title 5, canon 64.

A bishop or any member of the clergy may not transfer to another city. Council of Chalcedon, title 5, canon 11.

A bishop ought not to transfer from one diocese to another, whether driven by force or induced by persuasion. Council of Antioch, title 21, canon 6.

A bishop ought not to invade another city. Council of Antioch, title 22, canon 6.

A bishop shall not transfer from an obscure place to a distinguished one. Council of Carthage IV, title 27, canon 15.

A bishop ought not to be transferred to another city. Council of Sardica, title 1, canon 5.

No bishop shall leave his own church and transfer to another, where the bishops of Rome also celebrate their natal feast. Letter of Hilary to Ascanian, 75, title 2.

Ireneus, removed from Barcelona, is to return to his own church. Letter of Hilary to Ascanian, 75, title 3.

On the condemnation of Ireneus if he does not return to his own church. Letter of Hilary to Ascanian, 75, title 5.

On the removal of Ireneus; that improperly ordained bishops may remain in office through necessity or indulgence; and that two bishops must not be permitted in one church. Letter of Hilary to Ascanian, 76.

Bishops shall govern their own dioceses and shall not enter others. Council of Constantinople I, title 2, canon 8.

On not changing one’s parish. In Martin’s excerpts, title 6, canon 64.

If a bishop, abandoning his own city, seeks a greater see through ambition, he shall neither obtain that see nor retain his own. Letter of Leo to Anastasius, 57, title 7.

[Col. 0045A] On bishops holding possessions in another province. Council of Sardica, title 15, canon 5.

On bishops who build a basilica not on their own property but in another diocese. Council of Orange, title 10, canon 27.

Episcopal transfers are not permitted. Council of Carthage III, title 38, canon 14.

A bishop shall not remain in another province, even if he is more learned. Council of Sardica, title 14, canon 5.

Clerics who have suffered violence, if they go to another city, shall not be forbidden to remain there for as long as they are able. Council cited above, title 21, canon 5.

Clerics shall not remain in another city without necessity. Council of Carthage III, title 37, canon 14.

Foreign clerics shall not linger at Thessalonica. Council of Sardica, title 20, canon 5.

Bishops may not transfer to another province and ordain clerics there. Council of Antioch, title 13, canon 6.

On bishops who presume to perform ordinations in another province. In Martin’s excerpts, title 7, canon 64.

If anyone receives a deserter from his own church and promotes him to some dignity, he shall be subject to the sentence prescribed by the canons. General decree of Gelasius, 82, title 25.

## TITLE LIX. On priests and clerics to be lawfully transferred

On bishops and clerics lawfully transferred to another place. Council of Carthage IV, title 27, canon 15.

A bishop who has many clerics shall, when requested, give one to a bishop who needs one for ordination. Council of Carthage III, title 45, canon 14.

## TITLE LX. That no one may ordain or retain in his church another’s cleric, monk, layman, citizen, freedman, or slave

An alien cleric may not be ordained in another church without the consent of his own bishop [Col. 0045C]. Council of Nicaea, title 17, canon 1.

A bishop may not ordain another bishop’s cleric in his own church. Council of Sardica, title 18, canon 5.

Likewise, on the foregoing matter. Council cited above, title 19.

Bishops may not ordain clerics in another province. Council of Antioch, title 13, canon 6.

Likewise, on the foregoing matter. Council cited above, title 22.

Likewise, on the foregoing matter. Council of Constantinople I, title 3, canon 8.

No one shall appropriate another’s cleric for himself. Council of Carthage III, title 44, canon 14.

A bishop shall not retain or ordain another’s cleric. Council of Carthage III, title 21, canon 14.

No one shall ordain another’s cleric, nor shall anyone be a cleric who has not pledged the place where he has been ordained. [Col. 0046A] Council of Valence, title 6, canon 45.

On a cleric who transfers to another church, and on the one who receives him. Council of Toledo II, title 2, canon 47.

No bishop shall presume to ordain another bishop’s cleric. Council of Braga I, title 8, canon 63.

On clerics who desert. Council of Seville II, title 3, canon 67.

Clerics may in no way migrate to another city, except those who have lost their own cities. Council of Chalcedon, title 20, canon 11.

No bishop shall usurp the right to ordain another’s cleric. Letter of Innocent to Victoricus, 7, title 7.

One person shall not promote another’s cleric, nor receive one who has been rejected. Council of Turin, title 6, canon 25.

No one shall presume to entice or retain another’s cleric, nor to take anything valuable from the brothers of the church. Letter of Leo to Anastasius, 67, title 8.

Whoever attempts to defend another’s cleric shall be deprived of communion. Council of Arles III, title 4, canon 23.

[Col. 0046B] On those who have presumed to ordain another’s cleric. Council of Orange, title 8, canon 27.

Bishops shall not strive to claim for themselves clerics belonging to another’s authority. General decree of Gelasius, 82, title 16.

On not receiving wandering clerics, and on regulating the ordination of one who has been ordained by another bishop without the consent of his own bishop. In Martin’s excerpts, title 33, canon 64.

A cleric or layman shall not be ordained in another’s church. Council of Carthage I, title 5, canon 12.

On clerics or monks ordained by another bishop. Council of Carthage V, title 13, canon 16.

On those who have ordained citizens belonging to another place. Council of Orange, title 9, canon 27.

If a bishop has made another’s slave a cleric and ordained him deacon or presbyter. Council of Orléans I, title 5, canon 31.

No bishop shall promote another’s slave to the clerical office [Col. 0046C]. Letter of Leo to all the bishops throughout Campania, 64, title 1.

No one shall receive another’s slave into a monastery without his master’s consent. Council of Chalcedon, title 4, canon 11.

A slave must not, on the pretext of religion, despise his master. Council of Gangra, title 3, canon 4.

On not teaching another’s slaves to despise their master. In Martin’s excerpts, title 42, canon 64.

Slaves shall not be received or claimed in monasteries or among the clergy under the pretext of religion. General decree of Gelasius, 82, title 16.

If a bishop has made another’s slave a deacon or presbyter, he shall restore the slave with double compensation. Council of Orléans I, title 5, canon 31.

# BOOK TWO. ON THE INSTITUTIONS OF MONASTERIES AND MONKS, AND ON THE ORDERS OF PENITENTS

[Col. 0045]

## VERSE EXCHANGE: WHERE THE READER SPEAKS TO THE CORRESPONDING CODEX

[Col. 0045D]

**I.** After we had sanctified flowers gathered from the turf,

And carefully distinguished the sacred fields in order,

Where do you now command me to go, or by what path do you send me?

**R.** It is well that the ministers occupy the places assigned beforehand;

But now, diligently arrange the maidenly cohort,

[Col. 0046D] Bind the widow; let the penitent feel sorrow in her heart,

And let not that woman laugh wantonly in her movements

Who, still flourishing in pleasures, is dead while living.

**I.** With all our effort, if the Lord wills, we shall go there,

Where the great judgment of your mouth commands us.

## TITLE I. On monasteries of men and their orders

[Col. 0045D]

On monasteries not to be torn down. Council of Seville II, title 10, canon 67.

[Col. 0046D] New cells or communities shall not be built without the bishop’s knowledge. Council of Agde, title 58, canon 30.

No one shall build a monastery without consulting the bishop. If monks wander away, they shall be brought back; and, if necessary, with the abbot’s consent, a monk may be made a cleric [Col. 0047A]. Council of Agde, title 27, canon 30.

A bishop may make a monastery from one of the parish churches and may contribute from the church’s property whatever he wishes. Council of Toledo III, title 4, canon 48.

If a bishop builds a monastery or enriches a parish church, what portion of the church’s property he may contribute. Council of Toledo IX, title 4, canon 54.

A monk shall not build a cell for himself without the permission of the bishop or abbot. Council of Orléans I, title 18, canon 31.

On the authority to be exercised by a bishop in monasteries; and that places consecrated as monasteries must not subsequently be made secular habitations. Council of Chalcedon, title 24, canon 11.

On the limits of the authority that bishops may exercise in monasteries. Council of Toledo IV, title 51, canon 49.

Abbots shall be under the authority of the bishop; also concerning wandering monks and not receiving another’s monk [Col. 0047B]. Council of Orléans I, title 15, canon 31.

On clerics, monks, or laymen who are in poorhouses, monasteries, or martyrs’ shrines: they are to be under the authority of the bishop of each city. Council of Chalcedon, title 8, canon 11.

One abbot shall not be placed over two coenobia. Council of Agde, title 57, canon 30.

On the honor appropriate to a monk, and that none of them should undertake ecclesiastical or secular affairs, nor have the right to establish monasteries or oratories for himself. Council of Chalcedon, title 4, canon 11.

On wandering monks and those who have left the monastery. Council of Toledo IV, title 52, canon 49.

Clerics and monks shall not depart without a letter from the bishop. Also concerning the cells of abbots and monks, and concerning sick and aged monks. Council of Agde, title 38, canon 30.

On clerics and monks who do not remain in their profession. Council of Chalcedon, title 7, canon 11.

[Col. 0047C] On monks or maidens dedicated to God: they may not enter into marriage. Council cited above, title 16.

Monks shall not use the orarium or zancae. Council of Orléans I, title 16, canon 31.

If a monk takes a wife. Council cited above, title 17.

On monks being ordained clerics with the abbot’s consent; on not taking away what is offered to the monastery; and on basilicas built by laymen. Council of Lérida, title 3, canon 44.

On the advancement of monks to the clergy. Letter of Siricius to Eumerius, 3, title 13.

A monk sent somewhere must not presume to perform clerical ministry, nor act as a merchant or an executor. Council of Tarragona, title 11, canon 39.

On the profession of monks and the profession of their parents. Council of Toledo IV, title 49, canon 49.

## TITLE II. On monasteries for women

[Col. 0047D] A monastery for girls must be established far from monks. Council of Agde, title 28, canon 30.

Monasteries of virgins must be protected from monks. Council of Seville II, title 11, canon 67.

## TITLE III. On the guardianship of consecrated virgins

How consecrated virgins are to be protected by the bishop or priests. Council of Carthage III, title 33, canon 14.

A man to be placed over religious women must be approved by the bishop. Council of Carthage IV, title 97, canon 15.

That it pertains to the guilt of the priest if widows or religious women associate with the clergy who preside over them in familiar relationships. Council of the same [council], title 102, canon 15.

## TITLE IV. On the ordination of consecrated virgins

How a religious virgin is to be ordained. Council of Carthage IV, title 11, canon 15.

[Col. 0048A] Virgins are not to be ordained before the age of twenty-five. Council of Carthage III, title 4, canon 14.

Religious virgins are not to receive the veil before the age of forty. Council of Agde, title 19, canon 30.

Before the age of forty, religious virgins are not to receive the veil. Council of Zaragoza I, title 8, canon 41.

On the non-ordination of deaconesses. Council of Orange, title 26, canon 27.

On deaconesses who have fallen, and that they are not to be ordained before the age of forty. Council of Chalcedon, title 15, canon 11.

## TITLE V. On the time for veiling virgins

On the times at which sacred virgins are to receive the veil; nevertheless, because of necessity, at any time—as has also been said concerning baptism—so that they may not depart without this gift, which they are said to have lamented. Decree of Gelasius, 82, title 14.

## TITLE VI. On veiled sacred virgins who afterward fall, and on those who corrupt them

[Col. 0048B]

On veiled sacred virgins, if they should fall publicly or secretly. Letter of Innocent to Victoricus, 7, title 12.

On girls who have already been consecrated, if they afterward marry and thus incur the double crime of violating both their profession and their consecration. Letter of Leo to Rusticus, 66, title 14.

On sacred virgins who have not received the veil, if they should fall. Letter of Innocent to Victoricus, 7, title 13.

That girls who, not under compulsion but of their own will, have undertaken the profession of virginity commit an offense when they marry, even if they have not yet been consecrated. Letter of Leo to Rusticus of Narbonne, 66, title 13.

If a consecrated woman marries or commits adultery, she is to be assigned to penance. Council of Valence, title 2, canon 24.

On virgins consecrated to God, if they commit adultery. Council of Elvira, title 13, canon 38.

[Col. 0048C] If a consecrated woman commits adultery, she is to do penance for ten years; if she marries, she is not to be admitted to penance unless her husband has died. Council of Toledo I, title 16, canon 46.

If a consecrated woman sins or marries. In Martin’s excerpts, title 31, canon 64.

On sacred virgins who have suffered barbarian violence: that their minds are not considered corrupted on account of the violent corruption of their bodies, and that they are more praiseworthy if they do not compare themselves with those who are undefiled. Letter of Leo to the African bishops, 69, title 4.

That ravishers of widows or virgins, and those who marry sacred virgins by force or willingly, be deprived of communion. Letter of Symmachus to Caesarius, 85, title 3.

That those who join themselves to sacred virgins and enter into incestuous unions may not receive communion unless they have performed public penance; but when such persons depart from this world, the viaticum is not to be denied them. General decree of Gelasius, 82, title 22.

## TITLE VII. On the distinction between widows and virgins

[Col. 0048D]

On the distinction between secular and religious widows and virgins. Council of Toledo IV, title 56, canon 49.

On the profession and clothing of religious widows. Council of Toledo X, title 4, canon 55.

## TITLE VIII. On the proving of religious widows and virgins

Widows who have remained in their religious profession through long observance, and virgins who have spent many years in monasteries, are altogether forbidden to marry. Letter of Symmachus to Caesarius, 85, title 4.

On women who have professed widowhood before the bishop. Council of Orange, title 27, canon 27.

On removing the excuses of widows who follow transgression. Council of Toledo X, title 5, canon 55.

## TITLE IX. On the prohibition of women’s ministry

[Col. 0049A]

On women: that they are not to minister at the sacred altars or presume to undertake anything assigned to the offices of men. General decree of Gelasius, 82, title 28.

That no professed woman or widow, in the priest’s absence, perform priestly functions or light the lamp in her own house. Council of Toledo I, title 9, canon 46.

Women ought not to enter the altar area. Council of Laodicea, title 45, canon 7.

That women not enter the sacristy. In Martin’s excerpts, title 42, canon 64.

How widows or religious women are to be appointed to the ministry of baptism. Council of Carthage IV, title 12, canon 15.

That women not presume to teach publicly. Council of Carthage IV, title 99, canon 15.

That a woman must not dare to baptize. Council of the same [council], title 100.

## TITLE X. On widows not receiving the veil

[Col. 0049B]

Widows are not to receive the veil, because neither divine authority nor the established form of the canons has instituted this. General decree of Gelasius, 82, title 15.

That widows, as stated above, are not to receive the veil; and if, after changing their intention, they trample upon the continence they have professed, they themselves must render an account to God on their own behalf. General decree of Gelasius, 82, title 23.

## TITLE XI. On the chastity and rules of widows

Strangers must not reside with widows or widow-women. Council of Carthage I, title 4, canon 12.

On adolescent and infirm widows being supported from the provisions of the Church. Council of Carthage IV, title 101, canon 15.

That widows who are supported by the Church’s allowances assist the Church by their merits and prayers. In the same [source], [Col. 0049C] title 103.

Elderly widows are not to be received as though they had been ordained. Council of Laodicea, title 11, canon 7.

## TITLE XII. On the chastity of monks and virgins

On monks or girls dedicated to God: that they may not be joined in marriage. Council of Chalcedon, title 16, canon 11.

Clergy or religious women must not live with unrelated men or women. Council of Carthage I, title 3, canon 12.

Clergy, or persons professing continence, must never approach virgins or widows alone. Council of Carthage III, title 25, canon 14.

That a religious girl must not maintain intimacy with men. Council of Toledo I, title 6, canon 46.

On monks and virgins who do not maintain their profession of chastity. Letter of Siricius to Eumerius, 3, title 6.

That if anyone abandons the monastic profession, he must be cleansed by the public satisfaction of penance. Letter of [Col. 0049D] Leo to Rusticus, 66, title 12.

On sacred men and women who transgress their sacred profession. Council of Toledo VI, title 6, canon 51.

## TITLE XIII. On adulterous widows

On adulterous widows, if they afterward have the same man as husband. Council of Elvira, title 72, canon 38.

## TITLE XIV. On seeking the benefit of penance

That a Christian ought not to postpone conversion from day to day, lest he encounter the straits of his final hour. Letter of Leo to Theodore of Fréjus, 70.

## TITLE XV. What penance can accomplish

That in every time of necessity and danger, penance [Col. 0050A] and reconciliation must be conferred without delay. Letter of Leo to Theodore of Fréjus, 70.

That it is not fitting for a Christian, during the course of life, to place his hope in indulgences. In the same [source].

## TITLE XVI. On postponing penance and communion

On those who delay doing penance through fear of committing a more serious offense. Letter of Leo to Rusticus, 66, title 7.

On those who, prevented by some obstacle, do not come forward to receive penance: that this remedy of penance cannot be given to them after death, and that their merits must be sought in God’s judgment. Letter of Leo to Theodore of Fréjus, 70; letter of Innocent to Exuperius, 8, title 2.

On those who persist in sins until the end of life and ask for communion at the point of death. In Martin’s excerpts, title 82, canon 64.

## TITLE XVII. On granting penance and the times for doing penance

[Col. 0050B]

Those converted during illness are to receive the laying on of hands. Council of Arles I, title 6, canon 21.

On those who have received penance among heretics, and how they are to be received by the Church. Council of Milevis, title 23, canon 19.

The periods of penance are to be determined according to the distinction among sins. Council of Carthage III, title 31, canon 14.

That the priest impose the laws of penance upon the penitent without respect of persons. Council of Carthage IV, title 74, canon 15.

On those asking for penance who afterward become mute or fall into madness. Council of Carthage IV, title 76, canon 15.

Penance must not be denied to clergy who desire it. Council of Orange, title 4, canon 27.

On those who suddenly become mute, that they may receive both baptism and penance. Council of Orange, title 12, canon [Col. 0050C] 27.

On those who lose their reason, that what belongs to piety may be conferred upon them. Council of the same [council], title 13.

That whoever asks for penance, if he becomes mute, should receive what he sought when this has been established either by signs or by reliable testimony. Letter of Leo to Theodore of Fréjus, 70.

How the older are to receive penance, which is not readily to be entrusted to younger persons; and that the viaticum must be denied to no one placed at the point of death. Council of Agde, title 15, canon 30.

That penance be granted to married persons with mutual consent. Council of Arles II, title 22, canon 22.

How penance is to be given with the shaving of the head and a change of clothing. Council of Toledo III, title 12, canon 48.

On those who fall into various sins, that communion be granted if they have done penance worthily. Council of Laodicea, title 2, canon 7.

That final penance is to be denied to no one. Letter of [Col. 0050D] Celestine to the bishops of Gaul, 34, title 2.

On the penance of the faithful: when they come to it, their confession is not to be made public. Letter of Leo to the bishops throughout Campania, Samnium, and Picenum, 73, title 2.

That penance be granted to those weighed down by illness or rendered mute, on the testimony of those who hear them. Letter of Leo to Theodore of Fréjus, 70.

That in general cases nothing ought to be investigated without the metropolitan, and that penance and communion not be denied to those at the point of death. For God’s forgiveness can be obtained only through the supplications of priests. Letter of Leo to Theodore of Fréjus, 70.

## TITLE XVIII. On the laws governing penitents

Negligent penitents are to be received more slowly. Council of Carthage IV, title 75, canon 15.

[Col. 0051A] Sick penitents are to receive the viaticum. Council of Carthage IV, title 77, canon 15.

Penitents who have received the viaticum, if they survive, must not consider themselves absolved without the laying on of hands. Council of Carthage IV, title 78, canon 15.

The offering and memory of deceased penitents are to be commended. Council of Carthage IV, title 79, canon 15.

At every time of fasting, the priest must lay hands upon penitents. In the same [source], title 80.

Penitents who have died are to be carried out and buried by the Church. In the same [source], title 82.

Penitents must do penance according to the measure of the ancient canons. Council of Toledo III, title 11, canon 48.
