That whoever asks forgiveness for illicit acts ought also to abstain from many licit ones; and that if penitents do not abandon their causes out of love for perfection, they must plead them before an ecclesiastical judge. Letter of Leo to Rusticus, 66, title 8.

[Col. 0051B] It is not fitting for a penitent to engage in any business profits. In the same [source], title 9.

After penance, it is altogether impermissible to return to secular military service. In the same [source], title 10.

## TITLE XIX. On the times for releasing penitents

On the time for releasing penitents. Letter of Innocent to Decentius, 6, title 7.

## TITLE XX. On penitents not to be received

On penitents: they are not to be received by other bishops or priests, nor communicate elsewhere except in their own church; and if anyone receives them, he incurs blame. Letter of Felix to the bishops throughout Sicily, 79, title 6.

A penitent must receive communion where he received penance. Council of Arles I, title 16, canon 21.

## TITLE XXI. On those who die while under penance

[Col. 0051C]

Those who die while under penance are to receive communion, and their offering is to be accepted. Council of Arles II, title 12, canon 22.

On penitents who die suddenly: their offerings are to be accepted. Council of Vaison I, title 2, canon 28.

[Col. 0052A] Unreconciled penitents who depart from the body are to receive the viaticum; and if they survive, they are to remain among the penitents. Council of Orange, title 3, canon 27.

## TITLE XXII. On the condemnation of penitents and those professing chastity who transgress

Apostates who return late are not to be received except through worthy penance. Council of Arles I, title 22, canon 21.

On those who apostatize after their holy profession of religion and return to the world, and on those who, after penance, presume to wear secular clothing. Council of Arles II, title 25, canon 22.

If, after receiving penance, anyone marries or lives in any kind of intimacy with an unrelated person. Council of the same [council], title 21.

On those who violate their penance. Council of Orléans I, title 7, canon 31.

[Col. 0052B] On adulterous penitents, if after doing penance they again commit fornication. Council of Elvira, title 7, canon 38.

On widows who violate the continence they have professed. Council of Carthage IV, title 104, canon 15.

On women who have professed widowhood before the bishop: if they transgress with a ravisher, they are to be condemned. Council of Orange, title 27, canon 27.

On those who have professed chastity, if they transgress. Council of the same [council], title 28.

On male and female penitents, including consecrated widows and virgins, who turn aside and become laypersons, change their clothing, or enter into marriage. Council of Toledo IV, title 55, canon 49.

On those who violate a widow, a penitent woman, or a religious virgin. Council of Lérida, title 6, canon 44.

On those who have not at all kept the penance they received: what condemnation or what aid they will have. Letter of Siricius to Eumerius, 3, title 5.

That if a young man has done penance under the pressure either of fear of death or of the danger of captivity, and does not maintain continence, he may be sustained by the remedy of a wife. Letter of Leo to Rusticus, 66, title 11.

On transgressing penitents. Council of Toledo VI, title 7, canon 51.

That for certain penitents their former marriages are restored. Council of Toledo VI, title 8, canon 51.

On those who receive penance without understanding it. Council of Toledo XII, title 2, canon 57.

# BOOK THREE. ON THE INSTITUTIONS OF JUDGMENTS AND THE GOVERNANCE OF AFFAIRS

[Col. 0051]

## VERSE COMPOSITION

[Col. 0051D]

**I.** After our tongue had subjected itself to your commands

and prepared its mind for service more quickly than the word was spoken,

in what direction shall we send the traveler wandering on his course,

or now on what revolving sphere shall we balance his return?

Has the sequence, with strenuous beginning, until now collapsed?

**R.** From this point begin to arrange juridical motions:

bend the mouth, throat, tongue, and lip of the accuser;

do not permit a false witness to live unpunished;

let the judge learn to pronounce a just judgment,

and let him not turn even the smallest part of the law toward favor.

For whoever twists the laws is twisted toward the fires,

[Col. 0052D] and great guilt has weighed even small deeds.

I have completed the precepts impressed in sacred words,

bringing to you whatever you yourself command.

Do you think the legs slip from the straight path,

or are we deceived by an alternating step?

Directly, the throat struck the unjust mind,

cutting through all cunning with the sword of justice.

The liar was rightly punished for his ill-omened crime,

so that what perishes through truth might not stand as falsehood.

The whole course has met truth with a truthful step.

Go on vigorously; no error lies hidden in the caves.

## TITLE I. On retaining the government undertaken and carrying it out diligently

[Col. 0051D]

That the rights of government once undertaken are not to be abandoned for any reason. Preface to Leo’s letter to Rusticus of Narbonne, 66.

That the rights of government must be diligently exercised. Preface to Leo’s letter to the bishops throughout Sicily, 63.

## TITLE II. On ecclesiastical certificates

[Col. 0053A]

How an ecclesiastical certificate is made. Letter of Atticus, bishop of Constantinople, which appears in full at the end of the Greek councils, chapter 11.

How an ecclesiastical certificate is made, and that no cleric may travel anywhere without one. Council of Milevis, title 20, canon 19.

## TITLE III. On the manner of travel for ministers

A minister of the altar, or even a layman, ought not to travel anywhere without an ecclesiastical certificate. Council of Laodicea, title 41, canon 7.

A minister of the altar or any cleric ought not to travel to foreign places except by order of his bishop. Council of the same [council], title 42, canon 7.

No stranger is to be received without a letter, that is, an ecclesiastical certificate. Council of Antioch, title 7, canon 6.

[Col. 0053B] Letters are to be granted to the needy; persons of higher standing, however, are to be approved by letters of recommendation. Council of Chalcedon, title 11, canon 11.

Those who carry letters from confessors are to receive other letters of communion. Council of Arles I, title 9, canon 21.

On the letters of communion belonging to confessors. Council of Elvira, title 25, canon 38.

On those who carry letters of communion: they are to be questioned concerning the faith. Council of the same [council], title 58.

On clerics who travel without letters from their bishop. Council of Agde, titles 38 and 52, canon 30.

Clergy or laypeople must not receive communion in another church without letters from their own bishop. Council of Carthage I, title 7, canon 12.

On governors or others wishing to conduct public business: they must not receive communion without letters from their own bishop, and if they act contrary to discipline, they are to be excommunicated. Council of Arles I, title 7, canon 21.

Foreign clerics ought not to minister without letters of recommendation. Council of Chalcedon, title 13, [Col. 0053C] canon 11.

## TITLE IV. On the manner of travel for priests

A bishop must not travel far without an ecclesiastical certificate from the metropolitan. Council of Carthage III, title 28, canon 14.

If a bishop goes to the imperial court without the ruler’s summons and without just causes, he is to be deprived of communion and of his dignity. Council of Sardica, title 11, canon 5.

On restraining bishops, so that they do not presume to go indiscriminately to the imperial court. Council of Sardica, title 12, canon 5.

On bishops, and on all who are placed under ecclesiastical rule, that no one go to the ruler without the counsel and letters of the metropolitan and of all the bishops who are in the same province. Council of Antioch, title 11, canon 6.

Bishops must not go indiscriminately to the imperial court unless summoned by the ruler; and this is how bishops are to obtain relief from the authorities for the oppressed, widows, orphans, and condemned persons. Council of Sardica, title 8, [Col. 0053D] canon 5.

How bishops, either personally or through their ministers, may pursue causes that justly belong to them whenever they wish. Council of the same [council], title 9, canon 5.

A bishop must not go to the imperial court except for just causes or to obtain relief for orphans, widows, or persons suffering. Council of the same [council], title 10, canon 5.

On neighboring bishops residing in the royal city. Council of Toledo VII, title 6, canon 52.

## TITLE V. On the crime of conspiracy

On confederacies and conspiracies, which the Greeks call *phratriae* (brotherhoods). Council of Chalcedon, title 18, canon 11.

## TITLE VI. On informers

On informers. Council of Elvira, title 73, canon 38.

## TITLE VII. On investigating the conduct of accusers

[Col. 0054A]

The conduct of the accuser and the accused must be investigated in court. Council of Carthage IV, title 96, canon 15.

## TITLE VIII. On rejecting accusers

Those who are not of good conduct must not accuse clerics; and if a cleric is implicated in crimes, he must not accuse clerics. Council of Carthage II, title 6, canon 12.

On persons who cannot accuse clerics. Council of Carthage VII, title 2, canon 18.

On excommunicated persons: while they remain under the same sentence, they must not accuse. Council of the same [council], title 1, canon 18.

Accusers who have failed to prove the first charge brought must not be admitted to bring further accusations. Council of Carthage VII, title 3, canon 18.

On those who have accused priests but do not prove the charge. [Col. 0054B] Council of Elvira, title 75, canon 38.

Whoever accuses a cleric and does not prove it is to be excommunicated. Council of Braga II, title 8, canon 64.

Clerical accusers of their brothers are not to be received into communion or into the clergy. Council of Carthage IV, title 55, canon 15.

False accusers of their brothers are to remain excommunicated until death. Council of Arles I, title 14, canon 21.

On accusers of their brothers. Council of Arles II, title 24, canon 22.

Accusers are not to be heard in trivial cases; in criminal cases, however, they are to be examined, with the bishop understanding that he himself is to be examined in the place of the accuser. Council of Vaison, title 7, canon 28.

If a bishop brings a charge against anyone, he must be brought to proof in a synod. Council of Carthage IV, title 29, canon 15.

One must not believe an accusing bishop alone: if, having accused someone by himself, he excommunicates the person who denies the charge, [Col. 0054C] he himself must not receive communion. Council of Carthage VII, title 5, canon 18.

## TITLE IX. On accepting accusers

On the kinds of persons who are to be admitted as accusers in accusations against bishops and clerics. Council of Chalcedon, title 21, canon 11.

No one is to be condemned without a legitimate accusation. Council of Toledo VI, title 11, canon 51.

## TITLE X. On examining witnesses

No one is to accept the testimony of a person who frequently litigates and is quick to accuse without serious examination. Council of Carthage IV, title 58, canon 15.

## TITLE XI. On not compelling persons to testify

On clerics: no ecclesiastical person is to be compelled to give testimony. Council of Carthage V, title 1, [Col. 0054D] canon 16.

## TITLE XII. On rejecting witnesses

On persons who cannot testify against clerics. Council of Carthage VII, title 4, canon 18.

On false witnesses. Council of Elvira, title 24, canon 38.

On converted Jews who afterward transgress: they are not to be admitted as witnesses. Council of Toledo IV, title 64, canon 49.

On one whom a bishop has presumed to excommunicate on the testimony of that person alone. Council of Carthage VII, title V, canon 18.

## TITLE XIII. On contempt of judgment

On accused persons unwilling to appear in court. Letter of Boniface to the bishops of Gaul, in full, 31.

## TITLE XIV. On initiating a trial

[Col. 0055A]

No bishop is to accept gifts in judicial proceedings. Council of Tarragona, title 10, canon 39.

A bishop is to hear cases in the presence of clerics. Council of Carthage IV, title 23, canon 15.

No bishop or subordinate cleric is to presume to hear cases on Sunday. Council of Tarragona, title 4, canon 39.

## TITLE XV. On seeking judicial decisions

On clerics, if they seek a secular or episcopal judgment from the ruler. Council of Milevis, title 19, canon 19.

If a cleric thinks that his bishop has treated him unjustly with disciplinary severity, he is to appeal to a synod. Council of Carthage IV, title 66, canon 15.

Clerics who have been unjustly excommunicated may approach neighboring bishops. Council of Sardica, title 17, canon 5.

[Col. 0055B] On clerics who complain about the judgments of their own bishops. Council of Milevis, title 22, canon 19.

Whoever does not accept the sentence of his bishop is to appeal to a synod. Council of Vaison, title 5, canon 28.

## TITLE XVI. On not abandoning ecclesiastical judgments

Catholics must not bring cases before unbelievers. Council of Carthage IV, title 87, canon 15.

Clerics ought not, bypassing the bishop, to go to secular courts; and if a cleric has a case against a foreign bishop, he is to complain before the synodal hearing of that bishop’s province. But if a bishop or cleric has a case against a bishop of his own province or against the metropolitan, he is to go to the bishops of the diocese. Council of Chalcedon, title 9, canon 11.

Clerics must not appeal at all to public courts; if they do so, they must either lose the case or be deprived of their dignity. Council of Carthage III, title 9, canon 14.

A cleric must not go to a secular judge without consulting his bishop. Council of Agde, title 32, canon 30.

Two clerics may not bring a case against each other in the public forum. Council of Toledo III, title 13, canon 48.

## TITLE XVII. On the selection of judges

If judges have been selected by agreement of the parties, it is not permissible for the number of judges to be smaller than the prescribed number. Council of Carthage III, title 10, canon 14.

## TITLE XVIII. On the number of judges

On contumacious clerics and the number of judges who may judge a bishop, priest, or deacon. Council of Carthage I, title 11, canon 12.

How many are required to judge a bishop, priest, or deacon. Council of Carthage II, title 10, chapter 13.

[Col. 0055D] On accused bishops and their accusers: where and within what period they are to be examined, and concerning the period of their purification and communion. Council of Carthage III, title 7, canon 14.

How many bishops are to examine priests or deacons; and that the same procedure is ordered to be preserved with the accusers in their cases and examinations. The cases of other clerics are to be heard and concluded by the bishop of the place alone. Council of Carthage III, title 8, canon 14.

Gallican bishops are not to be examined in Gaul. Council of Vaison, title I, canon 28.

Priests or deacons are not to be deposed by one bishop alone. Council of Seville II, title 6, canon 67.

## TITLE XIX. On doubtful judgments

On bishops or clerics condemned by a synod or by their own bishop: if they seek a review, they are to turn to a larger synod of bishops and are not to bring any complaint before the ruler. Council of Antioch, title 12, canon 6.

On accused bishops: if one party has judged him innocent and the other guilty, another metropolitan is to come with several bishops so that he may resolve the dispute. Council of Antioch, title 14, canon 6.

## TITLE XX. On differing judgments

If anyone passes from some ecclesiastical judges to others, this is not to prejudice the first judges if the latter issue a different sentence; it must nevertheless be investigated whether they have been corrupted by any unjust motive. Council of Carthage III, title 10, canon 14.

## TITLE XXI. On unjust judgments

A bishop’s sentence is invalid unless confirmed by the judgment of his clerics. Council of Carthage IV, title 23, canon 15.

[Col. 0056B] An unjust condemnation by bishops is invalid and must therefore be reconsidered by a synod. Council of the same [council], title 28, canon 15.

A sentence approved in the absence of the person whose case is being heard is invalid; those who have done this will answer for the case in a synod. Council of the same [council], title 30, canon 15.

## TITLE XXII. On uncertain judgments

On bishops who have received a sentence from all the bishops of the province, so that their judgment cannot be overturned. Council of Antioch, title 15, canon 6.

A bishop or any cleric who has been deposed may not minister, so that restoration may not be possible. Council of Antioch, title 4, canon 6.

On clerics condemned for their crime: they are not to be defended by anyone. Council of Carthage V, title 2, canon 16.

On excommunicated clerics: for how long they may be defended. Council of the same [council], title 12, canon 16.

## TITLE XXIII. On overturning and confirming judgments

[Col. 0056C]

On a bishop who has been judged: if the Roman bishop wishes, he may either renew or confirm the judgment. Council of Sardica, title 4, canon 5.

If a bishop has been deposed by a synod, no one is to be ordained in his see in any way unless the Roman bishop has determined his case. Council of the same [council], title 5, canon 5.

On cases of clerics, both of higher and lower rank, which are not at all settled in the province: they are to be determined by the Apostolic See. Letter of Innocent to Victoricus, 7, title 3.

That what had been secretly obtained from the Apostolic See was changed for the better when it rescinded the condemnation of Photinus. Letter of Innocent to Rufus, 26, title 7.

On the order in which the deposed are to be ordained again. Council of [Col. 0056D] Toledo IV, title 28, canon 49.

On accused bishops, so that their case may be concluded by the Roman bishop or by those whom he sends. Council of Sardica, title 7, canon 5.

If a bishop, priest, or deacon complains in a council that he has been unjustly excommunicated. In Martin’s excerpts, title 37, canon 64.

## TITLE XXIV. On contributions for the poor

Things contributed for the use of the poor must not be given outside the Church. Council of Gangra, title 8, canon 4.

## TITLE XXV. On those who oppress the poor and defraud the offerings of churches

The offerings of those who oppress the poor are not to be accepted. Council of Carthage IV, title 94, canon 15.

Those who either deny the offerings of the dead or return them only with difficulty are to be excommunicated. Council of the same [council], title 95.

Those who retain the offerings of the dead are to be excommunicated. Council of Vaison, title 4, canon 28.

On those who defraud the churches of their own offerings or those of their relatives. Council of Agde, title 4, canon 30.

If a penitent strips anyone of his possessions and does not return them after being admonished by the bishop, he is to be excommunicated. Council of Toledo I, title 11, canon 46.

## TITLE XXVI. On holding councils

A council of bishops is to be held twice a year. Council of Nicaea, title 5, canon 1.

A council ought to be held twice a year in each province. Council of Chalcedon, title 19, canon 11.

The acts of councils are to be strengthened by the signatures of the bishops. Council of Carthage III, title 50, canon 14.

[Col. 0057B] A synod is to be convened at the metropolitan’s direction. Council of Arles II, title 18, canon 22.

The metropolitan is to sign and send letters summoning a council. Council of Milevis, title 10, canon 19.

In common cases of the Church, a general council ought to be convened; in private cases, however, a special council of each province. Council of Milevis, title 9, canon 19.

On the character of councils, and why or when they are held. Council of Toledo IV, title 3, canon 49.

A bishop is to attend on the day of the council. Council of Carthage V, title 10, canon 16.

On the procedure according to which a council is to be held. Council of Toledo IV, title 6, canon 44.

A sick bishop is to send a delegate to the synod in his place. Council of Carthage IV, title 21, canon 15.

On the time of Easter and the day on which the council ought to be held. Council of Carthage V, title 7, canon 16.

On a synod to be convened every year. Council of Agde, title 71, canon 30.

[Col. 0057C] A council is to be held every year. Council of Carthage III, title 2, canon 14.

A council is to be held twice a year. Council of Régium, title 8, canon 26.

A synod is to be held twice a year. Council of Antioch, title 20, canon 6.

On holding a synod twice a year, and that no other bishop may hold a council in his own place except the metropolitan alone. In Martin’s excerpts, title 18, canon 64.

No bishop may be absent from a synod or depart before the synod has been completed. Council of Arles II, title 19, canon 22.

No bishop may leave a council without consent or excuse himself from attending a council. Council of Orange, title 29, canon 27.

Once a year priests, judges, and administrators of the fiscal patrimony ought to assemble at a council. Council of Toledo III, title 18, canon 48.

The bishop is to notify diocesan priests and certain [Col. 0057D] laypeople by letter to assemble at the synod. Council of Tarragona, title 13, canon 39.

Every three years, the bishops of Sicily are to attend at Rome for a synod on the third day before the Kalends of October. Letter of Leo to the bishops throughout Sicily, 63, title 7.

Two councils of bishops are to be held each year. Letter of Leo to Anastasius, 67, title 6.

Two bishops from each province, whom the metropolitans have approved, are to be sent to Thessalonica. 67, title 9.

The bishops are not to remain at the council for more than fifteen days. Letter of the same [Leo] to the same [Anastasius], 67, title 10.

On holding a council every year. Letter of Hormisdas to the bishops throughout Spain, 91, title 3.

On bishops who, after the acts had been completed in the synod of Carthage, were detained to carry out the remaining business. Council of Milevis, title 27, canon 19.

## TITLE XXVII. On bishops who disdain to attend a synod

[Col. 0058A]

Bishops summoned to a synod must not disdain to attend. Council of Laodicea, title 40, canon 7.

Those who, disdaining their people, refuse to come to a council are to lose both their people and their honor. Council of Carthage III, title 43, canon 14.

No bishop may leave a council without consent or excuse himself from attending a council. Council of Orange, title 29, canon 27.

If a bishop, after being admonished by the metropolitan to attend a synod or an episcopal ordination, delays coming. Council of Agde, title 53, canon 30.

A bishop who, after being warned by the metropolitan, does not come to the synod is to be excommunicated. Council of Tarragona, title 6, canon 39.

On a bishop who is unwilling to come to a synod. In Martin’s excerpts, title 19, canon 64.

## TITLE XXVIII. On preserving the agreements of bishops, to be confirmed by the ruler

[Col. 0058B]

The acts of the council are to be confirmed by the signatures of the bishops. Council of Carthage III, title 50, canon 14.

Agreements made between bishops are to be preserved. Council of Carthage I, title 12, canon 12.

A bishop who acts contrary to his profession made in council is to be deposed. Council of Carthage II, title 13, canon 13.

Whatever is decreed in a council concerning heretics or unbelievers is to be obtained from the ruler. Council of Milevis, title 11, canon 19.

## TITLE XXIX. On excommunicated persons

On excommunicated clerics or laypeople. Council of Nicaea, [Col. 0058C] title 5, canon 1.

On excommunicated clerics: other bishops must not receive communion with them. Council of Sardica, title 16, canon 5.

What is to be observed concerning excommunicated persons. Council of Antioch, title 6, canon 6.

On excommunicated persons who come to the royal city against the will of the bishop. Council of Chalcedon, title 23, canon 11.

Whoever receives another person’s excommunicated member is to be excommunicated and held liable to the same offense. Council of Carthage II, title 7, canon 13.

If an excommunicated priest presumes to celebrate the sacrifice, he is to be anathematized. Council of the same [council], title 8.

On excommunicated clerics and monks who come to the royal city against the will of their bishop. Council of Chalcedon, title 23, canon 11.

That one who communicates or prays with an excommunicated person is to be excommunicated. Fourth Council of Carthage, title 73, canon 15.

Concerning those who receive persons excommunicated by another. Second Council of Arles, title 8, canon 22.

[Col. 0058D] Concerning clerics who, through their own fault, are excommunicated by their bishop: that they are by no means to receive communion from other bishops. Council of Agde, title 3, canon 30.

That an excommunicated person should humble himself, so that he may be reconciled more quickly. Council of Vaison, title C, canon 28.

Concerning one who makes some claim against his bishop: he is not to be deprived of the Church on account of that very suit. First Council of Orléans, title 4, canon 31.

Concerning excommunicated presbyters: that in necessity they may give communion. Council of Elvira, title 32, canon 38.

Concerning bishops who communicate with another's excommunicated person. Same council, title 53.

That those deprived by their own bishops are not to be received by others. First Council of Saragossa, title 5, canon 41.

Concerning those excommunicated by priests: that no one approach them. First Council of Toledo, title 15, canon 46.

Concerning not communicating with excommunicated persons. First Council of Braga, title 15, canon 63.

[Col. 0059A] Concerning excommunicated clerics. In Martin's excerpts, title 37, canon 64.

That it is not permitted to communicate with excommunicated persons. In Martin's excerpts, title 84, canon 64.

Concerning those who, not communicating in their own province, communicate elsewhere. Council of Milevis, title 18, canon 19.

If any cleric or layman has willingly been excommunicated for heresy, let him present a statement of his faith, so that he may clear himself of the suspicion of heresy. In Martin's excerpts, title 36, canon 64.

Concerning the condemnation of Acacius because he dared to communicate with heretics. Felix's letter in full to the same Acacius of Constantinople, 80.

Concerning bishops who receive another's excommunicated person. Council of Orange, title 11, canon 27.

TITLE XXX. Concerning excommunicated persons.

Concerning excommunicated persons departing this life. Council of Nicaea, [Col. 0059B] title 12, canon 1.

Concerning those deprived of communion and so deceased. Leo's letter to Rusticus, 66, title 6.

TITLE XXXI. Concerning preserving the integrity of jurisdictions.

Let a people that has always been subject to a diocese not receive another bishop. Third Council of Carthage, title 42, canon 14.

That a diocese which has never had a bishop is not to have one. Second Council of Carthage, title 5, canon 13.

That he who proves that his city was a metropolis is to retain the primacy. Council of Turin, title 1, canon 25.

That there are not to be two metropolitans in one province, and concerning cases in which this has occurred. Council of Chalcedon, title 12, canon 11.

That, according to the imperial statutes, there ought not to be two metropolitan bishops. Innocent's letter to Alexander, 23, title 2.

That every province ought to be content with its own metropolitan. Celestine's letter to the bishops [Col. 0059C] of Gaul, 34, title 4.

Concerning boundaries not to be transferred. Innocent's letter in full to Florentinus, 13.

That no bishop, having abandoned his see, reside in a diocese. Fifth Council of Carthage, title 5, canon 16.

A bishop established in a diocese is to retain only the people in which he was ordained. Third Council of Carthage, title 46, canon 14.

If bishops are negligent against heretics, let them lose the very places in which they are found to be negligent; also concerning judges by whom the case may be decided. Council of Milevis, title 24, canon 19.

That if a bishop, summoned by neighboring bishops in the principal sees, has not converted them to the unity of the Church within six months, he be excommunicated; and if a bishop has lied about being in communion, he be deprived. Same council, title 25.

TITLE XXXII. Concerning usurped sees and places.

[Col. 0059D]

Concerning bishops occupying vacant churches while their own churches are vacant, and that a synod is complete when the metropolitan is present. Council of Antioch, title 16, canon 6.

Let no bishop usurp the peoples or boundaries of another bishop. First Council of Carthage, title 10, canon 12.

That no one presume to take another's parish. Second Council of Carthage, title 11, canon 13.

That one bishop not usurp another's peoples. Third Council of Carthage, title 20, canon 14.

Concerning bishops who, without awaiting a synod, have seized what they could have reclaimed. Council of Milevis, title 21, canon 19.

TITLE XXXIII. Concerning governing churches by thirty years' possession.

Concerning churches situated in barbarian territory. First Council of Constantinople, title 4, canon 8.

Concerning churches in parishes possessed by a [Col. 0060A] bishop for thirty years, or newly restored cities. Council of Chalcedon, title 17, canon 11.

Concerning the period of thirty years and the distinction of cases because of provinces. Fourth Council of Toledo, title 34, canon 49.

Concerning the thirty-year limitation: after thirty years no one may appeal concerning that which the legal period has excluded. Gelasius's letter to the Sicilian bishops, 83, title 2.

That basilicas remain under the authority of the bishop in whose territory they are. First Council of Orléans, title 13, canon 31.

Concerning churches transferred from heresy: that they belong to the bishops in whose parishes they are. Third Council of Toledo, title 9, canon 48.

That the endowments of all churches ought to belong to the bishop's administration. Third Council of Toledo, title 19, canon 48.

Concerning the assembly of a territory and newly constructed basilicas: to which bishop they belong. Fourth Council of Toledo, [Col. 0060B] title 35, canon 49.

TITLE XXXIV. Concerning visiting and regulating parishes.

That each year bishops visit their dioceses, and that they receive no more than a third from their parishes. Council of Tarragona, title 8, canon 39.

Concerning the annual visitation to be performed by bishops in the parishes. Fourth Council of Toledo, title 36, canon 49.

That priests ought to act moderately in parishes. Third Council of Toledo, title 20, canon 48.

That a bishop take nothing from the property of churches except a third of the offerings and produce. Fourth Council of Toledo, title 33, canon 49.

That a bishop travel through his diocese. Second Council of Braga, title 1, canon 64.

That a bishop travelling through his diocese receive only two solidi, not demand a third share of offerings, and that clerics not be compelled in a servile manner. Same council, title 2, [Col. 0060C] canon 64.

That a bishop travel through his diocese, examining whether clerics serve well; and that catechumens be taught the Creed twenty days before Easter. Second Council of Braga, title 1, canon 64.

Concerning exemption of the churches of the province of Gaul. Seventh Council of Toledo, title 4, canon 52.

TITLE XXXV. If a dispute arises between parishes, by what examination it is to be decided.

Concerning the complaints of Theodulf, bishop of the church of Málaga, against the other bishops concerning certain parishes. Second Council of Seville, title 1, canon 67.

Concerning the complaints of bishops Fulgentius and Honorius concerning certain parishes. Same council, title 2.

Concerning two bishops of one province having a dispute with one another. Council of Sardica, title 3, canon 5.

TITLE XXXVI. Concerning the steward and defenders of the Church.

[Col. 0060D]

Concerning the appointment of stewards, that is, administrators, for individual churches. Council of Chalcedon, title 26, canon 11.

Concerning the appointment of stewards, that is, those who manage ecclesiastical property. Fourth Council of Toledo, title 48, canon 49.

Concerning stewards: that they not be appointed from laymen. Second Council of Seville, title 9, canon 67.

That defenders of churches be sought from the prince. Fifth Council of Carthage, title 9, canon 16.

That executors or advocates be sought from the prince for cases of the Church. Council of Milevis, title 16, canon 19.

That founders of churches, while they live, have their care and themselves choose ministers to serve there. Ninth Council of Toledo, title 2, canon 54.

TITLE XXXVII. Concerning administration of ecclesiastical property.

That the offering of the faithful made in money be kept with [Col. 0061A] each cleric, to be divided among the clerics at a suitable time. First Council of Braga, title 21, canon 63.

Concerning things offered to the altar, whether estates. First Council of Orléans, title 10, canon 31.

Concerning things offered by the faithful in parish basilicas. Same council, title 11.

Concerning ecclesiastical property: how many shares are to be made. First Council of Braga, title 7, canon 63.

Concerning administering church property: that such administration be carried out so that no need remains. In Martin's excerpts, title 16, canon 64.

That four shares ought to be made from the revenues of the church and the offerings of the faithful. General decree of Gelasius, 82, title 29.

Concerning bishops' good management of church property. Gelasius's letter to the Sicilian bishops, 83, title 1.

Concerning acquired property: what division is to be made between the Church and the intestate heirs of a priest. Ninth Council of Toledo, [Col. 0061B] title 4, canon 54.

That a bishop may confer upon whom he chooses the third part of ecclesiastical property due to him. Ninth Council of Toledo, title 6, canon 54.

TITLE XXXVIII. Concerning the custody and alienation of church property.

Concerning property bestowed on churches: that it continue under their right. Sixth Council of Toledo, title 15, canon 51.

That priests ought not to sell ecclesiastical property, but that what has been sold be recovered. Council of Ancyra, title 15, canon 2.

That any alienation carried out by a bishop without the consent of the clerics is invalid. Fourth Council of Carthage, title 32, canon 15.

Church property is not to be alienated by a bishop without consulting the metropolitan. Fifth Council of Carthage, title 4, canon 16.

That bishops may not alienate church property, but may give it for use to clerics, monks, and strangers. Third Council of Toledo, title 3, canon 48.

[Col. 0061C] That it is not permitted to a presbyter or cleric to sell or donate church property. Council of Agde, title 22, canon 30.

That it is not permitted to all ministers and priests to exchange, sell, or donate church property, nor for freedmen produced from parish households to leave the church. Council of Agde, title 49, canon 30.

That parish presbyters may not sell anything from church property. Same council, title 53.

That whatever parish presbyters purchase they draw up the deed in the church's name. Same council, title 54.

A bishop is to have authority over church property and not assign authority over it to members of his household or relatives. Council of Antioch, title 25, canon 6.

A bishop is to use church property as entrusted, not as his own. Fourth Council of Carthage, title 31, canon 15.

How church property is to be held by bishops, and concerning the manumission of freedmen. Council of Agde, title 7, canon 30.

[Col. 0061D] That a bishop may, without the consent of the clerics, sell something of small value. Same council, title 45.

That a bishop may sell fugitive slaves of the church. Same council, title 46.

Concerning slaves of the church manumitted by a bishop. First Council of Seville, title 1, canon 66.

Concerning insolent freedmen of the church: that they be recalled to service. Second Council of Seville, title 8, canon 67.

Concerning slaves of the church bestowed by bishops upon their relatives. First Council of Seville, title 2, canon 66.

If a bishop has bestowed anything from church property by testament. Council of Agde, title 51, canon 30.

Concerning a presumptuous bishop: if, without necessity and without the knowledge of the clergy, or from a place where there is no presbyter, he presumes to sell anything of church property. In Martin's excerpts, title 14, canon 64.

That clerics may not plunder property belonging to their bishop after his death. Council of Chalcedon, title 22, canon 11.

[Col. 0062A] That if a bishop dies intestate, the clerics make an inventory of his property and no one take anything from it. Council of Tarragona, title 12, canon 39.

If a priest dies, what is to be observed concerning church property. Council of Lleida, title 16, canon 44.

That when a bishop has died, no one presume anything concerning his property or that of the church. Council of Valence, title 2, canon 45.

Concerning ecclesiastical and episcopal property: how they are to be kept separately. Council of Antioch, title 24, canon 6.

Concerning the administration of church property and the separation of temporal property from spiritual matters. In Martin's excerpts, title 15, canon 64.

That relatives of a dying bishop usurp nothing from his property without the knowledge of the metropolitan and fellow-provincial bishops. Council of Valence, title 3, canon 45.

Concerning what ought to be observed regarding a bishop's own or acquired property. Council of Agde, title 48, canon 30.

If anything has been left to a bishop by anyone, it is to be claimed by the church, except things found to have been given by a trust [Col. 0062B] bequest. Same council, title 6.

That if a bishop, whether leaving children or not, has not made the church over which he presided his heir, the losses of the church be made good from the goods he left. Same council, title 33.

Concerning sales which abbots presume to make, and concerning freedmen from monasteries who were slaves: that these are in no way to be made. Same council, title 56.

Concerning payment to priests, from church property, of the promised support granted to them, that it may thus be confirmed by a council. Fourth Council of Toledo, title 37, canon 49.

If anything is said to be given from church property as a grant, the ground of the grant is to be examined. Ninth Council of Toledo, title 3, canon 54.

Concerning support to be allotted from property bestowed by them to founders of churches or their children. Fourth Council of Toledo, title 38, canon 49.

Church property bestowed for use is not to be defended by any prescription of time. Council of Agde, title 59, canon 30.

[Col. 0062C] If a bishop has granted anyone small parcels of land to cultivate, they are to be held without prejudice to the church's right. First Council of Orléans, title 19, canon 31.

That whatever clerics have held from the right of the church return to the church after their death. Second Council of Toledo, title 4, canon 47.

That church property not be alienated and be given for use to clerics, monks, or strangers. Symmachus's letter to Caesarius, 35, title 1.

Concerning clerics' stipends: that they not be alienated from the church's right. Sixth Council of Toledo, title 5, canon 51.

That bishops take nothing from church property, and how near relatives who are founders of churches are to exercise care. Ninth Council of Toledo, title 1, canon 54.

That documents which priests and ministers have unjustly made have their years counted after their death. Same council, title 8.

TITLE XXXIX. Concerning freedmen and households of churches.

[Col. 0062D]

Concerning freedmen made from the household of the church: if the priests who make them free contribute nothing from their own property. Fourth Council of Toledo, title 67, canon 49.

Concerning the distinction among those manumitted from the household of the church, how they are to be manumitted, and that they not give adverse testimony or accusations. Same council, title 68.

That freedmen may be made from the household of the church by bishops in compensation for property acquired. Same council, title 69.

Concerning the declaration to be made to priests by church freedmen and their descendants, lest length of time cause them to resist freedom. Same council, title 70.

Concerning church freedmen abandoning its protection. Same council, title 74.

Concerning declarations and obedience of church freedmen. Sixth Council of Toledo, title 9, canon 51.

Concerning the offspring of church freedmen: that they may not, even for [Col. 0063A] their maintenance, wander away from the church. Sixth Council of Toledo, title 10, canon 51.

That after a priest's death the term of years is to be counted in the freedom bestowed upon slaves. Ninth Council of Toledo, title 12, canon 54.

That those born of church freedmen and freeborn persons not withdraw from services owed to the church. Same council, title 13.

That if church freedmen are unwilling to return to it, all their little property be assigned to the church's right. Same council, title 14.

Concerning the service and discipline of church freedmen. Same council, title 15.

That church freedmen may transfer none of their property into another's ownership. Same council, title 16.

TITLE XL. Concerning not being ignorant of the canons.

[Col. 0063B] That no priest may be ignorant of the canons. Celestine's letter through Apulia, 35, title 1.

That ignorance of the holy Scriptures made Eutyches a heretic. Leo's letter to Flavian, 38, title 1.

That they know how to observe what they know and take care to know what they do not know. General decree of Gelasius, 82, title 18.

TITLE XLI. Concerning the preservation of canons and the condemnation of those who presume what is forbidden.

Concerning preserving canonical enactments. Leo's letter to the African bishops, 69, title 5.

That the Nicene canons and decrees of the apostolic see be observed. Hilary's decree, 74, title 1.

Concerning ecclesiastical institutions moderately arranged according to the condition of the times. Gelasius's decree, 82, title 1.

That, where no necessity presses, the enactments of the fathers be kept inviolate. In the work cited above, title 2.

[Col. 0063C] That the apostolic see with pious and devoted zeal preserves the canons of the fathers and commands that they be preserved with like purpose. General decree of Gelasius, 82, title 2.

That a bishop, presbyter, or deacon who acts contrary to these enactments incur penalty. General decree of Gelasius, 82, title 30.

That transgressors of prohibitions concerning communion know that they incur forfeiture. Symmachus's letter to Caesarius, 85, title 5.

That in the earlier rules both what must be observed and what is forbidden have been established, and ought in every respect to be diligently observed. Hormisdas's letter to Sallustius of Seville, 94.

That no one overturn ancient privileges, but that the enactments decreed by the fathers be preserved in their honor. Hormisdas's rescript in full to the bishops of Baetica, 95.

Concerning the condemnation of those who presume to usurp what has been forbidden. Zosimus's letter to Hesychius, bishop of Salona, 38, title 2.

[Col. 0063D] That the people ought to be taught. Celestine's letter through Apulia, 35, title 3.

That if any priest acts contrary to prohibitions, he be removed from [Col. 0064A] his office. Leo's letter to all bishops throughout Campania and various provinces, 64, title 5.

He who violates the ordinances will find the sentence against himself. Hilary's synodal decree, 74, title 4.

That bishops who act contrary to enactments be deprived of their rank. Council of Turin, title 12, canon 25.

Concerning Aggarus and Tiberianus, who were ordained from the laity. Leo's letter to the African bishops, 69, title 3.

Concerning the condemnation of those who pass over enactments and introduce new precepts. Decision at the end of the Council of Gangra, canon 4.

Concerning preserving the canons of each council. Council of Chalcedon, title 1, canon 11.

Concerning observance of the earlier canons. Third Council of Toledo, title 1, canon 48.

Concerning the stability of canons and the condemnation of violators. First Council of Braga, title 22, canon 63.

[Col. 0064B] That laymen who despise the canons be excommunicated and clerics deprived of rank. First Council of Carthage, title 14, canon 12.

Concerning Proterius, bishop of Alexandria: that he preserve the decrees of his predecessors. Leo's letter to the emperor Marcian, 58, title 1.

Where he asks the same emperor to send to the church of Alexandria, translated into Greek, the letter he had sent to Flavian, bishop of Constantinople. In the work cited above, title 2.

Where through his legates he exhorts the priests of God to order all things according to the holy Scriptures. Leo's letter in full to the Synod of Chalcedon, 54.

TITLE XLII. Concerning questions not to be despised and disputes to be avoided.

Deeper questions are not to be despised, nor yet asserted categorically. Celestine's letter to the bishops [Col. 0064C] of Gaul, 33, title 73.

That contention is especially to be avoided. Letter to Anastasius, 84, title 4.

TITLE XLIII. Concerning restoring the status of slaves.

That slaves are not to be received or claimed in monasteries or among the clergy under the pretext of religion. General decree of Gelasius, 82, title 16.

TITLE XLIV. Concerning all freedmen commended to the Church.

Concerning freedmen commended to the Church: that they not be oppressed. Council of Orange, title 7, canon 27.

Concerning freedmen: that in necessity they be protected by the Church. Council of Agde, title 29, canon 30.

That freedmen made by bishops or others and commended to the Church ought to remain free. Third Council of [Col. 0064D] Toledo, title 6, canon 48.

Concerning freedmen commended to the Church's patronage. Fourth Council of Toledo, title 72, canon 49.

BOOK FOUR. CONCERNING THE INSTITUTIONS OF OFFICES AND THE ORDER OF BAPTIZING.

[Col. 0063]

VERSE DIALOGUE.

[Col. 0063D] I. Behold, bearing the gifts of continual motion to please,

I have fulfilled with bowed mind all that you ordain:

What path henceforth will be laid beneath our feet,

Or whither shall we eagerly direct our course over the plains?

Thus far the tongue has run in a fixed

[Col. 0064D] order of words; now arrange choirs with responsive hymns;

Teach that baptism removes the stains of sin;

Distinguish altars, songs, and incense in the churches.

R. Swiftly summoned, I shall hasten to fulfil your commands

[Col. 0065A] and bear your sacred orders to proud minds:

The altar's sanctuary, the rites and songs of the temple,

the joys of feasts and the melody of preaching,

the customs, measures, laws, and places of sacred things—

the pen has fittingly set these out in distinct movements.

Do you think that you are made glad by these our labors?

Or what profit do we give that pleases you?

[Col. 0066A] I. Whatever you prepare refreshes me; such things delight me,

rejoicing in the riches which you place before me.

R. May the Lord grant that this our work can please you,

so that it may delight you and be able to refresh us.

TITLE I. That they harm only themselves when good things are administered by the wicked.

[Col. 0065A]

That the wicked, by administering good things, harm only themselves and do not defile the sacraments of the Church. Anastasius's letter to the emperor Anastasius, 84, title 8.

That no share of harm touches those whom Acacius baptized or ordained after his own condemnation. [Col. 0065B] In the work cited above, title 7.

TITLE II. Concerning not usurping teaching and the name of teacher.

That one to whom it has not been granted not assume the title of teacher. First Council of Saragossa, title 7, canon 41.

That a layman not teach in the presence of clerics. Fourth Council of Carthage, title 98, canon 15.

That women not presume to teach publicly. Fourth Council of Carthage, title 99, canon 15.

TITLE III. Concerning receiving canonical books and rejecting apocryphal books and psalms.

That psalms composed by unlearned persons may not be sung in church, nor books outside the canon be read; and which books are canonical. Council of Laodicea, title 59, canon 7.

That, apart from the holy Scriptures, nothing be read in church under the name of divine Scriptures; and which books are canonical. Council of Carthage, title 47, canon 14.

[Col. 0065C] Apart from canonical Scriptures, nothing is to be read in the catholic church; nothing is to be received as authoritative. First Council of Toledo, from the rule of faith, title 12, canon 46.

That outside the authority of the Old and New Testament nothing poetic is to be sung in church. First Council of Braga, title 12, canon 63.

Concerning the fact that it is not permitted to sing poetic psalms in church or read apocryphal books. In Martin's excerpts, title 67, canon 64.

Concerning receiving the book of Revelation everywhere. Fourth Council of Toledo, title 17, canon 49.

Concerning which canonical books ought to be received. Innocent's letter to Exsuperius, 8, title 7.

Concerning the canonical books that ought to be received and apocryphal books to be rejected. Decretal issued by Pope Hormisdas, 103.

TITLE IV. Concerning the creeds of the fathers.

[Col. 0065D] Creed of the Council of Nicaea, canon 1; and the faith of Saint Gregory the Great at the end of the capitulations.

Creed of the Council of Constantinople. At the end of canon 8.

Rule of faith adopted at the First Council of Toledo, canon 46, at the end of the capitulations.

Treatise and confession of faith of King Reccared, when the Gothic people was converted from the Arian heresy. Opening of the Third Council of Toledo, canon 48.

Concerning the manifest truth of the catholic faith. Fourth Council of Toledo, title 1, canon 49.

Concerning the fullness of the catholic faith. Sixth Council of Toledo, title 1, canon 51.

Concerning the truth of the one holy faith. Eighth Council of Toledo, title 1, canon 53.

TITLE V. Concerning preserving the creeds.

That the faith of the three hundred and eighteen fathers be preserved. First Council of Constantinople, title 1, canon 8.

TITLE VI. Concerning preaching the Creed.

[Col. 0066A]

Concerning preaching the Creed to the people in church. Third Council of Toledo, title 2, canon 48.

That the Creed be preached to the candidates eight days before Easter. Council of Agde, title 13, canon 30.

TITLE VII. Concerning constructing churches and altars.

[Col. 0066B] That new basilicas not be dedicated without the bishop's authorization. General decree of Gelasius, 82, title 6.

That no basilica built in the name of any deceased persons be dedicated. General decree of Gelasius, 82, title 27.

Concerning basilicas dedicated without relics of martyrs: that they be destroyed. Fifth Council of Carthage, title 15, canon 16.

That pictures not be made in a church. Council of Elvira, title 36, canon 38.

That it remain established if slaves of the fisc have made churches and enriched them from their own peculium. Third Council of Toledo, title 15, canon 48.

That an altar be both anointed and blessed. Council of Agde, title 14, canon 30.

Concerning what is to be observed in the restoration of churches in their structures or in building. Vigilius's letter to Bishop Profuturus, 96, title 4.

TITLE VIII. Concerning the honor of churches.

[Col. 0066C]

That God's gift and the assemblies held in it ought not to be despised. Council of Gangra, title 5, canon 4.

That it is not permitted to hold assemblies outside the church or, despising the bishop, to act with a presbyter. Same council, title 6.

That it is not permitted to despise the communion of the Church or communicate with excommunicated persons. Council of Antioch, title 2, canon 6.

Concerning produce to be given in church and not elsewhere. Council of Gangra, title 7, canon 4.

That it is not permitted to spread couches or hold an agape in churches of the Lord. Council of Laodicea, title 28, canon 7.

That no one hold a banquet in church. Third Council of Carthage, title 30, canon 14.

TITLE IX. Concerning the honor of martyrs.

[Col. 0066D] Concerning communicating in basilicas of martyrs. Council of Gangra, title 20, canon 4.

Concerning the tombs of martyrs and their honor. First Council of Carthage, title 2, canon 12.

That candles not be lit in cemeteries. Council of Elvira, title 34, canon 38.

TITLE X. Concerning the consecration of sacred offerings.

That only bread and a chalice be offered in the sacrifice. Third Council of Carthage, title 24, canon 14.

That nothing may be offered at the altar except bread, wine, and water. In Martin's excerpts, title 55, canon 64.

That the sacrament be consecrated upon one offering. Council of Orange, title 17, canon 27.

TITLE XI. Concerning the honor of sacred offerings.

That the sacrifice be performed by persons fasting. Words of bishops Honoratus and [Col. 0067A] Urbanus in the Third Council of Carthage, title 39, canon 14.

That Mass be celebrated by persons fasting. Same council, title 29.

That a presbyter not celebrate Mass for the dead after eating. Second Council of Braga, title 10, canon 64.

Offerings ought not to be made in houses by bishops or presbyters. Council of Laodicea, title 59, canon 7.

Concerning the fact that it is not permitted to celebrate Masses over tombs or in the open country, or distribute the sacraments. In Martin's excerpts, title 68, canon 64.

That sacred offerings for eulogiae at the Paschal feast not be sent to other parishes. Council of Laodicea, title 14, canon 7.

That baptism or Eucharist not be given to the dead. Third Council of Carthage, title 6, canon 14.

Concerning rejecting the offerings of those who do not communicate. Council of Elvira, title 28, canon 38.

Concerning those who enter church and do not communicate: [Col. 0067B] that they be excommunicated. First Council of Toledo, title 13, canon 46.

That one who receives the Eucharist in church and does not consume it there be anathematized. First Council of Saragossa, title 1, canon 41.

That one who has received the Eucharist and has not consumed it be rejected as sacrilegious. First Council of Toledo, title 14, canon 46.

Concerning the fact that it is not permitted to make banquets from offerings brought together. In Martin's excerpts, title 61, canon 64.

Concerning the fermentum, which is to be sent on Sunday only to the presbyters of the city. Innocent's letter to Decentius, 6, title 5.

Concerning feasts: if one celebration does not suffice for the people, there is to be no hesitation in repeating the sacrifice. Leo's letter to Dioscorus, 72, title 2.

Concerning illness occurring to ministering clerics. Seventh Council of Toledo, title 2, canon 52.

TITLE XII. Concerning position and access in the choir.

[Col. 0067C]

Concerning the distinction of presbyters and deacons: that they stand in their respective choirs. Fourth Council of Toledo, title 39, canon 49.

Concerning the fact that neither laymen nor women are permitted to communicate within the altar-rail. First Council of Braga, title 13, canon 63.

TITLE XIII. Concerning uniformity of offices.

That every province observe one order in the office. Council of Girona, title 1, 40.

Concerning one order to be celebrated in ministries and offices in all churches. Fourth Council of Toledo, title 2, canon 49.

Concerning one order to be celebrated in evening and morning offices in all churches. First Council of Braga, title 1, canon 63.

TITLE XIV. Concerning the order of offices.

[Col. 0067D]

That psalms may not be confused by being scattered about. Council of Laodicea, title 17, canon 7.

That nothing other than “Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit” be said. Vigilius's letter to Profuturus, 96, title 2.

That at the end of psalms “Glory and honor to God” be said. Fourth Council of Toledo, title 15, canon 49.

Concerning the distinction of the gloria at the end of responsories. Same council, title 16.

That prayers be said after antiphons, and that morning and evening hymns be sung with brief psalm verses. Council of Agde, title 30, canon 30.

Concerning not refusing to recite hymns. Fourth Council of Toledo, title 13, canon 49.

Concerning celebrating the office on the Friday of Easter. Fourth Council of Toledo, title 7, canon 49.

Concerning blessing the candle and lamp in the Easter vigil. Same council, title 8.

TITLE XV. Concerning prayers and the celebration of Masses.

[Col. 0068A]

Concerning daily prayers. Council of Laodicea, title 18, canon 7.

That petitions or prayers not be said unless they have been approved in a council. Council of Milevis, title 12, canon 19.

That the Lord's Prayer be said every day at the morning and evening hours. Council of Girona, title 11, canon 40.

Concerning the Lord's Prayer to be pronounced publicly every day. Fourth Council of Toledo, title 10, canon 49.

That presbyters ought to greet the people no differently from bishops, saying, “The Lord be with you.” First Council of Braga, title 3, canon 63.

Concerning not reading diverse lessons during the vigils or Masses of solemn days. First Council of Braga, title 2, canon 63.

Concerning singing the hymn of the three youths in all solemnities of Mass. Fourth Council of Toledo, title 14, [Col. 0068B] canon 49.

That the holy Gospel be read also on Saturdays. Council of Laodicea, title 16, canon 7.

That the Gospel be read after the epistle. Council of Valence, title 1, canon 45.

That the praises be said not immediately after the Apostle but after the Gospel. Fourth Council of Toledo, title 12, canon 49.

Concerning not singing Alleluia in Lent. Council of Toledo, title 11, canon 49.

That, according to the order of Mass received from the apostolic see by Metropolitan Bishop Profuturus, it ought to be celebrated. First Council of Braga, title 4, canon 63.

Concerning the order of the prayers of catechumens and faithful at the time of Mass, and concerning their communion. Council of Laodicea, title 19, canon 7.

Concerning the petitions and prayers of Mass, what order is to be observed in them, and that they are never to be brought forth without the consultation of the brethren. Third Council of Carthage, title [Col. 0068C] 23, canon 14.

Concerning giving the kiss of peace after the mysteries have been completed. Innocent's letter to Decentius, 6, title 1.

Concerning the names of offerers not to be recited before the priest's prayer. Innocent's letter to Decentius, 6, title 2.

Concerning the announcement of Easter, the order of prayers, and the solemnity of Masses. Vigilius's letter to Profuturus, 96, title 5.

That priests ought to communicate only after the blessing has been given to the people. Fourth Council of Toledo, title 18, canon 49.

That, because of the enactments of the apostolic see, all prayers of the Church resound with the grace of Christ, by which the human race is restored. Celestine's letter to the bishops of Gaul, 33, title 11.

That he acts as Christ's ambassador while praying for the peace of the Church. Anastasius's letter to Emperor Anastasius, 84, title 1.

TITLE XVI. Concerning the honor of Masses.

[Col. 0068D]

That vallematiae [uncertain term] and shameful songs be forbidden from sacred solemnities. Third Council of Toledo, title 23, canon 48.

That when a priest delivers an address, one who leaves the audience be excommunicated. Fourth Council of Carthage, title 24, canon 15.

That before Mass has been completed and the blessing received, none of the faithful or of the people depart or presume to leave. Council of Agde, title 47, canon 30.

That a bishop not presume to leave before Mass has been completed and the blessing received. First Council of Orléans, title 22, canon 31.

That one ought not to fast on Sunday. Council of Gangra, title 18, canon 4.

That no one fast on Sundays. First Council of Saragossa, title 2, canon 41.

[Col. 0069A] Concerning Sundays and Pentecost: that on them we pray standing. Council of Nicaea, title 20, canon 1.

Concerning not fasting on Sundays or bending the knee; likewise in the fifty days. In Martin's excerpts, title 57, canon 64.

TITLE XVII. Concerning litanies.

That litanies be celebrated after Pentecost from Thursday until Saturday. Council of Girona, title 2, canon 40.

That litanies be celebrated after the Ascension of the Lord. First Council of Orléans, title 23, canon 31.

Concerning holding second litanies on the Kalends of November. Council of Girona, title 3, canon 40.

Concerning the institution of new litanies. Fifth Council of Toledo, title 1, canon 50.

Concerning observance of litanies. Sixth Council of Toledo, title 2, canon 51.

TITLE XVIII. Concerning observance of fasts.

[Col. 0069B]

That it is not permitted to break the common fasts. Council of Gangra, title 19, canon 4.

Concerning those who deliberately fast on Sunday: that they not be considered catholic. Fourth Council of Carthage, title 64, canon 15.

Concerning the seasons of fasts: that a fast be kept in every month except July and August. Council of Elvira, title 23, canon 38.

That fasting be observed every Saturday. Same council, title 26.

That fasting be rightly observed every Saturday. Innocent's letter to Decentius, 6, title 4.

TITLE XIX. Concerning observance of Lent.

That martyrs' birthdays ought not to be celebrated in Lent, except that their commemoration be made only on Saturday and Sunday. Council of Laodicea, title 51, canon 7.

[Col. 0069C] That during all days of Lent fasting be observed on Saturday also, even with the authority of strict observance. Council of Agde, title 12, canon 30.

That it is not permitted to break the fast on Thursday of the final week. Council of Laodicea, title 50, canon 7.

Concerning not breaking the fast on Thursday of Easter. In Martin's excerpts, title 50, canon 64.

Concerning not breaking the fast on Friday of Easter. Fourth Council of Toledo, canon 49.

That before Easter not fifty days but forty days be observed. First Council of Orléans, title 20, canon 31.

That during the days of Lent no one absent himself from church. First Council of Saragossa, title 2, canon 41.

Concerning the non-celebration of martyrs’ feast days, or of human birthdays, and of weddings during the days of Lent. In the excerpts of Martin, title 48, canon 64.

During Lent, offerings are to be made only on Saturday and Sunday. Council of Laodicea, title 49, canon 7.

## TITLE XX. Concerning the determination and celebration of Easter

[Col. 0069D]

That bishops of the same province should inquire of their primate concerning the date of Easter. Third Council of Carthage, title 1, canon 14.

That bishops, assembling each year in council concerning the solemnity of Easter, should be informed by their primate. Council cited above, title 41.

Concerning announcing the time of Easter, or of the council, to the provinces by formal letters. Fifth Council of Carthage, title 7, canon 16.

Concerning the announcement of Easter to be sought among the bishops before Epiphany. Fourth Council of Toledo, title 5, canon 49.

That Easter should be announced each year by the metropolitan bishop. Second Council of Braga, title 6, canon 64.

Concerning celebrating Easter on one day and at one time. Fourth Council of Carthage, title 65, canon 15.

That Easter should be celebrated on one day and at one time. First Council of Arles, title 1, canon 21.

That Easter should not be celebrated at a different time, nor together with the Jews. Council of Antioch, title 1, canon 7.

[Col. 0070A] Concerning the notification and appointed times of Easter. Letter of Innocent to Aurelius, in full, 15.

Concerning the celebration of Pentecost. Council of Elvira, title 43, canon 38.

Concerning the celebration of the feast of the Lord’s mother Mary. Tenth Council of Toledo, title 1, canon 55.

## TITLE XXI. Concerning catechumens

That catechumens should hear the Gospels. Council of Orange, title 18, canon 27.

Concerning catechumens who do not attend church. Council of Elvira, title 45, canon 38.

Concerning sinful catechumens: they should either hear the word after being corrected or be completely rejected. Council of Neocaesarea, title 15, canon 3.

That catechumens should never approach the baptistery. Council of Orange, title 19, canon 27.

That catechumens should not receive the blessing together with the faithful. Council cited above, title 20.

[Col. 0070B] That the sacrament should not be given to catechumens. Third Council of Carthage, title 5, canon 14.

Concerning catechumens who die without baptism: they are not to be commemorated in the offering. First Council of Braga, title 17, canon 63.

## TITLE XXII. Concerning those who can administer baptism

That the faithful should baptize in cases of necessity. Council of Elvira, title 38, canon 38.

## TITLE XXIII. That baptism must be administered in the name of the Trinity

That one must be baptized in the name of the Trinity. Letter of Vigilius to Profuturus, 96, title 6.

## TITLE XXIV. Concerning the efficacy of baptism

That in baptism death precedes through the destruction of sin, and that the threefold immersion imitates Christ’s burial, while the raising from the waters is like resurrection from the tomb. Letter of Leo to the bishops throughout Sicily, 63, title 3.

That the purification instituted for those who are to be baptized also bears witness to the grace of God, since unclean spirits are driven out from them through exorcisms and breathings. Letter of Celestine to the bishops of Gaul, 33, title 12.

## TITLE XXV. Concerning baptismal immersion

Concerning threefold and single immersion in baptism. Fourth Council of Toledo, title 6, canon 49.

Concerning threefold immersion. Letter of Vigilius to Profuturus, 96, title 2.

Concerning threefold and single emergence. Letter of Gregory to Leander, in full, 97.

## TITLE XXVI. Concerning the time of baptism

[Col. 0070D]

Concerning when those who come to the faith should be baptized. Council of Elvira, title 42, canon 38.

That baptism should be administered only at Easter and the Nativity of the Lord, except for those who are in the weakness of illness. Council of Gerunda, title 4, canon 40.

That no one should be received for baptism after the second week of Lent. Council of Laodicea, title 44, canon 7.

That infants should not be received for baptism except before the three weeks preceding Easter, and that those to be baptized should recite the Creed, which they are to return to the priests on Thursday of Easter week. In the excerpts of Martin, title 49, canon 64.

That baptism should not be celebrated except at Easter and Pentecost; nevertheless, it may be celebrated at any time in cases of necessity. Letter of Siricius to Himerius, 3, title 2.

That the celebration of baptism on the day of Epiphany is prohibited. Letter of Leo to the bishops throughout Sicily, 63, title 1.

[Col. 0071A] That all the sacraments of salvation have been ordered for us according to the sequence of events through the incarnation of our Lord Jesus Christ. In the work cited above, title 2.

That baptism should be administered at Easter and Pentecost. In the work cited above, title 3.

That blessed Peter baptized three thousand men on the day of Pentecost. In the work cited above, title 4.

That baptism should be administered at Easter and Pentecost. In the work cited above, title 5.

That at any time those who are pressed by the danger of death, illness, siege, persecution, or shipwreck ought to be baptized. Also concerning the explanation of Christ’s baptism. In the work cited above, title 6.

That regeneration through baptism should not be given at every time except at Easter or Pentecost; nevertheless, it may be given at any time in cases of necessity. Letter of Leo to the bishops throughout Campania, Samnium, and Picenum, 73, title 1.

That outside the Easter season and Pentecost no one should presume to baptize. General decree of Gelasius, 82, title 12.

## TITLE XXVII. Concerning the baptism of the sick and the refusal to baptize the dead

[Col. 0071B]

Concerning those who are baptized during illness: once restored to health, they should be taught the Creed. Council of Laodicea, title 47, canon 7.

Concerning sick persons to be baptized who are already unable to speak. Third Council of Carthage, title 34, canon 14.

Concerning a female catechumen who has fallen gravely ill: when she is to be baptized. Council of Elvira, title 11, canon 38.

That an infant one day old should be baptized if it is in danger. Council of Gerunda, title 5, canon 40.

That baptism or the Eucharist should not be given to the dead. Third Council of Carthage, title 6, canon 14.

## TITLE XXVIII. Concerning the baptism of pregnant women

Concerning the baptism of pregnant women, since each person’s confession is accepted on her own behalf. In the excerpts of Martin, title 54, canon 64.

[Col. 0071C] Concerning the baptism of pregnant women: the sacrament of baptism communicates nothing to the child being generated. Council of Neocaesarea, title 6, canon 3.

## TITLE XXIX. Concerning the baptism of gentiles

Concerning the baptism of pagan prostitutes, if they convert. Council of Elvira, title 44, canon 38.

## TITLE XXX. Concerning doubtful baptism

Concerning those for whom no evidence establishes that they have been baptized: they are to be baptized. Fifth Council of Carthage, title 6, canon 16.

Concerning those who doubt whether they have received baptism: it is necessary that they be reborn. Letter of Leo to Rusticus, 66, title 15.

Concerning little children who have fallen into captivity and do not remember the grace of baptism: they are to be baptized. Letter of Leo to Leo of Ravenna, 71, title 1.

## TITLE XXXI. Concerning the rules for those to be baptized

[Col. 0071D]

That those who are to be baptized should give their names and abstain from wine and meat. Fourth Council of Carthage, title 85, canon 15.

That those recently baptized should live chastely and continently. Fourth Council of Carthage, title 86, canon 15.

Those to be baptized must be taught the Creed and return it on Thursday of Easter week. Council of Laodicea, title 46, canon 7.

## TITLE XXXII. Concerning the order of baptism

Concerning the order according to which it is proper to baptize. First Council of Braga, title 5, canon 63.

## TITLE XXXIII. Concerning the baptized who have not been confirmed and have died in that condition

Concerning the baptized who die before being confirmed. Council of Elvira, title 77, canon 38.

## TITLE XXXIV. Concerning the children of Catholics if they are given to heretics for baptism

[Col. 0072A]

Concerning Catholics who have given their children for baptism to heretics: their offering is not to be received. Council of Ilerda, title 13, canon 44.

## TITLE XXXV. Concerning not repeating baptism

Baptism received in the Trinity is not to be repeated. First Council of Carthage, title 1, canon 12.

Those converted from heresy, if they have been baptized in the Trinity, are to receive only the laying on of hands. First Council of Arles, title 8, canon 21.

Concerning those who have been rebaptized: how greatly they should repent. Council of Ilerda, title 9, canon 44.

Concerning bishops, priests, and deacons who, after falling into heresy, have submitted themselves to baptism: they are to have only lay communion. Letter of Felix to the bishops throughout Sicily, 79, title 2.

[Col. 0072B] Concerning clerics, monks, maidens of God, and secular persons who impiously have submitted themselves to being rebaptized. In the work cited above, title 3.

Concerning those who have been rebaptized through ignorance in childhood, and concerning the penalties established for those who fall into this impiety. In the work cited above, title 4.

Arians are not to be rebaptized by Catholics. Letter of Siricius to Himerius, 3, title 1.

That those who come from the Novatians or Montenses are not to be rebaptized. Letter of Innocent to Victoricus, 7, title 8.

That those who acknowledge that they have been baptized but do not know in which faith should appropriately be received through the laying on of hands. Letter of Leo to Rusticus, 66, title 16.

That those who have been baptized by heretics should be strengthened solely through invocation of the Holy Spirit. Letter of Leo to Nicetas of Aquileia, 68, title 7.

That those who are baptized by heretics should receive the Holy Spirit through the laying on of hands. Letter of Leo [Col. 0072C] to Leo of Ravenna, 71, title 2.

Concerning those who have grieved over being rebaptized and afterward wished to repent. Letter of Felix to the bishops throughout Sicily, 79, title 1.

Concerning those who are rebaptized by Arians; and that one laying on of hands is performed so that the Holy Spirit may be received, while another is performed so that the fruit of repentance may be obtained and they may be restored through holy communion. Letter of Vigilius to Profuturus, 96, title 3.

That those who have inclined their minds toward a repetition of baptism, whether compelled by force or fear, should be relieved by the remedy of repentance, and that careful consideration should also be given to old age, dangers, illnesses, and other necessities. Letter of Leo to Nicetas of Aquileia, 68, title 6.

The sacrilegious act of rebaptizing is not to be believed or undertaken as a good work. Third Council of Toledo, from the chapters against the Arians, title 15, canon 48.

## TITLE XXXVI. Concerning the baptized being sealed only by bishops

[Col. 0072D]

That the baptized should be sealed only by bishops, and that priests are not permitted to anoint the forehead with chrism, since this belongs exclusively to bishops when they confer the Holy Spirit. Letter of Innocent to Decentius, 6, title 3.

Concerning baptized demoniacs: with the bishop’s permission, they may be sealed by priests, and the other clerics should lay hands upon them. In the work cited above, title 6.

Concerning the anointing of the sick with chrism, and prayer to be offered for them in accordance with the remembrance of the letter of Saint James. Letter of Innocent to Decentius, 6, title 8.

## TITLE XXXVII. Concerning the baptized being anointed with chrism

Chrism is to be given after baptism. Council of Laodicea, title 48, canon 8.

That heretics who have been baptized in the Trinity are to be received with chrism and the laying on of hands. Second Council of Arles, title 17, canon 22.

That no estates or contributions are to be exacted from the faithful who are being baptized and sealed. General decree of Gelasius, 82, title 7.

## TITLE XXXVIII. Concerning the funerals of Christians

The bodies of the devout are to be carried to the graves with psalms and hymns alone. Third Council of Toledo, title 22, canon 48.

Human bodies are in no way to be buried within the basilicas of the saints. First Council of Braga, title 18, canon 63.

## TITLE XXXIX. Concerning not judging the dead

[Col. 0073B] It is not proper to judge rashly concerning those who have already departed to [Col. 0074A] the Lord. Letter of Anastasius to Anastasius Augustus, 84, title 2.

## TITLE XL. Concerning demoniacs

Hands are to be laid upon demoniacs every day by exorcists. Fourth Council of Carthage, title 90, canon 15.

Demoniacs should sweep the floors of the house of God. Council cited above, title 91.

Food is to be provided to demoniacs in the house of God by exorcists. Council cited above, title 92.

Concerning baptized demoniacs: they should obey the admonitions of the clergy. Council of Orange, title 14, canon 27.

Demoniacs and catechumens are to be consulted concerning baptism. Council of Orange, title 15, canon 27.

Concerning demoniacs: neither is their name to be recited nor are they themselves to minister. Council of Elvira, title 29, canon 38.

Concerning when demoniacs are to be baptized or admitted to communion. [Col. 0074B] Council cited above, title 37.

# BOOK FIVE. CONCERNING THE VARIETIES OF MARRIAGE AND THE CRIME OF OUTRAGES

[Col. 0073]

## VERSE

[Col. 0073B]

**I.** Whatever, illustrious one, it was your command to promulgate,

the whole laboring hand eagerly returned to you;

I have set forth the Church, baptism, choirs, and songs;

after these things, unfold the way by which the traveler may know how to proceed.

**R.** From this point arrange the rising of noble seed;

[Col. 0074B] let the married woman hold to her husband, and let the husband cease to leave his wife;

let offspring be born once the common will has been fulfilled;

let marital intercourse cease when mutual consent is withheld;

let a noble life thus govern both parents,

and let everlasting life retain them both after death.

## TITLE I. Concerning the non-condemnation of marriage and the regulation of marriages

[Col. 0073C]

Concerning how bridegroom and bride are blessed, and concerning their chastity during the time of marriage. Fourth Council of Carthage, title 13, canon 15.

Concerning those who condemn marriage. Council of Gangra, title 1, canon 4.

If anyone says or believes that human marriages, which are permitted according to divine law, are accursed, let him be anathema. First Council of Toledo, from the rules of the Catholic faith against the Priscillianists, title 16, canon 46.

Those who pursue virginity must not condemn marriage. Council of Gangra, title 9, canon 4.

Concerning those who are proud on account of virginity. In the work cited above, title 10.

One who condemns marriage must not separate from her husband. In the work cited above, title 14.

[Col. 0073D] Marriage may not take place during Lent. Council of Laodicea, title 52, canon 7.

It is not permitted for Christians going to weddings to form a procession or dance. In the work cited above, title 53.

Concerning one who violates the sister of his betrothed. Council of Ancyra, title 25, canon 2.

Concerning parents who break their betrothal pledges. Council of Elvira, title 54, canon 38.

That it is not permitted to take another man’s betrothed as one’s wife. Letter of Siricius to Himerius, 3, title 4.

If someone’s wife has been absent and the husband has contracted another marriage, when the first wife returns, the second woman must be dismissed. Letter of Innocent to Probus, in full, 14.

That women who have married other men after their husbands were captured should be joined to their former husbands when the latter return from captivity. Letter of Leo to Nicetas, 68, title 1.

That one who appears to have taken a captive’s wife in marriage is not to be considered culpable. In the work cited above, title 2.

[Col. 0074B] If men returning from captivity remain devoted to their wives, they shall receive them back. In the work cited above, title 3.
