# Councils of Spain (C)

[Note: [Col. 0301D] [ [Col. 0301] This note is printed at the foot of column 301, but its callout letter, a, does not appear in the text.] In the codices: Eliberitan.]

## Thirty-eighth Council of Eliberis, of nineteen bishops, issued in the time of Constantine, held at the same time as the Council of Nicaea

[Note: [Col. 0301D] Ae., T. 1, 2: the year 362.]

[Col. 0301B] 281–282 When the holy and devout bishops had assembled in the Church of Eliberis—that is, Felix, bishop of Acci; Hosius, bishop of Córdoba; Sabinus, bishop of Seville; Camerimnus, bishop of Tucci; Sinagius, bishop of Epagra; Secundinus [B. R.: Secundus], bishop of Castulo; Pardus, bishop of Mentesa; Flavianus [T. 1, 2: Flavius], bishop of Eliberis; Cantonius, bishop of Urci; Liberius, bishop of Mérida; Valerius, bishop of Zaragoza; Decentius, bishop of León; Melantius, bishop of Toledo; Januarius, bishop of Fibularia; Vincentius, bishop of Ossonoba; Quintianus, bishop of Elborum; Succesus, bishop of Eliocroca; Eutychianus, bishop of Bastetania; and Patricius, bishop of Málaga—together with the presbyters [Col. 0301C] [Note: [Col. 0301D] The names of the presbyters have been taken from Codices U. and G., in which several place-names are corrupted; we have thought it preferable to reproduce them as they appear there.], Restitutus, presbyter of Epora; Natalis, presbyter of Urso; Maurus, presbyter of Iliturgi; Lamponianus of Carbula; Barbatus of Astigi; Felicissimus of Ateva; Leo of Acinippo; Liberalis of Eliocroca; Januarius of Lauro; Januarianus of Barbe; Victorinus of Egabrum; Titus of Ajune; Eucharius of Municipium; Silvanus of Segalvinia; Victor of Ulia; Januarius of Urci; Leo of Gemella; Turrinus of Castelona; Luxurius of Drona; Emeritus of Baria; Eumantius of Solia; Clementianus of Ossigi; Eutyches of Carthage; and Julianus of Córdoba—on the Ides of May, with all residing at Eliberis, with the deacons and all the people present, all the bishops said:

### I. Concerning those who sacrificed to idols after baptism

It was agreed among them: If anyone, after professing the faith of saving baptism, should approach an idol’s temple in adulthood in order to worship the idol, and should do what is a capital crime [Note: [Col. 0302D] Ae., B.R., T. 1, 2: principal crime], since it is a very grave offense, it was agreed that he should not receive communion even at the end of his life.

### II. Concerning pagan priests who sacrificed after baptism

As for the flamines who sacrificed after professing the faith of the washing and regeneration [Note: [Col. 0302D] U., G.: after the baptism of regeneration], because they have doubled their offenses by homicide being added, or tripled their crime with adultery accompanying it, it was agreed that they should not receive communion even at the end of their lives.

### III. Concerning the same persons if they merely gave a gift to idols

Likewise, as for flamines who did not sacrifice but merely gave a gift, because they abstained from deadly sacrifices, it was agreed that communion should be granted to them at the end of their lives, provided that they had performed legitimate penance. But if these same persons committed adultery after penance, it was agreed that communion should no longer be given to them, lest they appear to have mocked [Note: [Col. 0302D] Ae., B.R., T. 1, 2, U., G.: played with] the Lord’s communion.

### IV. Concerning the same persons if, while still catechumens, they sacrifice [U., G.: sacrificed] when they are baptized

283 Likewise, if flamines are catechumens and have abstained from sacrifices, it was agreed that they ought to be admitted to baptism after a period of three years.

### V. If a mistress kills a maidservant out of jealousy

If any woman [T. 2: mistress], inflamed by the fury of jealousy, beats her maidservant with whips so that she gives up her life in agony within the third day [U., G.: before the third day], since it is uncertain whether she killed her intentionally or accidentally, then, if intentionally, she may be admitted to communion after seven years, and, if accidentally, after five years [Note: [Col. 0302D] T. 1, 2: after five years, once legitimate penance has been performed]; but if she should become ill before the prescribed periods, it was agreed that she should receive communion.

### VI. If anyone kills another person by sorcery

But if anyone kills another by sorcery, since he could not have accomplished this crime without idolatry, it was agreed that communion should not be granted to him even at the end of his life [U., G.: to him].

### VII. Concerning penitents for adultery if they commit adultery again

If any believer, after a fall into adultery, having performed penance after the prescribed periods, should again commit fornication, it was agreed that he should not have communion even at the end of his life.

### VIII. Concerning women who leave their husbands and marry others

Likewise, women who, without any prior cause, leave their husbands and unite themselves to other men shall not receive communion even at the end of their lives.

### IX. Concerning women who leave adulterous husbands and marry others

Likewise, if a believing woman leaves an adulterous husband [Col. 0303B] and marries another, she shall be prohibited from marrying. If she marries, she shall not receive communion before the man whom she left has departed from this world—unless, perhaps, the necessity of illness compels it to be given.

### X. Concerning a woman abandoned by a catechumen if she marries another

If the woman whom a catechumen abandons marries a husband, she may be admitted to the washing of the font. The same shall be observed concerning female catechumens. But if the woman being married is a believer, and the man marrying her has abandoned an innocent wife, and she knows that he has a wife whom he left without cause, it was agreed that communion of this kind should be given even at the end of her life [Note: [Col. 0303D] B.R.: it was agreed that communion should not be given to her even at the end of her life. T. 1, 2: it was agreed that communion should not be given to her even at the end.]

### XI. Concerning a female catechumen if she becomes seriously ill

But if a female catechumen becomes seriously ill within the period of five years, it was agreed that baptism should be given to her and not denied [Col. 0303C].

### XII. Concerning women who practice procuring prostitution

If a mother, relative, or any other believing woman practices procuring prostitution, because she has sold another person’s body—or rather her own—it was agreed that she should not receive communion even at the end of her life.

### XIII. Concerning virgins consecrated to God if they commit adultery

If virgins who have dedicated themselves to God lose the pledge of their virginity and continue to serve the same lust, not understanding what they have committed, it was agreed that communion should not be given to them even at the end of their lives. But if, having been persuaded only once or having fallen through the weakness of the body, such women perform penance throughout the whole period of their lives so as to abstain from intercourse, since they appear rather to have fallen, it was agreed that they ought to receive communion at the end of their lives.

### XIV. Concerning secular virgins if they commit adultery

If virgins who have not guarded their virginity marry and retain as husbands the very men who violated them, since they have violated only the marriage bond, they ought to be reconciled after one year without penance. But if they have relations with other men, since they have committed adultery, it was agreed that they ought to be admitted to communion after performing legitimate penance for five years.

### XV. Concerning the marriage of those who come from paganism

Because of the abundance of young women among the pagans, Christian virgins must by no means be given to them in marriage [Col. 0304A], lest an age swelling in the flower of youth be dissolved into the adultery of the soul.

### XVI. That believing girls not be joined to unbelievers

If heretics refuse to transfer themselves to the Catholic Church, Catholic girls are not to be given to them. Nor did it seem right to give them to Jews or heretics, since there can be no fellowship between a believer and an unbeliever. If parents act contrary to the prohibition, it was agreed that they should abstain for five years.

### XVII. Concerning those who join their daughters to pagan priests

If anyone should join his daughters to priests of idols, it was agreed that communion should not be given to them even at the end of their lives.

### XVIII. Concerning priests and ministers if they commit adultery

[Col. 0304B] If bishops, presbyters, or deacons, while serving in the ministry, are discovered to have committed adultery, it was agreed that, because of the scandal and the profane crime, they ought not to receive communion even at the end of their lives.

### XIX. Concerning clerics who pursue commerce and markets

Bishops, presbyters, and deacons must not leave their places for the sake of conducting business, nor travel through the provinces pursuing profitable markets [Note: [Col. 0303D] U.: lest, traveling through the provinces and pursuing profitable markets, they incur danger]. For obtaining their own sustenance, however, they may send a son, freedman, hired worker, friend, or anyone [Note: [Col. 0304D] U.: any faithful person]. And if they wish to trade, they shall trade within the province.

### XX. Concerning clerics and laymen who practice usury

If any cleric is discovered to accept interest, it was agreed that he should be degraded and placed under abstention. If a layman is also proven to have accepted interest [Col. 0304C] and, when corrected, promises that he will now cease and will not exact it thereafter, it was agreed that he should also be granted pardon. But if he persists in that wickedness, he must be expelled from the Church.

### XXI. Concerning those who come late to church

If anyone residing in a city fails to come to church for three successive Sundays, he shall be placed under abstention for a short time, so that he may appear to have been corrected.

### XXII. Concerning Catholics who pass over to heresy, if they return

If anyone transfers from the Catholic Church to heresy and returns again, it was agreed that penance should not be denied him, since he has recognized his sin. He shall also perform penance for ten years, after which communion ought to be granted to him. But if children have been led over, since they have not sinned through their own fault, they must be received without hesitation [B. R.: they shall have to be received].

286 ### XXIII. Concerning the times of fasting

It was agreed that the appointed fasts [Ae., T. 2: additional fasts] should be observed each month, except during the days of the two months of July and August, because of the infirmity of certain persons.

### XXIV. Concerning those baptized abroad, that they not enter the clergy

Everyone baptized abroad, because their way of life is by no means known [Col. 0305A], shall not be promoted to the clergy in foreign provinces.

### XXV. Concerning the commendatory letters of confessors

Anyone who brings confessor’s letters with the confessor’s name removed, since all simple people are indiscriminately harassed under the glory of this name, shall be given letters of communion.

### XXVI. That there be fasting every Saturday

It was agreed that an error should be corrected, so that we observe the appointed fasts on every Saturday.

### XXVII. Concerning clerics, that they not have strange women in their houses

A bishop or any other cleric shall have with him only a sister or a virgin daughter dedicated to God. It was agreed that he should have no unrelated woman at all.

### XXVIII. Concerning the offerings of those who do not communicate

[Col. 0305B]

It was agreed that a bishop must not accept a gift from one who does not communicate [Note: [Col. 0305D] Ae., B.R., T. 1, 2. G.: gifts].

### XXIX. How the possessed are to be treated in church

The name of one who is tormented by a wandering spirit is neither to be recited at the altar with the offering, nor is he to be permitted to minister with his own hand in the church.

### XXX. Concerning those who commit adultery after baptism, that they not become subdeacons

Those who have committed adultery in their youth must not be ordained subdeacons, since afterward they may be promoted through stealth to a higher rank. If any have already been ordained, they shall be removed.

287 ### XXXI. Concerning young men who commit adultery after baptism

[Col. 0305C]

Young men who have committed adultery after professing the faith of saving baptism shall, once they have taken wives and performed legitimate penance, be admitted to communion.

### XXXII. Concerning excommunicated presbyters, that they give communion in necessity

If anyone, having suffered a serious fall, has fallen into mortal peril while under a presbyter, it was agreed that he should not perform penance there but rather before the bishop. Nevertheless, when illness compels it, the presbyter must grant communion, and the deacon also if the priest orders him to do so.

### XXXIII. Concerning bishops and ministers, that they abstain from their wives

It was agreed to prohibit entirely bishops, presbyters, deacons, and all clerics serving in the ministry from having intercourse with their wives and begetting children [Col. 0305D]. Whoever does so shall be expelled from the honor of the clergy.

### XXXIV. That candles not be lit in cemeteries

It was agreed that candles should not be lit in a cemetery during the day, for the spirits of the saints are not to be disturbed. Those who do not observe this shall be barred from communion with the Church.

### XXXV. That women not keep vigil in cemeteries

It was agreed to prohibit women from keeping vigil in a cemetery [Col. 0306A], since they often secretly commit crimes under the pretext of prayer.

### XXXVI. That paintings not be made in a church

It was agreed that there should be no paintings in a church, lest what is worshiped and adored be depicted on the walls [Note: [Col. 0305D] Ae., B.R., E. 3, T. 1, 2: lest it not be depicted].

### XXXVII. Concerning the possessed who have not been baptized

Those who are tormented by unclean spirits, if they are at the point of death, should, it was agreed, be baptized; if they are believers, communion should be given to them. It must also be prohibited that such persons publicly light lamps. If they wish to act contrary to the prohibition, they shall be placed under abstention from communion.

288 ### XXXVIII. That, in necessity, believers also baptize

In a place abroad, or if there is no church nearby, a believer who has kept his own washing undefiled and is not a bigamist may, in a case of illness and necessity, baptize a catechumen. If the catechumen survives, he must be brought to the bishop, so that the rite may be completed through the laying on of hands.

### XXXIX. Concerning pagans who request baptism in danger

If pagans, during illness, desire that hands be laid upon them, and if their life has been honorable in some respect, it was agreed that hands should be laid upon them and that they should become Christians.

### XL. That believers not accept what has been offered to idols

It was agreed that, when possessors receive their accounts, they must not enter as received anything that has been given to an idol. If they act after the prohibition, they are to be barred from communion for a period of five years.

### XLI. That masters prohibit their slaves from worshiping idols

[Col. 0306C]

It was agreed that believers should be admonished, so far as they can, to prevent idols from being kept in their houses. If they fear force from their slaves, let them at least keep themselves pure. If they do not do so, they shall be regarded as outside the Church.

### XLII. Concerning those who come to the faith, when they are to be baptized

Those who come to the first faith of belief, if their conduct has been good, ought, it was agreed, to be admitted to the grace of baptism within two years—unless illness makes it necessary to give more rapid aid to one in danger or requesting grace.

### XLIII. Concerning the celebration of Pentecost

It was agreed that a corrupt institution should be corrected according to the authority of the Scriptures, so that we all celebrate the day of Pentecost [Col. 0306D], lest anyone who fails to do so be accused of introducing a new heresy [Note: [Col. 0305D] T. 1: let us celebrate the day of Pentecost after Easter, not the fortieth but the fiftieth day; whoever does not do so].

### XLIV. Concerning pagan prostitutes if they convert

If a prostitute who had once been [Note: [Col. 0306D] U.: who had once been a pagan] and later had a husband subsequently comes to belief, it was agreed that she should be received without hesitation.

289 ### XLV. Concerning catechumens who do not attend church

If someone has at some time been a catechumen and for countless periods has never come to church, but someone from the clergy knows him to be a Christian, or some faithful witnesses have come forward, it was agreed that baptism should not be denied him [Col. 0307A], since he appears to have abandoned the old man [Note: [Col. 0307D] Ae., T. 1, 2, U.: since he appears to have fallen into the old man].

### XLVI. Concerning believers who apostatize, how long they should do penance

If a believing apostate has not come to church for countless periods, but has eventually returned and has not been an idolater, it was agreed that he should receive communion after ten years.

### XLVII. Concerning one who, although he has a wife, repeatedly commits adultery

If a believer who has a wife has committed adultery not once but repeatedly, he must be summoned at the point of death. If he promises that he will cease, communion shall be given to him. If, after being restored to life, he again commits adultery, it was agreed that he should no longer be trifled with concerning the communion of peace.

### XLVIII. Concerning the baptized, that the clergy receive nothing

[Col. 0307B] It was agreed that it should be corrected so that those who are baptized do not, as used to be done, put coins into the basin, lest the priest appear to sell for a price what he received freely. Nor are their feet to be washed by priests or [T. 1: but] clerics.

### XLIX. Concerning the produce of believers, that it not be blessed by Jews

It was agreed that possessors should be admonished not to allow their produce, which they receive from God with thanksgiving, to be blessed by Jews, lest they render our blessing invalid and ineffective. If anyone presumes to do this after the prohibition, he shall be completely expelled from the Church.

### L. Concerning Christians who eat with Jews

If any cleric or believer eats food with Jews, it was agreed that he should be excluded from communion, so that he may be corrected [Col. 0307C].

### LI. Concerning heretics, that they not be promoted to the clergy

If a believer comes from any heresy, he must by no means be promoted to the clergy. If any have been ordained in the past, they shall without doubt be deposed.

290 ### LII. Concerning those who post defamatory notices in a church

Those who are found posting defamatory notices in a church shall be anathematized.

### LIII. Concerning bishops who communicate with another’s excommunicate

It was agreed by all that a person should receive communion from the bishop by whom he had been excluded when he was excluded for some offense. But if another bishop presumes to admit him, while the former bishop has neither done so nor consented—he by whom the man was deprived of communion—let that other bishop know that he will have to answer for such matters among the brethren at the peril of his own standing.

### LIV. Concerning parents who break their betrothal pledges

If parents break the pledge of a betrothal, they shall abstain for three years. If, however, the same bridegroom or bride is discovered to have committed a serious offense, the parents shall be excused. If the fault was in those persons themselves and they polluted themselves, the preceding sentence shall be observed.

### LV. Concerning pagan priests who no longer sacrifice

Priests who merely wear crowns, neither sacrifice nor contribute anything from their own resources to idols, were permitted, it was agreed, to receive communion after two years.

### LVI. Concerning magistrates and duumvirs

As for a magistrate, during the one year in which he serves as duumvir, it was agreed that he should be required to keep himself away from the Church [T. 1, 2: it was agreed that he should].

### LVII. Concerning those who give garments for the adornment of worldly pomp

Matronae, or their husbands, must not give their garments for the secular adornment of pomp. If they do so, they shall abstain for three years.

### LVIII. Concerning those who carry letters of communion, that they be questioned about the faith

It was agreed everywhere, and especially in the place where the first episcopal see was established, that those who deliver letters of communion should be questioned as to whether everything is in proper order and attested by their testimony.

291 ### LIX. Concerning believers, that they not ascend the Capitol for the purpose of sacrifice

[Col. 0308B]

It must be prohibited that any Christian, like a pagan, ascend to the idol of the Capitol for the purpose of sacrificing or observing. If he does so, he shall be held guilty of the same offense. If he is a believer, he shall be received after ten years, once he has performed penance.

### LX. Concerning those who are killed while destroying idols

If anyone breaks idols and is killed there, since it is not written in the Gospel, nor will it be found ever to have been done under the apostles [Note: [Col. 0308D] G.: since it is not written in the Gospel], it was agreed that he should not be admitted to the number of martyrs.

### LXI. Concerning those who marry two sisters

If anyone, after the death of his wife, marries her sister [Col. 0308C], and she herself is a believer, it was agreed that he should abstain from communion for five years—unless perhaps the necessity of illness compels peace to be granted more quickly.

### LXII. Concerning charioteers and pantomimes if they convert

If a charioteer or pantomime wishes to believe, it was agreed that he must first renounce his arts and only then be received, on the condition that he not return to them thereafter. If they attempt to act contrary to the prohibition, they shall be expelled from the Church.

### LXIII. Concerning wives who kill children conceived in adultery

If a woman conceives through adultery while her husband is absent and then kills the child after the crime, it was agreed that communion should not be given to her even at the end of her life, because she has doubled her offense.

### LXIV. Concerning women who commit adultery with other men until death

[Col. 0308D]

If a woman commits adultery with another man until the end of her life, it was agreed that communion should not be given to her even at the end of her life. But if she leaves him, she may receive communion after ten years, once she has performed legitimate penance.

### LXV. Concerning adulterous wives of clerics

If the wife of a cleric commits adultery, and her husband knows that she is committing adultery but does not immediately cast her out, he shall not receive communion even at the end of his life, lest those who ought to be examples of good conduct appear to provide models of wickedness.

292 ### LXVI. Concerning those who marry their stepdaughters

[Col. 0309A]

If anyone takes his stepdaughter [Note: [Col. 0309D] T. 1: his stepdaughter descended from an ancestor] as wife, since this is incest, it was agreed that communion should not be given to him even at the end of his life.

### LXVII. Concerning the marriage of a female catechumen

It must be prohibited that any believing woman or female catechumen have either long-haired men (*comati*) or male hairdressers (*cinerarii*) [Note: [Col. 0309D] From Ae., B.R., T. 1, U. In A., E. 3: *cenorarii*. In T. 2: *generarii*.]. Any who do this shall be barred from communion.

### LXVIII. Concerning an adulterous female catechumen who kills her child

If a female catechumen conceives through adultery and suffocates the child, it was agreed that she should be baptized at the end of her life.

### LXIX. Concerning married men who afterward fall into adultery

If anyone who has a wife falls once, it was agreed that he should perform penance for five years and then be reconciled, unless the necessity of illness compels communion to be given before the appointed time [Col. 0309B]. The same shall be observed concerning women.

### LXX. Concerning women who commit adultery with the knowledge of their husbands

If a wife commits adultery with the knowledge of her husband, it was agreed that communion should not be given to her even at the end of her life [B. R., U., G.: to them]. But if he leaves her, she may receive communion after ten years, if, while knowing her to be adulterous, he retained her in his house for any period.

### LXXI. Concerning those who sexually violate boys

Communion must not be given to those who sexually violate boys, even at the end of their lives.

### LXXII. Concerning adulterous widows if they later take the same man as husband

If a widow commits adultery and afterward has the same man as her husband, it was agreed that she should be reconciled to communion after five years, once she has performed legitimate penance [Col. 0309C]. If she leaves him and marries another, communion must not be given to her even at the end of her life. Or if the man whom she has taken is a believer, she shall not receive communion except after ten years, once she has performed legitimate penance—unless illness compels communion to be given more quickly.

293 ### LXXIII. Concerning informers

If an informer is a believer, and someone is proscribed or killed through his denunciation, it was agreed that he should not receive communion even at the end of his life. If the matter is less serious, he may receive communion within five years. If he is a catechumen, he shall be admitted to baptism after five years.

### LXXIV. Concerning false witnesses

A false witness shall abstain in proportion to the crime. If what he alleged was not a mortal offense, and he proves that he did not keep silent, he shall abstain for two years [Col. 0309D]. But if he does not prove it, then, after the clergy have been consulted [Col. 0310A], it was agreed that he should abstain for five years.

### LXXV. Concerning those who accuse priests or ministers but do not prove the charge

If anyone attacks a bishop, presbyter, or deacon with false accusations and cannot prove them, communion must not be given to him even at the end of his life.

### LXXVI. Concerning deacons who are proved to have sinned before their ordination

If anyone allows himself to be ordained a deacon and afterward is discovered to have committed a mortal offense at some earlier time, then, if he has confessed voluntarily, it was agreed that, after performing legitimate penance, he should receive communion after three years [Col. 0310B]. But if someone else exposes him, he must, after five years and after performing penance, receive lay communion.

294 ### LXXVII. Concerning baptized persons who die before being confirmed

If a deacon governing a congregation without a bishop or presbyter baptizes anyone, the bishop must complete them through a blessing. But if they depart from this world beforehand, each may be justified under the faith in which he believed.

### LXXVIII. Concerning married believers who commit adultery with a Jewess or pagan woman

If a married believer commits adultery with a Jewess or pagan woman, he shall be barred from communion. But if someone else exposes him, he may, after five years and legitimate penance [Col. 0310C], be joined to the Lord’s communion.

### LXXIX. Concerning those who play at tables

If a believer plays for money at dice—that is, at tables—it was agreed that he should be placed under abstention. If, once corrected, he stops, he may be reconciled to communion after one year.

### LXXX. Concerning freedmen

It must be prohibited that freedmen whose patrons are still in the world be promoted to the clergy.

### LXXXI. Concerning women’s letters

Women must not presume to write to laymen under their own names without the names of their husbands. Those who are believers may receive letters of peace addressed solely in their own names [Col. 0310D].

# Thirty-ninth Council of Tarragona, of ten bishops, held in the year 554 of the era, in the sixth year of King Theodoric, during the consulship of Peter, on the eighth day before the Ides of November

[Col. 0309]

[Col. 0309D] 295–296 The ancient statutes of the Fathers seem to have judged concerning matters that either reached them in their own time or that they certainly confirmed by their own testimony. Following their example, we too decreed that the matters now occurring should be observed, so that past provisions may be kept without ambiguity and present ones may be made firm through observance. Therefore, when we had assembled together in the city of Tarragona, which is metropolitan [Col. 0311A] [Note: [Col. 0311D] A., E. 3: founded upon metropolitan observance], we wrote down the titles appended below for observance.

### I. That clerics also go to their closest blood relatives with a witness

Concerning those whom permission is granted to care for because of the closeness of their kinship: they must support their needs with such caution that they provide from a distance the benefits of charity necessary for them. When they enter to visit them, they themselves must return after a swift greeting and must not remain there. Nevertheless, when they go to visit them, they shall bring with them as a witness to their companionship someone proved by faith and age. If any cleric despises these provisions established by us, he shall be deprived of the dignity of his office. But if he is a religious or monk, he shall be shut up in a monastic cell and devote himself to the laments of penance [Col. 0311B], where, under the abbot’s direction, he shall receive bread and water as his sole food with singular affliction.

### II. That clerics not be permitted to buy cheaply or sell dearly

As has been established by the statutes of the canons, whoever wishes to remain in the clergy must not engage in the pursuit of buying cheaply or selling dearly. Certainly, if he wishes to practice these things, he shall be restrained from the clergy.

### III. That if clerics lend a solidus, they receive it back without interest

If a cleric lends a solidus in a time of need, he shall receive in return such an amount of wine or grain as has been decreed for sale at the appointed time for purposes of trade. Otherwise, if he does not have the required commodity, he shall receive back exactly what he gave, without any increase.

### IV. That no bishop or inferior cleric presume to judge cases on Sunday

[Col. 0311C]

No bishop, presbyter, or cleric shall presume to judge on Sunday the matter of anyone’s case, except only that they may perform the solemn rites appointed for God. On the other days, with the parties consenting, they shall have permission to judge what is just, except in criminal matters.

### V. That a bishop not ordained in the metropolitan city present himself to the metropolitan after two months

If anyone is not ordained bishop in the metropolitan city, then, after receiving the blessing [Ae., T.: ordination] and obtaining the dignity of the episcopate through the metropolitan’s letters [Col. 0311D], we have decreed that the best course is for him afterward, at the appointed time—that is, when two months have been completed—to present himself before his metropolitan, so that, instructed more fully by him in ecclesiastical admonitions, he may recognize what he ought to observe [Ae., E. 3, U., G.: what]. If he should neglect to fulfill this, he shall be rebuked by the brethren in synod and corrected. But if some illness prevents him from fulfilling it, he shall take care to inform the metropolitan of this by letter.

297 ### VI. That a bishop who, after being summoned by the metropolitan, does not come to the synod be excommunicated

If any bishop [T. 1, 2, U.: bishop], having been summoned by the metropolitan [Col. 0312A] to the synod, contemptuously refuses to come when no serious bodily necessity intervenes, then, as the statutes of the Fathers have decreed, he shall be deprived of the communion of charity with all the bishops until the next council.

### VII. That the clerics of diocesan churches serve weekly rotations and all assemble on Saturday

Concerning diocesan churches and the clergy, it was agreed to define that the presbyters or deacons established there [Note: [Col. 0311D] Ae., B.R., E. 3: therein. U., G.: in the village] shall observe weekly rotations with the clerics: that is, the presbyter shall serve one week, and when it is completed the deacon shall succeed him in the same way. This condition must be observed: that the entire clergy be ready for vespers on Saturday, so that the solemnity of Sunday may more easily be celebrated in the presence of all. Nevertheless, vespers and matins shall be celebrated on every day, because we have discovered that, when the clergy withdraw—which is most deplorable—not even lights are supplied in the basilicas. If any, through the fault of negligence, refuse to fulfill these provisions, let them know that, according to the statutes of the canons and in proportion to their status, they will be subjected to canonical discipline.

### VIII. That bishops visit their dioceses each year and receive no more than a third from the parishes

Experience, that teacher of many circumstances, has shown us that some diocesan churches have been left abandoned. For this reason we decreed by constitution that the order of ancient custom be preserved and that dioceses be visited annually by the bishop, so that, if any basilica should be found abandoned, it may be restored by his appointment. For we know that it was established by ancient tradition that bishops receive a third from all the parishes [Col. 0312C].

## IX. Concerning clerics and doorkeepers who associate with adulterous women, so that they are to be expelled from the clergy

If any of the lectors wishes to associate or keep company with an adulterous woman, let him either abandon the adulteress or be regarded as an outsider by the clergy; the same sentence shall apply to the doorkeepers.

## X. That no bishop accept gifts in return for judgments

We have also decreed that no priest or cleric, like secular judges, dare accept gifts in return for services of advocacy, except perhaps gifts freely offered in the church, which do not appear to have been accepted because of the favor purchased by the gift but brought forward as an offering of devotion. For if any are proved to accept such things [G., “who accept such things”], let them know that, according to the statutes of the Fathers, they are to be degraded like extortioners of interest or possessors of usurious profits.  
[Note: [Col. 0312D] In all the other codices except A., where it reads: “to be denied.”]

## XI. That a monk sent somewhere presume not to perform clerical ministry, nor become a businessman or agent

We prohibit monks who go out from the monastery from presuming to perform any ecclesiastical ministry, unless perhaps with the command of the abbot. Likewise, let none of them—that is, of the monks—become an undertaker or agent in secular business, except for whatever the needs of the monastery require, with the abbot nevertheless issuing the command, while the constitution of the Gallican canons concerning them is observed above all.

## XII. That if a bishop dies intestate, the clerics make an inventory of his possessions and no one remove anything from them

[Col. 0313A]

If a bishop dies anywhere without a will, after his deposition the priests and deacons shall faithfully draw up a brief inventory of his possessions, from the smallest to the greatest—that is, of utensils [G., “utensils”] and of all his household goods—yet in such a way that if anyone is convicted of having presumed to take anything from them or of having secretly carried anything away, he shall restore everything according to the law concerning theft.

## XIII. That a bishop summon diocesan priests and certain laymen to the synod by letter

Such letters are to be sent by the brethren from the metropolitan, so that they summon to the council not only priests from the cathedral churches but also priests from the dioceses, and so that they bring with them some secular sons of the Church. [Col. 0313B]

John, bishop of the city of Tarragona, in the name of Christ, have signed the constitutions written by us [U., “made”].

[Col. 0314A] Paul, bishop of the city of Emporiae, in the name of Christ, have signed.

Hector, bishop of the metropolitan city of Carthage, in the name of Christ, have signed.  
[Note: [Col. 0313B] Ae., B.R., “of the metropolis of Carthage.” T. 1, “of the metropolis of Carthage.”]

299 Vincentius, bishop of the city of Zaragoza, in the name of Christ, have signed.

Ursus, bishop of the city of Dertosa [Note: [Col. 0313B] From Ae., B.R., E. 3, T. 1, 2, G. In A., U., “of the city of Tortosa.”], in the name of Christ, have signed.

Cynidius [Note: [Col. 0314B] From Ae., E. 3, T. 2, U., G. In A., Dinudius. B.R., T. 1, Canidius.], bishop of the city of Ausona, in the name of Christ, have signed. 300 [Col. 0314B]

# XL. COUNCIL OF GIRONA, OF SEVEN BISHOPS, HELD IN THE ERA 555, IN THE SEVENTH YEAR [B. R., THIRD YEAR] OF KING THEODORICUS, ON THE SIXTH IDES OF JUNE, WITH AGAPETUS, A MAN OF ILLUSTRIOUS RANK, AS CONSUL

[Col. 0313]

## I. That each province maintain one order in the Church’s worship

[Col. 0313C]

Concerning the arrangement of the Masses: just as they are celebrated in the metropolitan church, so, in the name of God, throughout the entire province of Tarragona both the order of the Mass itself and the custom of psalm-singing and ministering shall be maintained.

## II. That litanies be celebrated after Pentecost from Thursday through Saturday

Concerning the litanies: once the solemnity of Pentecost has been completed, during the following week abstinence shall be observed for these three days, from Thursday through Saturday.

## III. Concerning the celebration of the second litanies on the Kalends of November

Likewise, the second litanies are to be celebrated on the Kalends of November, with this condition observed: if a Sunday falls during those same days, they shall begin in another week on Thursday, according to the observance of the preceding abstinence, and shall conclude when Mass has been celebrated on Saturday evening. Yet during those days we have decreed that people abstain from meat and wine.

## IV. That baptism be administered only at Easter and the Nativity of the Lord, except to those who are ill

Concerning the baptism of catechumens, this has been established: because fewer people come to be baptized at the solemnity of Easter or at the Nativity of the Lord, when the celebration of the solemnity is greater, only the sick are to be baptized at the other solemnities; baptism is not to be denied to them at whatever time is suitable.

## V. That an infant one day old be baptized if in danger

[Col. 0314C]

Concerning little children who have recently been born from their mother’s womb, it was decided to establish that if they are weak, as commonly happens, and do not desire their mother’s milk, they are to be baptized even on the very day on which they were born, if they are brought forward.

## VI. That married men, from the bishop down to the subdeacon, live with a witness

Concerning the conduct of life, from the bishop down to the subdeacon: if any married men have been ordained after undertaking the office of honor, they are not to avail themselves of the assistance of another without that brother’s testimony. They are not to live with the woman who was formerly their wife; but if they wish to live with her, they are to avail themselves of the assistance of another brother, by whose testimony their life may appear more above reproach.  
[Note: [Col. 0313] This canon has been taken from Ae.; in the other codices it conveys neither proper sense nor syntax.]

## VII. That those ordained without wives not have unrelated women in their household

[Col. 0314D]

Concerning those who are ordained without wives and have households: after having a brother living with them as a witness to their manner of life, they must not allow their property to be managed by any female person whatsoever. They must arrange their household either through a boy or through a friend. If, however, they have a mother or sister in the household, their property is to be safeguarded through those women, according to the statutes of the earlier canons.

## VIII. Concerning laymen who take a widow or a divorced woman, so that they are not admitted to the clergy

If any layman, after his wife, has intercourse with another woman of whatever condition, he is in no way to be admitted to the clergy.

## IX. Concerning those who do not receive public penance but only the viaticum, so that they may be promoted to the clergy

But a man who, overcome by the weakness of illness, has received the blessing of penance—which we designate as the viaticum—through communion, and afterward, having recovered, has not publicly submitted himself in the church to the beginning of penance, is to be admitted to the clergy if he is not held guilty of prohibited vices.

## X. Concerning the discernment of penitents: who can and who cannot be promoted to ecclesiastical orders

[Note: [Col. 0315B] This canon is taken from Ae., since it is absent from A. and the others.]

Those who receive penance while in danger, confessing no manifest crimes but merely proclaiming themselves sinners—if they recover, such persons may even attain ecclesiastical ranks through uprightness of conduct. But those who receive penance in such a way that they publicly confess having committed some mortal sin can in no way attain the clergy or ecclesiastical honors, because they have branded themselves by their own confession.

## XI. That the Lord’s Prayer be said every evening and morning

[Note: [Col. 0315B] In the other codices, except Ae., this canon is numbered tenth [Col. 0316B], because the preceding canon is absent from them.]

It has pleased us that every day, after Matins and Vespers, the priest recite the Lord’s Prayer.

John, bishop, in the name of Christ, have signed. Frontinianus, bishop, in the name of Christ, have signed. Paul, bishop, in the name of Christ, have signed. # XLI. FIRST COUNCIL OF ZARAGOZA, OF TWELVE BISHOPS, ON THE FOURTH NONES OF OCTOBER

[Col. 0315]

[Col. 0315B] The bishops Fitadius [U., Hitadius], Delphinus, Eutychius, Ampelius, Auxentius, Lucius, Itacius [U., Etacius], Splendonius [B. R., Splendinius], Valerius, Symposius, Cartherius, and Idacius [U., Hidacius] were seated in the secretariat at Zaragoza. It was said by all: “Let the decrees be read.” Bishop Lucius read.

## I. That faithful women be separated from gatherings of unrelated men

[Col. 0315C]

That all women of the Catholic Church and the faithful be separated from the reading and gatherings of unrelated men; nor should other women come to those who read for the sake either of teaching or of learning, since the Apostle commands this. All the bishops said: “Anathema to those who do not observe this decision of the council.”

## II. That no one fast on Sundays, nor be absent from the church during Lent

He also read: “Let no one fast on Sunday because of the season, persuasion, or superstition; and during the days of Lent let them not be absent from the churches, nor let those who persist in these suspicions inhabit hiding places in bedrooms or mountains. Instead, let them observe the example and command of the priests, and let them not gather at other estates for the purpose of holding assemblies.” All the bishops said: “Let him be anathema who commits this.”

## III. That one who receives the Eucharist in the church but does not consume it there be anathematized

He also read: “If anyone is proved to have received the grace of the Eucharist in the church but not to have consumed it there, let him be anathema forever.” All the bishops said: “It is approved.”

## IV. That during the three weeks before Epiphany no one withdraw from the church

[Col. 0316B]

He also read: “During the twenty-one days from the sixteenth day before the Kalends of January up to the day of Epiphany, which is the eighth day before the Ides of January, no one may be absent from the church on any of the successive days, nor hide in houses, nor withdraw to an estate, nor seek the mountains, nor walk barefoot; instead, they are to hasten to the church. Whoever does not observe this among those who have received the decree, let him be anathema forever.”  
[Note: [Col. 0315D] Ae., T. 2, “whoever does not observe these decrees, let him be anathema.”]  
All the bishops said: “Let him be anathema.”

## V. That those deprived of communion by their own bishops not be received by others

It was also read: “Those who have been separated from the Church through the discipline or judgment of a bishop are not to be received by other bishops. If bishops knowingly do this, let them not have communion.” All the bishops said: “Whoever commits this shall not have the communion of the bishops.”

## VI. That a cleric who wishes to become a monk for the sake of license be excommunicated

[Col. 0316D]

He also read: “If any cleric, because of presumed luxury and vanity, voluntarily withdraws from his office and wishes to appear more observant of the law as a monk than as a cleric, he is to be expelled from the Church in such a way that he is not received unless, by begging and observing [T. 1, 2, U., ‘by imploring’] for a very long time, he has made satisfaction.” All the bishops said: “Let it be done so.”

## VII. That no one assume for himself the name of teacher unless it has been granted to him

[Col. 0317A]

It was also read: “Let no one assume for himself the name of teacher except those persons to whom it has been granted, according to what is written.” All the bishops said: “It is approved.”

## VIII. That consecrated virgins not be veiled before the age of forty

[Note: [Col. 0317A] This canon is absent from U.]

[Col. 0318A]

It was also read: “Virgins who have vowed themselves to God are not to be veiled unless they have reached the proven age of forty years, as certified by the priest.” All the bishops said: “It is approved.”

# XLII. SECOND COUNCIL OF ZARAGOZA, IN THE SEVENTH YEAR OF KING RECARED, ERA 630

[Col. 0317]

[Col. 0317B]  
[Note: [Col. 0317] [ [Col. 0317] This note is printed at the foot of column 317, but its callout letter, a, does not appear in the text.] This council is absent from all the codices except Ae., from which it has been taken.]

## I.

When we had gathered in the city of Zaragoza, in the province of Tarragona, in the name of God, with the permission of the glorious and most holy prince, King Recared, in the seventh year of his reign, deliberating out of fear of God, it pleased the holy and venerable synod that the priests who had been converted from the Arian heresy to the holy Catholic Church, who had maintained the holy and pure faith and a most chaste life, should, after receiving again the blessing of the presbyterate, minister in holiness and purity. But the others who had neglected to fulfill or maintain the life described above are to be deposed from office and remain among the clergy. The same has also been established concerning deacons as concerning priests.

## II.

The holy synod decreed that relics found anywhere from the Arian heresy are to be brought forth by the priests in whose churches they are discovered and presented to the bishops, and tested by fire. If any such relics are concealed by anyone and are discovered, the concealers are to be separated from the assembly of the most holy Catholic Church.

## III.

The holy synod decreed that bishops coming from the Arian heresy, if they have consecrated any churches under the name of the Catholic faith, are to have them consecrated again by a Catholic priest, since they have not yet received the blessing.

On the day of the Kalends of November, in the year stated above.
