Let a synod be held once a year, and let the judges and fiscal agents be present. Council of Toledo III, 353.

[Col. 0923] The judgment of the Council of Sardica, recited at the request of Bishop Novatus. Council of Carthage VI, 162.

A synod is to be convened every year. Council of Agde, 243.

The Synod of Arles is to be convened at the discretion of the metropolitan. Council of Arles II, 201.

### Concinnabula

Let there be no *concinnabula* or conspiracies among clerics, such as used to be formed under the patronage of laymen. Council of Narbonne, 660.

### Concupiscence

Concerning unconsummated concupiscence. Council of Neocaesarea, 25.

### Persons conditionally manumitted

Persons conditionally manumitted are not to be ordained except with the consent of their patrons. Council of Braga II, 622.

### Confessors

Letters of communion are to be given to confessors. Council of Elvira, 286.

Those who carry letters from confessors are to receive others. Council of Arles I, 195.

### Marriage

A female catechumen is to have neither long-haired men nor men who wear ashes. Council of Elvira, 292.

The marriages of heretics are to be avoided. Council of Laodicea, 55.

The daughters of clerics are not to be joined in marriage to unbelievers. Council of Carthage III, 129.

Married men, from the bishop down to the subdeacon, are not to live without a witness. Council of Gerunda, 301.

Concerning the daughter of a bishop, presbyter, or deacon, if she has been consecrated and takes a husband. Council of Braga II, 619.

Concerning those whom their parents, from infancy, have committed to the clerical office, if they later wish to marry. Council of Toledo II, 329.

A vowed woman who takes a husband is not to be admitted to penance unless her husband has departed. Council of Toledo I, 325.

Deacons, like the bishop and presbyter, ought to abstain from marital relations, but they are not nevertheless to repudiate marriage. Letter of Leo to Rustic., 104.

A believing woman who has left an adulterous husband who is a believer and marries another is to be prohibited from marrying. Council of Elvira, 283.

Faithful women who join themselves to pagans are to be excommunicated. Council of Arles I, 196.

Women who had married while their husbands were in captivity, when those husbands return from captivity, ought to be reunited with their former husbands, so that each may recover what belongs to him. Letter of Leo to Nicetas, 111.

Women who, having left their husbands, marry others are not to receive communion even at the end of life. Council of Elvira, 283.

A husband whose wife has committed adultery is not to take another wife. Council of Arles I, 196.

A woman is not to take a husband against her will. Council of Toledo II, 350.

He who appears to have taken a wife in marriage while she was captive is not judged to be culpable. Letter of Leo to Nicetas, 111.

Parents who break the pledges of betrothal are to abstain for a period of three years. Council of Elvira, 290.

Catholic girls are not to be given in marriage to heretics or to Jews. Council cited above, 284.

Betrothed girls cannot enter into the rights of marriage with another man. Letter of Siricius to Himerius, 4.

Girls who, not under compulsion but of their own will, have undertaken a resolve of virginity commit an offense when they marry, even if they have not yet been consecrated. Letter of Leo to Rustic., 106.

Those who have already been consecrated, if they later marry, commit a grave crime. Letter cited above, ibid.

Those who enter into marriage with a vowed virgin are to be deprived of communion. Council of Barcelona II, 658.

Those who join their daughters to pagan priests are not to receive communion even at the end of life. Council of Elvira, 285.

Those who marry their stepdaughters are not to communicate even at the end of life. Council cited above, 292.

Those who are ordained without wives are not to have unrelated women in their house. Council of Gerunda, 301.

If a man who has a wife has a concubine, let him not receive communion. Council of Toledo I, [Col. 0924] 325.

Whoever gives his daughter in marriage to a man who has a concubine does not err. Letter of Leo to Rustic., 104.

A catechumen’s wife who has been abandoned, if she marries another, may be admitted to the baptismal font. Council of Elvira, 283.

An abandoned presbyter’s or deacon’s wife is not to join herself to another man. Council of Orléans I, 247.

A religious daughter of a priest or deacon who has sinned and taken a husband is to receive communion only at the end of life. Council of Toledo I, 325.

Laymen who abandon their wives without proof of separation are to be excluded from communion with the Church. Council of Agde, 235.

If women do not wish to return to their former husbands, they are to be deprived of ecclesiastical communion as impious women. Letter of Leo to Nicetas, 111.

If the widow of a priest or Levite takes a husband, she is to receive communion only at the end of life. Council of Toledo I, 325.

If men who have returned from captivity have not been offended by the incontinence of their wives and wish to receive them back in marriage, they are to have free permission to do so. Letter of Leo to Nicetas, 111.

Carnal marriage is to be denied to subdeacons. Letter of Leo to Anastasius, 108.

Christian virgins are by no means to be given in marriage to pagans. Council of Elvira, 284.

### The bishop of Constantinople

He is to have the honor of primacy after the bishop of Rome. First Council of Constantinople, 61.

### Continence

Concerning those who practice continence and the use of cloaks. Council of Gangra, 30.

No one ought, on account of continence, to neglect his children. Council cited above, 31.

### Converts

During illness, converts are to receive the laying on of hands. Council of Arles I, 195.

### Banquets

They are not to be held in churches. Council of Carthage III, 131.

### Crimes

In ordinations, it is not to be believed that crimes are removed. Letter of Innocent to Rufus and Eusebius, 32.

### Curiales

They are not to be admitted to the clergy. Letter of Innocent to all the bishops in Toulouse, 34.

They are not to become clerics. Letter of the same to Victoricus, 15.

### Cyril

His letters to Nestorius. Council of Ephesus, 79.

His rescript to the Sixth Council of Carthage. Sixth Council of Carthage, 168.

D

**Demons.** See Devil.

**Demon-possessed persons.** Those ensnared by demonic possession or other afflictions may not handle the sacred ministries. *General Decree of Gelasius*, 133.

**Pope Damasus.** His letter to Paulinus, bishop of Antioch, 1.

**The dead.** The bodies of the dead are in no way to be buried inside the basilica of the saints. *Council of Braga I*, 605. One must not rashly judge those who have already departed to the Lord. Letter of Anastasius to the Emperor Anastasius, 137. No basilica constructed in the name of the dead is to be dedicated. *General Decree of Gelasius*, 134.

**Informers.** Informers in graver cases are not to receive communion even at the end of their penance; in lesser cases they are to do penance for five years. *Council of Elvira*, 293. See Accusers.

**Betrothal.** Betrothed girls who have been violated by others are to be returned to those to whom they had previously been betrothed. *Council of Ancyra*, 20.

**The consecrated woman.** Concerning a consecrated woman who sins or who marries. *Council of Braga II*, 620. A consecrated virgin who turns to earthly marriage is to be deprived of communion. *Council of Barcelona II*, 658.

**The Devil.** Those who say that the Devil comes from himself or from chaos, and has a nature of his own, are condemned. Letter of Leo to [Col. 0925] Thuribius of Astorga, 92. Those who say that human bodies are the Devil’s creations and are formed by demons in the womb are condemned. Letter of Leo to Thuribius of Astorga, 92. How we may avoid his snares and cunning. Rescript of Flavian to Pope Leo, 51.

**Deacons.** They are not to be deposed by one bishop alone. *Council of Seville I*, 642. They are not to be ordained before the age of twenty-five. *Council of Arles III*, 203. The obstinate or proud are to be admonished by three bishops. *Council of Carthage I*, 119. When questioned before a presbyter, they are to answer. *Council of Carthage IV*, 146. They are not to sit before a presbyter or distribute the Eucharist. *Council of Arles II*, 201. A deacon overtaken by a bodily sin shall refrain from the ministry. *Council of Neocaesarea*, 26. Concerning those who have been ordained presbyters or deacons without examination. *Council of Braga II*, 618. Concerning presbyters or deacons who are denounced after ordination. *Ibid.*, 619. Concerning the use by deacons of a single orarium, neither ornamented but plain. *Council of Toledo IV*, 379. A deacon or presbyter who has committed a capital crime is to be expelled from office and communion. *Council of Orléans I*, 246. A deacon or presbyter who has committed a capital crime is to be deposed from the honor of office and confined in a monastery. *Council of Epaon*, 264. Their ordination is to be celebrated on Holy Saturday, that is, on Sunday. Letter of Leo to Dioscorus, 118. They are to show the greatest humility and reverence toward their bishop. *Council of Mérida*, 671. They are to administer the Eucharist at the command of a presbyter. *Council of Carthage IV*, 146. Those chosen for the diaconate are to remain chaste. *Council of Braga II*, 622. They are in no way to sit in the presbyters’ assembly. *Council of Braga I*, 655. They may not sit in the presbytery. *General Decree of Gelasius*, 131. At a presbyter’s command they are to sit. *Council of Carthage IV*, 146. They are to observe their proper measure according to the decrees of the Fathers. *General Decree of Gelasius*, 131. They are not to give the body of Christ to presbyters or receive communion before presbyters. *Council of Nicaea*, 5. They are to offer nothing without a presbyter. *Council of Arles I*, 197. A deacon may not sit without being ordered to do so. *Council of Braga II*, 622. No one is to be ordained deacon before his twenty-fifth year. *Council of Orléans II*, 253. They are to obey a presbyter as they do a bishop. *Council of Carthage IV*, 146. At what age they are to be ordained. *Council of Agde*, 232. How they are to be instituted. *Council of Carthage IV*, 141. Those proved to have sinned before receiving the honor of office, if they confess the crime, are to do penance for three years; if another exposes them, they are to receive lay communion after five years. *Council of Elvira*, 293. Those who have sacrificed must cease from every sacred ministry. *Council of Ancyra*, 17. One who has served as a soldier after baptism is not to be promoted to the diaconate. *Council of Toledo I*, 323. Those who have taken widows are not to become deacons. *Council of Toledo I*, 322. There are to be seven, however large the city may be. *Council of Neocaesarea*, 26. If they are accused, how many bishops are to hear them. *Council of Carthage III*, 128. If, when they are ordained, they protested that they wished to have wives and could not remain continent, they are to remain in the ministry. *Council of Ancyra*, 20. If they incur guilt, they are to be heard by three bishops. *Council of Carthage II*, 124. They are to wear a white garment only during the time of their office. *Council of Carthage IV*, 146. They are to have a good testimony concerning their life. *Council of Toledo IV*, 575. See Levites.

**Deaconesses.** Deaconesses are not to be ordained. *Council of Orange*, 222. They are not to be ordained unless they are forty years old; anathema is pronounced upon them if afterward they give themselves to marriage. [Col. 0925] *Council of Chalcedon*, 102.

**Dictinius.** Corrections to be made in the book of Dictinius. Letter of Leo to Thuribius of Astorga, 94.

**Sunday.** See Lord’s Day.

**Bimarried men.** They are not to be admitted to the clergy. Letter of Innocent to Bishop Felix, 19. They are not permitted to enter the clerical order. Letter of Siricius to Eumerius, 7. They are not to be promoted to the priesthood. *Council of Arles*, 204. They are not to be consecrated or ordained. *Council of Valence*, 207. They are to devote themselves to prayers and fasts; and, according to the remission granted, communion is to be restored to them. *Council of Laodicea*, 51.

**Diocese.** A diocese that has never had a bishop is not to have one. *Council of Carthage II*, 122.

**Those in despair.** Whoever escapes an attempted killing shall remain for two months entirely excluded both from the fellowship of Catholics and from the body and sacred blood of Christ. *Council of Toledo XVI*, 570.

**Divination.** Those who consult divinations are to be expelled from communion. *Council of Orléans I*, 250.

**Diviners.** They are to be publicly flogged and sold. *Council of Narbonne*, 662. If men or women diviners are found in anyone’s house, or if anyone thereafter dares to consult them about their vain incantations and does not wish to announce this publicly, they are not only to be suspended from the Church but are also to pay six ounces of gold to the count of the city. *Council of Narbonne*, 622.

**Divorce.** Those who leave their wives after a divorce has taken place are to be excommunicated. *Council of Toledo XI*, 498. A divorced woman is not to be joined to another man. *Council of Milevis*, 186. A divorced man is not to be admitted with another wife. *Council of Milevis*, 186.

**Teacher.** No one is to assume the title of teacher when it has not been granted to him. *Council of Zaragoza I*, 304.

**The Lord’s Day.** Sundays are to be observed, and on them people are to abstain from work. *Council of Orléans II*, 219. Concerning Sundays and Pentecost, so that on them we may pray standing. *Council of Nicaea*, 7. Every person, whether freeborn or enslaved, Goth, Roman, and so forth, is to do no work on Sunday; nor are oxen to be yoked. *Council of Narbonne*, 659.

**Donations.** The donations of those who oppress the poor are to be rejected by priests. *Council of Carthage IV*, 151. Donations, sales, or exchanges of ecclesiastical property made by bishops without the consent and subscription of the clergy are to be invalid. *Council of Carthage IV*, 145.

**Donatus.** Concerning Donatus, bishop of the Novatianists. Letter of Leo to the Africans, 114.

E
## Church. Churches

Concerning those who presume to strip altars or remove the church’s lamps. Council of Toledo XIII, 518.

Concerning the reception or communion of the guilty in the church. Council of Toledo XII, 494.

Concerning the service and discipline of the church’s freedmen. Council of Toledo IX, 453.

Concerning the administration of church property. Council of Braga II, 616.

Concerning the governance of ecclesiastical property. Council of Braga II, 616.

From the revenues of the church or the offerings of the faithful, four portions are to be made. General Decree of Gelasius, 133.

Concerning the repair of churches and various other matters. Council of Toledo XVI, 571.

The church, together with its property, is subject to the bishop’s administration. Council of Toledo III, 353.

A ruined church, if it has been restored from its foundations, is to be consecrated. [Col. 0926] Letter of Vigilius to Profuturus, 155.

While churches are harassed by difficulties, a defender is to be requested from the ruler. Council of Carthage V, 156.

How the cases of churches are to be brought to an end. Council of Auvergne II, 277.

The alms of churches are not to be alienated. Council of Auvergne II, 276.

Churches consecrated by Arian bishops are to be consecrated again by a Catholic priest. Council of Zaragoza II, 305.

Those who plunder church property are to be excluded. Council of Auvergne I, 268.

Three equal portions are to be made from ecclesiastical property. Council of Braga I, 603.

Outside a necessity, no one may alienate church property. Council of Toledo III, 349.

Ecclesiastical possessions are not to be alienated. Council of Orléans II, 235.

Those who defraud the church are to be deprived of communion. Council of Auvergne I, 270.

Fruits are to be given in the church and nowhere else. Council of Gangra, 29.

Those born of the church’s freedmen, and of free persons, are not to withdraw from the church’s service. Council of Toledo IX, 452.

Those who have sold anything from the vessels used in the church’s ministry are not to be regarded as holding ecclesiastical office. Council of Braga II, 617.

Contention must be avoided with the greatest care in the church. Letter of Anastasius to the emperor Anastasius, 137.

Pictures are not to be made in the church. Council of Elvira, 287.

In churches it is not permitted to spread couches or hold a communal meal (*agape*). Council of Laodicea, 54.

The thirty-year prescription is to be observed with regard to church property. Letter of Gelasius to the bishops of Sicily, 136.

The church’s freedmen may not transfer ownership of anything from their property to another. Council of Toledo IX, 453.

If the church’s freedmen do not wish to return to it, all their little property is to be applied to the church’s right. Council of Toledo IX, 453.

No one may presume to take another church’s property. Council of Auvergne II, 276.

No one is to be expelled from the church without remedy or hope of pardon. Council of Epaon, 265.

A church that has been held by a bishop for thirty years is to remain immovable in his possession. Council of Chalcedon, 102.

During the days of Lent no one is to be absent from the church. Council of Zaragoza I, 303.

What discretion the rulers of churches must exercise, lest their subjects incur the charge of homicide through undisciplined discipline. Council of Toledo XI, 480.

What division is to be made of property acquired between the church and the priest’s heirs. Council of Toledo IX, 449.

Property bestowed upon churches is to remain under their ownership. Council of Toledo VI, 407.

Those who place defamatory pamphlets in a church are to be anathematized. Council of Elvira, 290.

Those who enter a church and do not communicate are to be excommunicated. Council of Toledo I, 324.

Those who, when ordered by the bishop, refuse to leave the church for any fault are to be received into pardon only later. Council of Huesca, 315.

What is to be observed in governing churches established among barbarian peoples. Council of Constantinople I, 61.

Whatever clerics have held by right of the church is to return to the church after their death. Council of Toledo II, 331.

That it performs an embassy for Christ while praying for the church’s peace. Letter of Anastasius to the emperor Anastasius, 137.

The rulers of the church are not to concern themselves with their own rights more than with ecclesiastical rights. Council of Braga III, 635.

Church property is to be properly administered by bishops. Letter of Gelasius to the bishops of Sicily, 136.

Church property is not to be alienated without the bishop’s consent. Council of Orléans II, 258.

Church property is not to be alienated. Council of Epaon, 263.

Church property is not to be alienated, but is to be given to clerics, monks, or pilgrims solely for their use. Letter of Symmachus to Caesar, 14.

Church property entrusted for use is not to be protected by the passage of time. Council of Agde, 241. [Col. 0927]

The sale of ecclesiastical property made by a bishop without the clerics’ subscription is invalid. Council of Carthage IV, 145.

If it is said that something was given from church property as a payment, the reason for the payment is to be investigated. Council of Toledo IX, 449.

During the three weeks before Epiphany no one is to withdraw from the church. Council of Zaragoza I, 303.

A sale of church property made by parish priests is to be considered empty and void. Council of Agde, 240.

### Ecclesiastical property

It is not to be alienated by the bishop without consulting the metropolitan. Council of Carthage V, 155.

How it is to be held by the bishop. Council of Carthage IV, 145.

How it is to be preserved. Council of Antioch, 48.

See *Church*.

### King Egica

His address to the Fathers of the Fifteenth Council of Toledo. Council of Toledo XV, 539.

His address to the Fathers of the Fifteenth Council of Toledo. Council of Toledo XV, 557.

His address to the Fathers of the Seventeenth Council of Toledo. Council of Toledo XVII, 587.

A law issued in confirmation of the Sixteenth Council of Toledo. Council of Toledo XVI, 581.

### Elections

The people may not conduct the election of those who are called to the priesthood; rather, the judgment is to belong to the bishops. Council of Braga II, 613.

### Demoniacs

They are not to be promoted to the clergy. Council of Orange, 221.

Those who have been baptized may communicate. Council of Orange, 220.

They and the catechumens are to be questioned concerning baptism. Council of Orange, 221.

The faithful who are at the point of death may receive communion. Council of Elvira, 287.

Their name is not to be recited at the altar with the offering. Council of Elvira, 286.

If they are at the end of life, they are to be baptized; if they are faithful, they are to receive communion. Council of Elvira, 287.

Every day exorcists are to lay hands upon them. Council of Carthage IV, 151.

They are to sweep the pavements of the houses of God. Council of Carthage IV, 151.

Those who have been baptized and afterward become demoniacs are not to be signed by priests or deacons. Letter of Innocent to Decentius, 12.

The exorcists are to provide daily food for demoniacs who sit in the house of God. Council of Carthage IV, 151.

### Epirus

The metropolitan of Epirus is to report to the bishop of Thessalonica concerning the elected man whom he is about to ordain bishop. Letter of Leo to Anastasius, 109.

### Episcopate

Concerning an invasion of a vacant church. Council of Braga II, 615.

Unlawful persons are not to be promoted to the episcopate. Letter of Leo to the Africans, 113.

No one is to attain the episcopate except through the ecclesiastical grades. Letter of Celestine to the bishops of Gaul, 47.

No one is to obtain the episcopate by payment or rewards. Council of Auvergne II, 276.

No reward is to be accepted for the episcopate. Letter of Hormisdas to the bishops throughout Spain, 148.

### Bishops

When summoned to a synod, they are to attend its celebration. Council of Laodicea, 56.

Every year bishops are to visit their diocese. Council of Tarragona, 297.

Regarding familiarity with foreign women, bishops, priests, and deacons are to observe the statutes of the earlier canons. Council of Orléans I, 249.

Neighboring bishops are annually to seek information from their primate concerning the sacred solemnity of Easter. Council of Zaragoza III, 307.

Neighboring bishops are to reside in the royal city each month of the year. Council of Toledo VI, 418.

When bishops have gathered in council, they are to be instructed by their primate concerning the solemnity of Easter. Council of Carthage III, 134.

Confession of faith made by the Gothic bishops at the Third Council of Toledo, 342.

When they are at variance, the synod is to reconcile them. [Col. 0927] Council of Carthage IV, 144.

Together with the judges, they are to destroy idols. Council of Toledo III, 352.

Those defiled by, and involved in intimate familiarity with, any women are to be deprived of the dignity of their place and order. Council of Toledo VIII, 434.

Concerning the condemned presumption of certain bishops who, proceeding to the church on the feast days of martyrs, are carried in little chairs by white-clad deacons, with relics hung around their necks. Council of Braga III, 633.

Concerning disagreement in the judgment of bishops. Council of Braga II, 616.

Concerning bishops who were negligent toward heretics. Council of Milevis, 188.

Concerning bishops who, after being ordained, are not received. Council of Ancyra, 22.

Concerning the ordination of bishops. Council of Toledo IV, 373.

Concerning the primacy of bishops. Council of Braga I, 603.

Concerning church property, how it is to be held by bishops; and concerning church slaves, how they are to be manumitted by the bishop. Council of Agde, 231.

Concerning the will of bishops. Council of Epaon, 263.

Deposed bishops are not to appeal to the emperor. Council of Antioch, 45.

The discretion of the authority that bishops may exercise in monasteries. Council of Toledo IV, 381.

Two bishops are not to make a bishop. Council of Orange, 221.

A sentence of bishops against an absent person is invalid. Council of Carthage IV, 143.

Bishops and ministers are to abstain from wives. Council of Elvira, 287.

Bishops are not to admit another bishop’s excommunicated person to communion. Council of Elvira, 290.

Bishops, priests, and deacons are not to pursue business or markets. Council of Elvira, 285.

How the funerals of bishops are to be conducted. Council of Toledo VI, 416.

The bishops of the province of Galicia are not to conduct exactions. Council of Toledo VI, 416.

Gallican bishops are not to be investigated in Gaul. Council of Vaison I, 223.

What heretical and schismatic bishops must observe if they come to the Catholic faith. Council of Riez, 214.

In summoning provincial bishops by the bishop of Thessalonica, moderation is to be observed. Letter of Leo to Anastasius, 109.

An unjust condemnation of bishops is to be reconsidered by a synod. Council of Carthage IV, 145.

In their own church they are to have an archpriest, an archdeacon, and a chief cleric. Council of Mérida, 671.

They are to take nothing from church property, and the neighboring founders of churches are to provide care. Council of Toledo IX, 447.

Those are not to be regarded as bishops whom neither the clergy elected, nor the people sought, nor the provincial bishops consecrated. Letter of Leo to Rusticus of Narbonne, 104.

They are not to invade, bypassing a synod, what they could have reclaimed. Council of Milevis, 187.

When not invited, they are not to go beyond their dioceses. Council of Constantinople I, 60.

Neither laymen, nor bigamists, nor husbands of widows, but irreproachable men are to be ordained bishops. Letter of Leo to Anastasius, 108.

Bishops may not perform church consecrations except on Sundays. Council of Zaragoza III, 307.

Bishops, priests, and deacons may not keep dogs for hunting or hawks. Council of Epaon, 261.

A bishop may not ordain another church’s cleric in his own church. Council of Sardica, 40.

Bishops may not ordain clerics in another province. Council of Antioch, 46.

They may not minister if they have been deposed from office. Council of Antioch, 43.

Translations of bishops are not permitted. Council of Carthage III, 133.

They are not to be ordained without the counsel of the metropolitans and neighboring bishops. Council of Laodicea, 52.

No bishop may ordain a deacon or priest who is ignorant of letters; but if any have been ordained, they are to be compelled to learn. Council of Narbonne, 661. [Col. 0928]

At the time when they are to be ordained, all bishops and rulers of churches are to promise under guarantee that they will live as justly as possible. Council of Toledo XI, 181.

Agreements made between bishops are to be observed. Council of Carthage I, 119.

They are not to receive more than a third from the parishes. Council of Tarragona, 297.

At what age bishops and priests are to be consecrated. Council of Agde, 233.

How they are to be ordained. Council of Carthage IV, 139.

How they are to be ordained, so that they are ordained by all the bishops who remain in the province, or at least by three gathered together for this purpose. Council of Nicaea, 3.

How they are to be consecrated. Council of Carthage IV, 141.

Which bishops attended the First Council of Arles. Council of Arles I, 197.

Those who act contrary to the statutes are to be deprived of their honor. Council of Turin, 210.

Those who receive another’s excommunicated person incur guilt. Council of Orange, 220.

Those who have been unlawfully ordained are to be removed, and there are not to be two bishops in one church. Letter of Hilary to Ascanias, 123.

Those who have estates in another province may remain there for a fixed period. Council of Sardica, 39.

Those who have built a basilica not on their own property but in another’s diocese are not to presume to dedicate it. Council of Orange, 220.

Those who were retained after the proceedings of the synod at Carthage in order to complete the remaining business. Council of Milevis, 189.

Those who excommunicate either innocent persons or persons for very minor causes are to be admonished by letters from the neighboring bishops of any province. Council of Agde, 230.

Those who have gone to the emperor without letters from the metropolitan are to be deprived of communion. Council of Antioch, 45.

What is to be done if bishops have a dispute among themselves concerning parishes. Council of Mérida, 669.

They may not convey church property by testament. Council of Agde, 240.

If bishops wish to give something from their church’s property to their friends, slaves, or freedmen. Council of Mérida, 677.

Bishops are to grant freedom to their servile clerics. Council of Toledo IX, 452.

If bishops are accused, the matter is to be settled before the metropolitan of a neighboring province. Council of Antioch, 46.

If they come to another bishop’s church to visit it, they are to be received according to their rank. Council of Carthage IV, 145.

They are to govern their own dioceses and not go into others. Council of Constantinople I, 59.

### Bishop

Another bishop may not invade a parish. Council of Auvergne I, 269.

No one is to receive chrism from another bishop. Council of Vaison I, 225.

No bishop is to be ordained without the metropolitan. Council of Riez, 216.

He is to return on the day of the council. Council of Carthage V, 156.

He is accountable if widows or religious women are subjected to the familiar associations of clerics. Council of Carthage IV, 152.

At the bishop’s table, the divine Scriptures are to be read. Council of Toledo III, 350.

He is not to presume upon another’s parish. Council of Carthage II, 124.

He is not to presume upon another’s diocese. Council of Braga II, 614.

He cannot alienate church property. Council of Agde, 240.

He is not to usurp another’s congregations. Council of Carthage III, 130.

He is not to promote another’s cleric. Council of Auvergne II, 274.

He is to rebuke another’s sinful cleric. Council of Vaison, 226.

He is not to dare retain or ordain another’s cleric. Council of Carthage III, 130.

He is to travel through his diocese, and twenty days before Easter the catechumens are to be taught the Creed. Council of Braga II, 609.

He is not to impose forced services or levies in the diocese. Council of Toledo III, 354.

Before he is ordained, he is to know the canons. Council of Carthage III, 127.

He is to hear cases in the presence of clerics. Council of Carthage IV, 144.

He is not to presume to ordain another’s cleric. Council of Orange, 219.

He is not to appoint clerics without testimony from the clergy and the people. Council of Carthage IV, 144.

A person who ordains a cleric contrary to the statutes is to be suspended from celebrating the offices for six months; if he presumes to celebrate Masses during that period, he is to be deprived for an entire year of communion with all the brethren. Council of Orléans II, 253.

A stubborn or proud man is to be heard by twelve fellow bishops. Council of Carthage I, 119.

Together with the judges, he is to correct the murderers of children with stricter discipline. Council of Toledo III, 352.

He is not to move from one city to another. Council of Chalcedon, 99.

Concerning a contemptuous bishop. Council of Braga II, 615.

Concerning a bishop whose see is vacant by necessity. Council of Braga II, 615.

Concerning the funeral of a dying bishop. Council of Valence, 319.

From the possessions of the churches, except for a third of the offerings, the bishop is to take nothing. Council of Toledo IV, 377.

He is not to pass from an ignoble place to a noble one through ambition, except by the sentence of a synod. Council of Carthage IV, 144.

Concerning persons who, after going to their metropolitan to present their affairs, are not to be excommunicated by their own bishop. Council of Toledo XIII, 524.

Concerning the ordination of a bishop. Council of Braga II, 613.

Concerning a bishop’s presumption regarding church property. Council of Braga II, 616.

Concerning the fulfillment of a promise from church property. Council of Toledo IV, 378.

Concerning a certain bishop of the Acephali. Council of Seville II, 645.

Concerning the removal of the man whom two persons rashly presumed to ordain improperly. Council of Riez, 213.

Concerning the inquiry to be made by bishops each year in the parishes. Council of Toledo IV, 378.

Concerning a seditious bishop. Council of Braga II, 615.

After a bishop’s death, no one is to presume to take anything from his property or the church’s. Council of Valence, 317.

After a bishop’s death, no one is to seize his possessions. Council of Auvergne II, 275.

He may leave his own property to his heirs; but what he acquired belongs to the church. Council of Agde, 239.

On Sunday he must not be absent from the church. Council of Orléans I, 250.

He is to notify the diocesan priests and certain laymen by letter to assemble at the synod. Council of Tarragona, 298.

The bishop is to be ordained by election of the clergy or citizens, with the consent also of the metropolitan of the same province. Council of Auvergne I, 267.

He is to defer to the senior bishop and not presume to do anything without consulting the primate. Council of Milevis, 185.

Where and within what period an accused bishop is to be examined. Council of Carthage III, 127.

He is to protect both the poor and the sick. Council of Orléans I, 247.

He may dispose of a small amount even without the clerics’ consent. Council of Agde, 239.

He must not eradicate the church’s household. Council of Mérida, 673.

He is not to read pagan books. Council of Carthage IV, 143.

If he has no heirs, he is to make the church over which he presided his heir. Council of Agde, 237.

He may honor and enrich clerics striving toward perfection with church property. Council of Mérida, 672.

He is not to intrude into another’s diocese. Council of Orléans II, 256.

In his private chamber he is to have suitable testimony. Council of Toledo IV, 375.

In the assembly of the church he is to sit higher than the priests. Council of Carthage IV, 145.

In places where there has never been a bishop, no bishop is ever to be ordained. Council of Toledo XII, 494.

At the ordination of clerics he is to receive no advantage. Council of Braga II, 610.

He is not personally to undertake the care of the needy. Council of Carthage IV, 143. [Col. 0929]

He must not presume to ordain an unwilling or protesting man. Council of Orléans II, 253.

It is permitted for the bishop to sell fugitive church slaves. Council of Agde, 239.

It is permitted for the bishop to make one basilica from his parishes into a monastery. Council of Toledo III, 349.

He must not transfer himself to another city. Council of Sardica, 33.

He must not intrude into another city. Council of Antioch, 48.

A bishop must not be ordained without the counsel and presence of the metropolitan. Council of Braga II, 614.

He must not pass from one diocese to another. Council of Antioch, 48.

A bishop ordained by two bishops is not to be recognized. Council of Riez, 213.

He must not remain in another province. Council of Sardica, 38.

He may not appoint another as his successor before the end of his life. Council of Braga II, 615.

A bishop may not ordain a bishop without the metropolitan’s counsel. Council of Antioch, 47.

He may not appoint a successor for himself. Council of Antioch, 48.

He is not to have a guesthouse far from the church. Council of Carthage IV, 143.

He is not to be ordained from among the laity while the clerics of the churches are disregarded. Letter of Celestine to the bishops throughout Apulia and Calabria, 49.

He is not to be ordained in villages and hamlets. Council of Laodicea, 58.

He may not accept secular estates or cases. Council of Chalcedon, 98.

No bishop may depart from the Council of Arles. Council of Arles II, 201.

No one is to presume to claim another’s cleric for himself. Council of Carthage III, 135.

No bishop or cleric whatsoever may have in his house any woman other than the female relatives mentioned by the earlier canons. Council of Orléans II, 252.

No bishop is to leave his own church and transfer to another. Letter of Hilary to Ascanias, 122.

No bishop is to trample upon another bishop. Council of Arles I, 197.

No bishop is to depart from a council without consent or excuse himself from going to a council. Council of Orange, 223.

No bishop is to presume to judge cases on Sunday. Council of Tarragona, 296.

No bishop is to choose a successor for himself. Decree of Pope Hilary, 121.

No one is to be ordained from among the laity. Council of Sardica, 38.

No one is to be ordained bishop against his will. Letter of Leo to Anastasius, 108.

No one is to be ordained bishop against his will. Council of Auvergne II, 276.

No one is to be ordained without the metropolitan’s knowledge. Letter of Innocent to Victoricus, 15.

He is not to pass from province to province unless he has been invited. Council of Sardica, 33.

He is not to usurp the ordination of another’s cleric. Letter of Innocent to Victoricus, 14.

No layman is to be ordained bishop before a year has passed since his conversion. Council of Auvergne II, 275.

No one is to be ordained without consulting the metropolitan. Council of Carthage II, 125.

No one is to be ordained against the will of the people and clergy. Letter of Celestine to the bishops of Gaul, 48.

No one is to be ordained through money. Council of Chalcedon, 98.

No one is to approach the episcopate through ambition. Letter of Symmachus to Caesar, 140.

No one is to remain in a diocese after abandoning his see. Council of Carthage V, 155.

No one is to be ordained bishop without the metropolitan’s consent. Letter of Hilary to Ascanias, 122.

No one is to be appointed while the bishop is alive. Council of Auvergne II, 276.

He is to protect the poor and the people. Council of Toledo IV, 377.

As he travels through the diocese, he is to receive only two solidi. Council of Braga II, 609.

A place for celebrating the sacrifice is to be given to a visiting bishop. Council of Arles I, 197.

He is not to usurp another bishop’s congregations or boundaries. Council of Carthage I, 118.

The bishop of the principal see is not to be called “chief of the priests” or “high priest.” Council of Carthage III, 131. [Col. 0930]

After a bishop’s death, no one may say anything derogatory about him. Council of Mérida, 674.

He has authority to dispose of ecclesiastical property. Council of Antioch, 49.

If he wishes, he is to make cathedral priests and deacons for himself from his parish. Council of Mérida, 671.

He is to demand nothing for the consecration of a basilica. Council of Braga II, 610.

He is to accept nothing for chrism. Council of Braga II, 610.

He is not to accept gifts for judgments. Council of Tarragona, 297.

He is not to litigate over secular matters. Council of Carthage IV, 143.

For his own person he is to send to the council not a deacon but either an archpriest or a priest. Council of Mérida, 668.

The relatives of a dying bishop are to appropriate nothing from his property without the knowledge of the metropolitan and the bishops of the province. Council of Valence, 319.

At the time of his consecration he is to receive letters from those who ordained him. Council of Milevis, 186.

A provincial bishop is to inquire of his primate about Easter. Council of Carthage III, 125.

How a bishop, after receiving an admonition, is to come to his metropolitan. Council of Mérida, 668.

How he is to make freedmen. Council of Mérida, 676.

What food and furnishings he ought to use. Council of Carthage IV, 143.

What benefit a bishop may take from a church whose priest he has buried. Council of Toledo IX, 451.

What the bishop or his predecessor has arranged unlawfully is to be corrected by his successor. Decree of Hilary, 121.

Anyone who, after being admonished by the metropolitan, delays coming for a synod or episcopal ordination is to be deprived of communion with the church until the next synod. Council of Agde, 237.

Anyone who, after being warned by the metropolitan, does not come to the synod is to be excommunicated. Council of Tarragona, 297.

Anyone who brings a complaint against a bishop is not to be deprived of the church for that very assembly. Council of Orléans I, 246.

Anyone who has ordained foreign citizens is either to recall them to himself or obtain the favor of those with whom they live. Council of Orange, 219.

Anyone who, after the death of a bishop, presumes to take anything belonging to the church from the episcopal residence is to be anathematized. Council of Huesca, 316.

A bishop who was not ordained in the metropolitan city is to present himself to the metropolitan after two months. Council of Tarragona, 296.

Anyone unwilling to come to the synod will be guilty of violating fraternal agreement. Council of Braga II, 617.

Anyone who has more clerics is to give one to a person who requests one for ordination and is in need. Council of Carthage III, 136.

Anyone who does not acquiesce in the sentence of his own bishop is to appeal to the synod. Council of Vaison I, 225.

Anyone who buries a bishop is to take charge of his church. Council of Riez, 215.

Anyone ordained without the metropolitan’s knowledge must not be a bishop. Council of Arles II, 199.

What must be guarded against so that no one becomes a bishop through reward, and what sentence is to be imposed on one discovered, after receiving the honor, to have been ordained through reward. Council of Toledo XI, 481.

Wherever he is sitting, he is not to permit a priest to remain standing. Council of Carthage IV, 145.

When he is ordained with the metropolitan’s consent, three bishops are to ordain him. Council of Arles II, 199.

He is not to make another’s slave a cleric. Council of Orléans I, 246.

If he has been judged in any case, the Roman bishop is to be written to. Council of Sardica, 34.

If he is carried off by death before the condemned person’s absolution, his successor may absolve the corrected and penitent person. Council of Epaon, 264.

If he has charged a cleric or layman with a crime, he is to be brought to proof in the synod. Council of Carthage IV, 145.

If he has ordained foreign clerics or monks, he is to be separated from communion with the others. Council of Carthage V, 157.

If he acts contrary to his profession made in the council, he is to be deposed. Council of Carthage II, 126.

If he has granted small plots of land for cultivation, they are to be held without prejudice to the church’s right. Council of Orléans I, 248.

If, when the bishop is being elected, he has opponents, five priests are to assemble. Council of Carthage III, 134.

If he is ill, he is to send a representative to the synod in his place. Council of Carthage IV, 144.

If anything has been left to a bishop by anyone, it is to be counted among the church’s possessions. Council of Agde, 232.

If a bishop has been judged in any case and thinks that he has a good case, the Roman bishop is to be written to. Council of Sardica, 34.

If he appoints foreign or heretical heirs, he is to be anathematized. Council of Carthage V, 158.

If he dies intestate, the clerics are to make an inventory of his property, so that no one may take anything from it thereafter. Council of Tarragona, 298.

If he has a lawsuit against his brother bishop, neither of the two is to summon bishops from another province to judgment. Council of Sardica, 34.

If he establishes a monastery or enriches a parish church, he is to contribute a fourth part of the church’s property. Council of Toledo IX, 450.

If he ordains a cleric who has had a widow or a divorced wife, he is to be deposed. Council of Carthage IV, 149.

If, disregarding his own people, he refuses to come to the council, he is to lose both his people and his honor. Council of Carthage III, 135.

If he incurs guilt, he is to be heard by twelve bishops. Council of Carthage II, 124.

If, abandoning his own city, he seeks a larger see through ambition, and cannot obtain it, he is also to lose his own. Letter of Leo to Anastasius, 109.

If, after receiving the laying-on of hands, he does not go to his own church, he is to be excluded from communion. Council of Antioch, 47.

He is not to travel far without the metropolitan’s formal letter (*formata*). Council of Carthage III, 131.

No bishop is to be ordained without three bishops. Council of Arles I, 197.

He is to retain only the congregation in which he was ordained. Council of Carthage III, 137.

He ought to be concerned only with spiritual matters. Council of Carthage IV, 143.

He is not to take a third from the parish churches. Council of Mérida, 674.

He may confer the third of ecclesiastical property owed to him upon whomever he chooses. Council of Toledo IX, 450.

He is to strive to fulfill the divine testimony concerning himself. Council of Auvergne I, 270.

He is not to undertake the administration of wills. Council of Carthage IV, 143.

One bishop must not presume to ordain another bishop, because of arrogance. Council of Telepte, 191.

A vacant or wandering bishop who arrives at a vacant church is to be rejected. Council of Antioch, 46.

### Letters

Only chorepiscopi are to issue them. Council of Antioch, 44.

They are to be given to the needy. Council of Chalcedon, 101.

### King Ervig

Address to the Fathers of the Twelfth Council of Toledo. Council of Toledo XII, 487.

His exhortation to the Fathers of the Thirteenth Council of Toledo. Council of Toledo XIII, 511.

### Eucharist

It is not to be given to the dead. Council of Carthage III, 127.

Whoever receives the Eucharist and does not consume it is to be rejected as a sacrilege-worker. Council of Toledo I, 324.

Whoever receives the Eucharist in the church and does not consume it there is to be anathematized. Council of Zaragoza I, 303.

If anyone does not consume the Eucharist received from a priest, he is to be driven away as a sacrilege-worker. Council of Toledo XI, 482.

### Eulogies

It is not permitted to receive eulogies from heretics. Council of Laodicea, 55.

### Eunuchs

Concerning eunuchs who are made so by others, or who cut off their own natural organs. Council of Braga II, 618.

No one is to be ordained if he has voluntarily castrated himself. Council of Nicaea, 1.

### Eutyches

Concerning his blasphemies and his most just excommunication. Rescript of Flavian to Pope Leo, 52.

His blasphemies are condemned again. Letter of Hormisdas to the emperor Justin, 141.

His exile. Letter of Pope Leo to the emperor Augustus Marcian, 80.

Ignorance of the holy Scriptures made Eutyches a heretic. Letter of Leo to Flavian, 53.

### Eutyches and Nestorius

Confirmation of the condemnation of the sects of Eutyches and Nestorius. Council of Auvergne II, 273.

### Gospel

The holy Gospel is also to be read on Saturdays. Council of Laodicea, 53.

### The Excommunicated

They are not to be admitted to bring accusations against clerics. Council of Carthage VII, 179.

No one is to approach those who are excommunicated by priests. Council of Toledo I, 324.

No one is to receive into communion those who have been excommunicated by others. Council of Nicaea, 3.

A Catholic who appeals to unbelievers concerning cases is to be excommunicated. Council of Carthage IV, 151.

We cannot share communion with those deprived of communion who have died. Letter of Leo to Rusticus, 105.

No one is to receive another’s excommunicated person. Council of Arles II, 200.

An excommunicated person is to humble himself so that he may be reconciled more quickly. Council of Vaison I, 226.

He is not to come to the royal city without his bishop’s consent. Council of Chalcedon, 104.

No one is to presume to communicate with those excommunicated for heresy or any crime. Council of Braga I, 604.

It is not permitted to communicate with them. Council of Antioch, 42.

They are not to be deprived of the viaticum if they are hastening to depart from the world. Council of Nicaea, 5.

It is not permitted to communicate with the excommunicated, to enter their houses, or to pray with them. Council of Braga II, 628.

Anyone who goes to spectacles on a solemn feast day is to be excommunicated. Council of Carthage IV, 151.

Anyone who leaves while the bishop is speaking in the church is to be excommunicated. Council of Carthage IV, 144.

Anyone who receives another’s excommunicated person is to be excommunicated. Council of Carthage II, 123.

What is to be done concerning one whom a bishop has presumed to excommunicate on his sole testimony. Council of Carthage V, 180.

How those who have not observed the canons of the Council of Mérida are to be excommunicated. Council of Mérida, 677.

If anyone has been excommunicated by his own bishop, he is not to be received by others. Council of Antioch, 44.

If anyone of the powerful has despoiled someone and, when admonished by the bishop, has not restored what he took, he is to be excommunicated. Council of Toledo I, 324.

### Excommunication

Excommunication is not to be imposed for minor matters. Council of Auvergne II, 273.

### Exorcists

Those who have not yet been advanced by bishops ought not to perform exorcisms. Council of Laodicea, 54.

How they are to be appointed. Council of Carthage IV, 142.

### Exposed infants

Concerning exposed infants, the provision established long ago by the holy synod is to be observed. Council of Agde, 235; and Council of Valence I, 227–228.

Whoever finds an exposed infant is to notify the church. Council of Vaison I, 227.

Whoever, contrary to the established rule, reclaims an exposed infant is to be regarded as a murderer. Council of Vaison I, 228.

F
## Faustinus, bishop

His exposition to the Sixth Council of Carthage. Council of Carthage VI, 162. His opinion concerning the uncertainty of a certain chapter. Council of Carthage VI, 163. His response concerning matters established in the Church either by canon or by custom [Col. 0932]. Council of Carthage VI, 160.

## Felix, pope

Felix’s letter to Acacius, bishop of Constantinople, concerning the condemnation of his having dared to communicate with heretics, 128. His letter to the bishops throughout Sicily, 126. His letter to Bishop Zeno, 129.

## Women

Women shall not dare to write letters to laymen. Council of Elvira, 294. Foreign women shall not live together with clerics. Council of Carthage III, 130. Female believers shall separate themselves from gatherings of unrelated men. First Council of Zaragoza, 303. Which women ought to live with clerics. Letter of Siricius to Eumerius, 6. They shall not minister at the sacred altars or presume to undertake any of the duties assigned to men. General Decree of Gelasius, 135. See Women.

### Consecrated women

They shall not live with unrelated men. Council of Carthage I, 116.

## Feriatica

Those sent by Jews or heretics must not be accepted. Council of Laodicea, 56.

## Fermentum

It is to be sent through the priests of the city. Letter of Innocent to Decentius, 12.

## Feasts

They shall not be celebrated together with pagans. Council of Laodicea, 56.

## Celebrations

Concerning celebrations: if one liturgical offering does not suffice for the people, there should be no hesitation about repeating the sacrifice. Letter of Leo to Dioscorus, 119.

## Faith

The faith of the three hundred and eighteen Fathers must be preserved. First Council of Constantinople, 59. Profession of the faith of the Council of Nicaea. Council of Carthage VI, 164.

### Catholic faith

Concerning the evident truth of the Catholic faith. Council of Toledo IV, 363. Those who carry letters of communion shall be questioned about their faith. Council of Elvira, 290.

## Sons

On the pretext of religion, they shall by no means despise their parents. Council of Gangra, 31.

## Treasury

Concerning the treasury of Barcelona. Council of Barcelona I, 646.

## Flavian

Clerics who adhered in faith to Bishop Flavian are commended. Letter of Leo to Anatolius, 69. His rescript to Leo, 51.

## Formatae

No one shall travel to the imperial court without letters of authentication. Council of Milevis, 187.

## Fornication

Young men who have committed adultery after baptism may, after performing penance, be admitted to communion. Council of Elvira, 287. The baptized who have been defiled by incest shall perform penance. Council of Valencia, 207. In the case of incestuous married couples, the earlier regulations shall be observed. Council of Agde, 242. Incestuous clerics, if they do not separate themselves, shall be excluded from communion. Council of Orléans II, 254. Concerning those who have had intercourse with animals. Second Council of Braga, 627. Concerning those whose wives commit adultery. Second Council of Braga, 619. Concerning incestuous unions. Council of Epaon, 265. Concerning a woman who marries two brothers, or a man who has two sisters as wives. Second Council of Braga, 627. If a consecrated woman commits adultery, she shall do penance for ten years. Council of Toledo I, 325. If bishops, priests, or deacons have committed adultery, they shall not receive communion even at the end of life. Council of Elvira, 285. Women who commit adultery with unrelated men until death shall not receive communion even at the end of life. Council of Elvira, 291. Married believers who commit adultery with a Jewish woman or a pagan woman shall be barred from communion. Council of Elvira, 294. Incestuous persons shall be deprived of communion. Council of Auvergne I, 269. Incestuous persons shall be excommunicated. Council of Orléans I, 248. Incestuous persons, as long as they remain in their crime, shall be counted among the catechumens [Col. 0933]. Council of Huesca, 313. Women who commit fornication and procure abortions shall perform penance for ten years. Second Council of Braga, 627. Women who practice procuring prostitution shall not receive communion even at the end of life. Council of Elvira, 284. Penitents for adultery who commit adultery again shall not receive communion even at the end of life. Council of Elvira, 283. Those who serve at the altar, if they suddenly fall through the weakness of the flesh, shall remain under the authority of the bishop, who may either refrain from suspending those who are genuinely afflicted for long, or separate the negligent from the body of the Church for a longer period. Council of Huesca, 314. Those who are joined to two sisters shall abstain from communion for five years. Council of Elvira, 291. Those who, after baptism, have committed adultery shall not become subdeacons. Council of Elvira, 286. Those who unite themselves with their close relatives shall be separated from communion. Council of Toledo II, 331. A man who has a wife and repeatedly commits adultery shall be confronted at the point of death. Council of Elvira, 289. Whoever violates a penitent widow or a religious virgin shall be deprived of communion. Council of Huesca, 314. Priests and Levites shall not have intercourse with their wives. Council of Telepte, 192. Those who violate boys shall not receive communion even at the end of life. Council of Elvira, 292. Adulterous widows who later marry the same husband shall do penance for five years; if they marry another, they shall not receive communion even at the end of life. Council of Elvira, 292. Virgins consecrated to God who commit adultery shall not receive communion even at the end of life. Council of Elvira, 284. Secular virgins who commit adultery may be admitted to communion after five years of penance. Council of Elvira, 284. A virgin who has vowed herself to God, if she marries or commits adultery, shall be assigned to penance. Council of Valencia, 207. Deserters of either sex from a professed life of chastity are to be regarded as violators of their commitment. Council of Orange, 222. The adulterous wives of clerics shall be cast out by those clerics; if they do otherwise, they shall not receive communion even at the end of life. Council of Elvira, 291.

## Fratriae

What the Greeks understand by this term. Council of Chalcedon, 103.

## Fraudsters

Those who defraud the Church shall be deprived of communion. Council of Auvergne I, 270.

## Fruits

Concerning fruits being given in the church and nowhere else. Council of Gangra, 29. The fruits and crops of the faithful shall not be blessed by Jews. Council of Elvira, 289.

## Fulgentius

Concerning the complaints of Bishops Fulgentius and Honorius regarding certain parishes. Council of Seville II, 639.

## Founders

Founders of churches, as long as they live, shall have care of them and shall themselves choose the ministers who are to serve there. Council of Toledo IX, 449. Concerning assistance to be granted to the founders of churches or to their sons. Council of Toledo IV, 378.

# G

## Gardingi

Concerning accused priests, as well as palace nobles and gardingi, and the judicial safeguards under which they ought to be examined. Council of Toledo XIII, 514.

## Geilan

The execration of Geilan. Council of Toledo IV, 387.

## Gelasius

General decree of Pope Gelasius, 130. A bishop, priest, or deacon who acts against this pope’s regulations shall incur danger to his rank. General Decree of Gelasius, 135. Letter to the bishops of Sicily, 136.

## Pagans

Those who live according to pagan custom shall perform penance for five years [Col. 0933]. Council of Ancyra, 24. Those who, out of fear, have performed pagan rites shall, after three years of penance, be received into communion without an offering. Council of Ancyra, 18.

## Clerical orders

What periods of time are prescribed for each of the clerical orders. Letter of Zosimus to Hesychius, bishop, 36.

## Grace

The grace of God not only forgives sins but also helps to prevent them from being committed. Council of Milevis, 182. Through it we know what we ought to do. Same council, ibid. What the Fathers established concerning grace. Letter of Celestine to the bishops of Gaul, 43. It enables the law to be fulfilled. Council of Milevis, 183.

## Gregory the Great (Saint)

His faith. Council of Nicaea, 16.

### Gregory

Letter to Leander, bishop of Seville, concerning the single immersion in baptism, 156. Letter of the same Pope Gregory to Leander concerning the pallium sent from the see of blessed Peter the Apostle, 158. Letter of the same Pope Gregory to Reccared, king of the Goths, 159. Letter of the same to Bishop Leander concerning the books of the *Pastoral Rule* and the *Exposition of Blessed Job* that were sent, 157. Command of Saint Gregory, Pope of Rome, given to the governors of Sicily, 163.

## King Gundemar

Decree confirming the dignity of the holy Church of Toledo. Council of Toledo XII, 504.

# H

## Heirs

The heirs of a priest who dies shall not presume to take possession of his property contrary to the established order. Council of Toledo IX, 451.

## Heresy

Concerning the purging of the opinion of heresy. Second Council of Braga, 641. Those who have fallen into heresy through fear, if they are converted, shall be received. Letter of Leo to Anatolius, 68.

## Heretics

They shall not be promoted to the clergy. Council of Elvira, 289. Whatever is decreed in a council concerning heretics shall be sought from the ruler. Council of Milevis, 185. The meeting places of heretics are not to be called churches but assemblies. Council of Carthage IV, 149. Neither prayer nor psalmody shall be practiced with heretics. Council of Carthage IV, 149. Condemnation of certain heretics. Letter of Damasus to Paulinus, 2. Their disputes are to be avoided. Council of Toledo XIV, 535. Their fraudulent subtlety. Rescript of Flavian to Pope Leo, 51. Their names shall not be recited at the altar. Letter of Leo to Anatolius of Constantinople, 68 and 71. Those converted from heresy, if they were baptized in the Trinity, shall receive the laying on of hands. Council of Arles I, 195. Feriatica sent by heretics must not be accepted. Council of Laodicea, 56. The judge shall punish those who rebaptize heretics. Council of Orléans II, 260. It is not permitted to receive *eulogiae* from heretics. Council of Laodicea, 55. They are not permitted to enter the church. Council of Laodicea, 51. Those who become involved in the errors of heretics through fear or by choice shall be received by the Church after making satisfaction. Letter of Leo to Anatolius of Constantinople, 71. Whoever wishes to separate himself from heretics shall be received by the Catholic Church. Council of Valencia, 211. If they convert when in danger of death, they shall be received. Council of Orange, 218.

## Bishop of Jerusalem

Concerning the honor paid to him by ancient tradition. Council of Nicaea, 3.

## Hilary

Synodal decree of Pope Hilary, 120. His letter to Ascanus, bishop of Tarragona, 123. Letter to Ascanus and to all the bishops of the province of Tarragona, 122.

## Spaniards

Their rebuke because they were ordaining clerics irregularly [Col. 0934]. Letter of Innocent to all the bishops in Toulouse, 34.

## Murderers

### Homicide

Murderers shall be removed from ecclesiastical communion. Council of Agde, 237. The canons of the Council of Nicaea concerning murderers shall be observed. Council of Epaon, 265. No commemoration shall be made in the offering for those who inflict death upon themselves. First Council of Braga, 604. Concerning those who commit homicide unwillingly. Council of Ancyra, 23. Concerning those who commit homicide intentionally. Same council, 22. Concerning voluntary and involuntary homicide. Second Council of Braga, 627. Women who, having committed fornication, kill the children they bear shall be assigned ten years of penance. Council of Ancyra, 22. Whoever kills a person by sorcery shall not receive communion even at the end of life. Council of Elvira, 283. If a mistress kills a maidservant out of jealousy, she shall, if she acted intentionally, be admitted to communion after seven years; if by accident, after five years. Council of Elvira, 283. Wives who kill children begotten in adultery shall not receive communion even at the end of life. Council of Elvira, 291.

## Honorius

Concerning the complaints of Bishops Fulgentius and Honorius regarding certain parishes. Council of Seville II, 639.

### Honorius Augustus

His rescript to Pope Boniface, 39.

## Hormisdas

Letter to the Emperor Justin, 141. Decree issued by him in the city of Rome: concerning the divine Scriptures, what the universal Catholic Church accepts and what it must henceforth avoid, 164. Letter to Epiphanius, bishop of Constantinople, 150. Letter to the bishops established throughout Spain, 147. Another letter to the bishops of Spain, 149. Rescript to the bishops of the province of Baetica, 153. Letter to John, bishop of the Church of Elche, 145. Letter to Bishop John concerning the institutions transmitted and the authority entrusted to him, 146. Letter to Sallustius, bishop of Seville, 152.

# I

## Idols

### Idolatry

Masters shall prohibit their slaves from worshiping idols. Council of Elvira, 288. The faithful shall not accept anything that has been offered to idols. Council of Elvira, 288. Those who are killed while destroying idols shall not be enrolled among the martyrs. Same council, 291. The baptized who worship idols shall perform penance. Council of Valencia, 207. Idol worshipers voluntarily subject themselves to death. Council of Toledo XII, 501. Concerning worshipers of idols. Council of Toledo XVI, 568. Idolatry must be destroyed. Council of Carthage V, 158. Those who sacrificed to idols before baptism may be promoted to the orders. Council of Ancyra, 20. Those who induced others to sacrifice shall be kept among the catechumens for three years and perform penance for six years. Same council, ibid. Those who frequently sacrificed to idols shall be received after two years of penance. Same council, 19. Those who ate in places dedicated to idols shall perform penance for three years and afterward communicate for two years without an offering. Same council, ibid. Those who dined in the temples of idols shall perform penance for three years. Same council, 18. Those who under compulsion sacrificed to idols shall submit themselves to penance for four years. Same council, 19.

## Immunity of the Church

See Asylum.

## Enchanters

They shall be separated from the assembly of the Church. Council of Carthage IV, 151. Priests and clerics are not permitted to make incantations or charms [Col. 0935]. Second Council of Braga, 624.

## Prisoners

They shall be visited by the archdeacon or the provost of the church, and their needs shall be relieved mercifully. Council of Auvergne II, 279.

## The mystery of the Lord’s Incarnation

Against those who attempt to divide the mystery of the Lord’s saving dispensation into two sons. Letter of Leo to Flavian, 53. See Jesus Christ.

## The incontinent

Neither penance nor the Eucharistic provision for the journey shall be denied to those who are in the hour of death. Letter of Innocent to Exuperius, 17.

## Infanticide

Concerning women who, having committed fornication, kill the children they bear. Council of Ancyra, 22.

## Pope Innocent

His letter to Acacius, bishop of Beroea, concerning Saint John, bishop of Constantinople, 29. His letter to Agapitus and the other bishops, stating that no one may be admitted to the clergy after penance, 20. His letter to Alexander, bishop of Antioch, concerning peace, 26. His letter to the same, 27, 28. His letter to Aurelius, bishop of Carthage, concerning Easter, 23. His letter to the same, stating that no one is to be made a bishop contrary to the order of the canons, 24. His letter to Aurelius and Augustine, African bishops: writings full of saving instruction and charity, 23. His letter to Boniface the priest, concerning the Church of Antioch, 25. His letter to Bishop Decentius, 10. His letter to Exuperius, bishop of Toulouse, 16. His letter to Felix, bishop of Nocera, 18. His letter to Florentius, bishop of Tivoli, concerning boundaries not being transferred, 22. His exhortatory letter to Julianus the nobleman, 24. His letter to Laurentius, bishop of Siena, concerning the Bonosians, who are to be compared with the Jews, 29. His letter to Bishop Maximian, concerning Atticus, bishop of Constantinople, 26. His letter to Bishops Maximus and Severus, concerning those who have fathered sons while priests, 20. His letter to Probus: if someone’s wife has been carried away into captivity and the husband has taken another, the second wife must be excluded, 22. His letter to Rufus and Eusebius and the other bishops, 30. His letter to Rufus, Gerontius, and the other bishops established throughout Macedonia, concerning Bubalius and Taurianus, condemned by the provincial bishops, 21. His letter to all the bishops in Toulouse, 34. His letter to Victoricus, bishop of Rouen, 13.

## Intercessors

They shall not retain the see of a deceased bishop for long. Council of Carthage V, 156.

## Prohibitions

Whoever disregards the prohibitions shall be subject to the danger of losing his rank. Letter of Zosimus to Hesychius, 36.

## Irenaeus

Irenaeus, removed from the Church of Barcelona, shall return to his own church. Letter of Hilary to Ascanus, 122. Irenaeus: if he does not return to his own church, he shall be removed. Letter of Hilary to Ascanus, 123.

# J

## James the Apostle

Concerning his letter, in which prayer for the sick is commanded. Letter of Innocent to Decentius, 12.

## Fasting

A person who deliberately fasts on the Lord’s Day is not to be regarded as Catholic. Council of Carthage IV, 148. Concerning not ending the fast on Good Friday. Council of Toledo IV, 369. No one shall fast on Sundays [Col. 0935]. Protracted fasts shall be observed in each month. Council of Elvira, 286. One shall not fast or kneel on the Lord’s Day, and likewise during Lent. Second Council of Braga, 624. One shall fast every Saturday. Council of Elvira, 286. It is not permitted to fast on the Lord’s Day. Council of Gangra, 31. It is not permitted to abolish the common fasts. Same council, 31. It is not permitted to end the fast on the Thursday of the final week. Second Council of Braga, 623. A fast shall be observed every Saturday. Letter of Innocent to Decentius, 11. Whoever, without necessity, bodily weakness, or the incapacity of age, presumes to eat meat during the days of Lent shall be deprived of communion at the Lord’s Resurrection and shall abstain from all meat for the whole year. Council of Toledo VIII, 437.

## Jesus Christ

Address to the entire structure of the Church concerning the two inseparable and perfect natures of Christ. Council of Toledo XIV, 534. Against those who, in their madness, assert that the form of a servant which the Word assumed from us was heavenly or of some other substance. Letter of Leo to Flavian, 55. Against those who foolishly claim that the Lord had two natures before union but fabricate one after union. Letter of the same to the same, 56. Against those who argue for mixture or confusion in Christ’s two natures. Letter of the same to the same, 54. Against those who dare to assert that the divinity of the Only-Begotten Son was passible. Letter of the same to the same, ibid. All the mysteries of our salvation have been arranged for us, in due order, through the Incarnation of our Lord. Letter of Leo to the bishops throughout Sicily, 98. Concerning the divinity and humanity of the Lord Jesus Christ. Letter of Hormisdas to Emperor Justin, 142. Concerning the two natures and one person in Christ. Council of Seville II, 646. Concerning the wills and operations of Christ’s two natures. Council of Toledo XIV, 535. Julian’s explicit assertion concerning the three substances remaining in Christ. Council of Toledo XV, 543. Those who say that Christ is called the Only-Begotten because he alone was born of the Virgin are condemned. Letter of Leo to Turibius of Astorga, 91.

## John, bishop of Constantinople

A letter, or statement of faith, sent to Pope Hormisdas, in which he anathematizes Nestorius and Eutyches and the blasphemies of the other heretics, 144.

## Thursday

Whoever, on Thursday, except during the feasts that fall on it, dares to take the day off and refrain from work, whether man or woman, shall be expelled from the church. Council of Narbonne, 662.

## Jews

Baptized Jews shall celebrate feast days with the bishops. Council of Toledo IX, 453. Concerning the marriages of Christians and Jews. Council of Toledo IV, 384. Confirmation of the laws promulgated against their wickedness. Council of Toledo XII, 498. Safeguarding the faith concerning the Jews. Council of Toledo VI, 402. Concerning the condemnation of the Jews. Council of Toledo XVII, 595. Concerning Jewish unbelief. Council of Toledo XVI, 567. Distinguishing which Jews are not to be compelled to believe and which are to be compelled. Council of Toledo IV, 382. Faithful children of Jews must not be exiled from their property because of their parents’ transgression. Council of Toledo IV, 384. Jewish children separated from their parents are to be assigned to Christians. Same council, 383. Jews may not proceed among Christians to the Lord’s Supper until the second day of the Passover Sabbath, nor may they mingle with Catholic peoples on any pretext. Council of Orléans II, 200 [Col. 0936]. Baptized Jews who associate with unbelieving Jews shall be subjected to public flogging. Council of Toledo IV, 384. Jews shall not be appointed judges over Christian peoples. Council of Auvergne I, 260. Converted Jews who later transgress shall not be admitted to give testimony. Council of Toledo IV, 384. Jews who were formerly Christians and later returned to their former rite shall, after correction by episcopal authority, be recalled to the observance of Christian doctrine. Same council, 383. Jews shall not possess a Christian slave. Same council, 385. Jews shall not hold public offices. Same council, 384. How Jews who wish to convert are to be received. Council of Agde, 237. Jews may not have Christian wives or concubines, nor acquire a Christian slave for their own use. Council of Toledo III, 352. Jewish banquets are forbidden not only to laymen but also to clerics. Council of Epaon, 263. Jews are not permitted to conduct a body in procession while singing psalms; rather, according to their ancient custom and practice, they shall conduct and bury the body. Council of Narbonne, 661. Whoever, against the faith of Christ, grants a gift or favor to Jews shall be made an outsider to the Catholic Church and the kingdom of God. Council of Toledo IV, 383.

## Judges

They shall be considered immune while they are drafting petitions or criminal documents. Letter of Innocent to Exuperius, 17. Judges may not force clerics or the Church’s slaves into their own compulsory services. Council of Toledo III, 354. They exercise their offices according to discipline and the authority of the Lord. Letter of the same to the same, ibid.

## Judgment

If a case has been brought before judges where the authority is greater, this shall not prejudice the first sentence. Council of Carthage III, 122.

## Julian

Bishop Julian is commended. Letter of Leo to Anatolius, 69.

## Oath

Whoever proves to be a profaner of his oath shall be anathema. Council of Toledo XVI, 376.

## Emperor Justin

Letter to Pope Hormisdas, 143.

## The righteous person

He must say: “Forgive us our debts.” Council of Milevis, 184.

# K

## Kalends

It is not permitted to observe the Kalends. Second Council of Braga, 626.

# L

## Laymen

They may bring a charge against clerics, if it is true. Council of Epaon, 264. Concerning laymen who bring a charge against clerics. Council of Turin, 210. Which of them may not be admitted to the clergy. Letter of Innocent to Felix, 19. Despisers of the canons shall be excommunicated. Council of Carthage I, 120. They shall not appoint clerics as their agents or accountants. Council of Carthage I, 118. No one shall reach the highest priesthood except through the ecclesiastical orders. Letter of Zosimus to Hesychius, 36. They shall not dare to teach in the presence of clerics. Council of Carthage IV, 152. If they communicate with an excommunicated person, they shall be excommunicated. Same council, 149. If they marry a widow, they shall not become clerics. Letter of Innocent to Victoricus, 14.

## Those who have fallen

A cleric or layman who has fallen shall be deprived of every rank of his honor. Council of Toledo VI, 411. Priests or deacons who have fallen into some crime cannot obtain the remedy of penance through the laying on of hands. Letter of Leo to Rusticus, 104. What penance is to be imposed on those who have fallen voluntarily. Council of Nicaea, 4. Those who fall into various sins, if they demonstrate complete conversion, shall be admitted to communion [Col. 0937]. Council of Laodicea, 51. See Apostates.

## Leander, bishop of Seville

Concerning the key of the body of blessed Peter and the cross of the Lord sent, or concerning the pallium sent to blessed Leander, bishop. Letter of Pope Gregory to Reccared, 161. Homily of Saint Leander, bishop, in praise of the Church. Council of Toledo III, 359.

## Lepers

The necessities of food and clothing shall be supplied to lepers from the Church’s house [Col. 0937]. Council of Auvergne II, 279.

## Levites

They shall abstain from their wives. Council of Carthage V, 155. They shall not be consecrated before the age of twenty-five. Council of Carthage III, 127. They shall preserve chastity. Council of Carthage II, 121. They must not have intercourse with women. Letter of Innocent to Victoricus, 14. Levites and clerics who are magicians or enchanters shall be expelled from the Church. Council of Agde, 243. They shall not offer sacrifice. Council of Arles I, 196. If they are incontinent, they shall be deprived of ecclesiastical honor. Letter of Innocent to Exuperius, 16. They shall not sit without the command of a priest. Council of Agde, 243. See Deacons.

## Freedmen

They shall never depart from the protection of the Church. Council of Mérida, 676. They shall not be promoted to the clergy. Council of Elvira, 294. Concerning Church freedmen who are to be promoted to the priesthood. Council of Toledo IV, 386. Concerning proud Church freedmen, who are to be recalled to service. Council of Seville II, 643. Distinguishing which freedmen may attain ecclesiastical honors. Council of Toledo IV, 386. Distinguishing the Church’s manumitted slaves. Council of Toledo IV, 385. Bishops shall not presume to alienate the Church’s freedmen. Same council, 385. From the Church’s household, priests may make freedmen of persons acquired as compensation for property. Council of Toledo IV, 386. The children of Church freedmen may not wander away from it for the sake of their maintenance. Council of Toledo VI, 406. Freedmen belonging to others shall be defended by the bishop. Council of Toledo III, 350. Church freedmen shall pursue the Church’s business. Council of Agde, 240. Freedmen must renew their declarations before the Church and demonstrate obedience to the Church. Council of Toledo VI, 405. Freedmen whom bishops manumit from the household, if they neglect to present their certificates of freedom to the succeeding bishop, shall within a year be reduced to their former condition of slavery. Council of Zaragoza III, 309, and Toledo VI, 405. Freedmen who are entrusted to the Church’s protection shall be guarded by priestly defense. Council of Toledo IV, 386. The freedom of manumitted persons shall be defended justly by the churches within the Church. Council of Auvergne II, 275. Declaration of the Church’s freedmen. Council of Toledo IV, 386. If Church freedmen, abandoning its protection, attach themselves to any persons and, after being admonished, disdain to return, their manumission shall be invalid. Council of Toledo IV, 386. Except for fiscal slaves or fiscal freedmen, no one from the slavery of any person, nor any freedman, shall henceforth at any time pass into palace service. Council of Toledo XIII, 518. See Church.

## Free will

What the Church has established concerning it. Letter of Celestine to the bishops of Gaul, 43.

## Apocryphal books

List of apocryphal books that are not accepted. Decree of Hormisdas, 166.

## Canonical books

Works of the holy Fathers that are accepted. Decree of Hormisdas, 165. Order of the canonical books of the Old and New Testaments. Same decree, 164. Which books are to be accepted. Letter of Innocent to Exuperius, 18. Which books they are. Council of Laodicea, 58.

## Litanies

The days of the litanies shall be celebrated throughout all twelve months of the year. Council of Toledo XVII, 593. Institution of new litanies. Council of Toledo V, 395. Litanies shall be celebrated after the Lord’s Ascension. Council of Orléans I, 249. Observance of the litanies. Council of Toledo VI, 402.

## Gaming

Those who play dice—that is, board games—for money shall abstain. Council of Elvira, 294.

# M
## M
